Tanzania ni taifa lililobarikiwa kwa utajiri mkubwa wa rasilimali, tamaduni mbalimbali na watu wenye moyo wa upendo. 
Mojawapo ya alama muhimu inayolitambulisha taifa letu duniani ni taswira njema ya amani na mshikamano. 
Taswira hii haikutokea kwa bahati; imetokana na juhudi za waasisi wa taifa, viongozi wetu na wananchi wote walioamua kuishi kwa umoja na kuheshimiana. 
Kwa sababu hii, Watanzania tunapaswa kuendelea kulinda na kuienzi taswira hii ili taifa letu liendelee kuwa kimbilio la utulivu na matumaini.

*1,Amani na utulivu ndizo nguzo kuu za maendeleo ya nchi yoyote.* 
Bila amani, shughuli za kiuchumi, kijamii na kisiasa haziwezi kusonga mbele. Tanzania imekuwa mfano wa nchi inayodumisha amani licha ya kuwa na makabila, dini na mila mbalimbali. 
Ni jukumu la kila Mtanzania kuhakikisha tofauti hizi haziwi chanzo cha migogoro bali utajiri unaotujenga. Kila mmoja anapaswa kutumia maneno yenye kujenga, kuhamasisha maelewano na kuzuia kauli zinazoweza kuchochea chuki.

*2, Upendo na mshikamano ni muhimu katika kulinda taswira ya taifa.* 
Upendo hurahisisha watu kushirikiana, kuheshimiana na kusaidiana bila ubaguzi. Mshikamano huifanya jamii kuwa imara dhidi ya changamoto zinazoweza kuleta mgawanyiko. 
Kwa kuheshimu viongozi, kufuata sheria, na kushiriki katika shughuli za kijamii kama vile usafi, uokoaji na kusaidia wenye uhitaji, tunaunda jamii inayothamini utu na maridhiano. 
Haya yote huongeza heshima ya nchi yetu mbele ya mataifa mengine.

*3,katika ulimwengu wa sasa wa teknolojia,* 
wananchi wanapaswa kuwa makini katika namna wanavyotumia mitandao ya kijamii. Mara nyingi taswira ya nchi hujengwa au kubomolewa kupitia taarifa zinazowekwa mtandaoni. 
Ni wajibu wa Watanzania kusambaza taarifa sahihi, zenye manufaa na zinazojenga, badala ya kueneza uvumi, chuki au taarifa zinazodhalilisha nchi. 
Mamlaka zinaweza kuweka sheria, 
lakini nidhamu binafsi ya mtumiaji wa mitandao ndiyo kinga madhubuti.

Pope Leo XIV at the Armenian Cathedral in Istanbul: “May the Language of Love Blossom for the Sake of Dialogue!”
A spiritual, ecumenical, and historic visit carrying dimensions that transcend time and space

— إسطنبول، 30 نوفمبر (تشرين الثاني) 2025

⭕️ في مشهد مسكوني استثنائي يجمع بين التاريخ والحاضر، تجسّد في إسطنبول يوم الأحد التلاقي العميق بين الكنائس الشرقية والكاثوليكية، حين زار قداسة البابا لاون الرابع عشر كاتدرائية الأرمن الأرثوذكس، لتكون شهادة الإيمان الأرمني والتاريخ المسيحي في تركيا حاضرة بكل جلالها وروحانيتها. هذه الزيارة ليست مجرد خطوة رمزية، بل رسالة أمل ووحدة تنبض بالشهادة المسيحية المشتركة، وتعكس الرغبة الصادقة في تعزيز الحوار بين الكنائس ودعم الأقليات المسيحية، وسط تاريخ حافل بالتحديات والابتلاءات.

🔻 حيث اليوم الرابع من زيارته إلى تركيا، قام قداسة البابا لاون الرابع عشر يوم الأحد بزيارة تاريخية إلى كاتدرائية الأرمن الأرثوذكس في إسطنبول، حيث التقى بطريرك الكنيسة الرسولية الأرمنية في تركيا، غبطة البطريرك ساهاك الثاني ماشاليان بطريرك القسطنطينية للأرمن الأرثوذكس، وألقى كلمة مؤثرة أمام أبناء الكنيسة الأرمنية، التي يُقدّر عددها بنحو خمسين ألف نسمة، يتركّز معظمهم في مدينة إسطنبول.

🔻جاءت هذه الزيارة في إطار مبادرة رمزية لتعزيز الحوار بين الكنائس ودعم الأقليات المسيحية في تركيا، وتُعد بادرة مسكونية وروحية لتقوية الروابط الأخوية بين الكنيسة الرسولية الأرمنية والكنيسة الكاثوليكية، وللتذكير بالشهادة التاريخية للشعب الأرمني عبر القرون، خاصة في ظل الظروف المأساوية التي مرّ بها.

🔻وجّه قداسة الحبر الروماني تحياته القلبية إلى قداسة الكاثوليكوس كاريكين الثاني يطريرك الكرسي الأم في إتشميادزين و كاثوليكوس عموم الأرمن، معبّرًا عن شكره للزيارة الأخوية التي قام بها مؤخرًا إلى الكرسي الرسولي، وقال:

«بحسب نعمة الله يزدهر حوار المحبة».

🔻وأشار قداسة البابا إلى شهادة الإيمان العظيمة التي قدّمها الشعب الأرمني عبر التاريخ، وأعرب عن امتنانه العميق للروابط الأخوية المتنامية بين الكنيسة الرسولية الأرمنية والكنيسة الكاثوليكية.

🔻كما استعاد البابا اللحظة التاريخية التي أعقبت المجمع الفاتيكاني الثاني، حين كان الكاثوليكوس كورين الأول في مايو 1967 أول رئيس كنيسة أرثوذكسية شرقية يزور أسقف روما ويتبادل معه قبلة السلام، ثم تلتها الخطوة التاريخية بتوقيع أول إعلان مشترك بين الكاثوليكوس فاسكين الأول والبابا بولس السادس في مايو 1970، حيث دعوا المؤمنين إلى النظر إلى بعضهم كإخوة في المسيح لتعزيز الوحدة. ومنذ ذلك الحين، واصل حوار المحبة ازدهاره بين الكنيستين.

🔻 وأوضح البابا أن هذه الزيارة في ذكرى مرور 1700 سنة على انعقاد أول مجمع مسكوني تمثّل فرصة للاحتفال بقانون الإيمان النيقاوي، ومن هذا الإيمان الرسولي المشترك ينبغي أن نستمد القوة لاستعادة الشركة بين كنيسة روما وكنائس الشرق القديمة، مؤكّدًا:

«الوحدة ليست انصهارًا ولا هيمنة، بل تبادل عطايا الروح القدس».

🔻وشدّد البابا على أهمية استئناف عمل اللجنة الدولية المشتركة للحوار اللاهوتي بين الكنيسة الكاثوليكية والكنائس الأرثوذكسية الشرقية، بهدف البحث في نموذج الشركة الكاملة، مستدلاً برسالة القديس يوحنا بولس الثاني: «ليكونوا واحدًا».

🔻وأشار إلى «سحابة من الشهود» التي تسبقنا على طريق الوحدة، مستحضرًا من التقليد الأرمني شخصية القديس نرسيس الرابع شنورهالي، الكاثوليكوس والشاعر في القرن الثاني عشر، الذي كرّس حياته للمصالحة بين الكنائس، ساعيًا لتحقيق صلاة المسيح: «ليكونوا جميعًا واحدًا».

🔻 وفي ختام كلمته، شكر البابا البطريرك ساهاك الثاني على حفاوة الاستقبال، مؤكدًا التزامه بقضية الوحدة المسيحية، وداعيًا الجميع إلى قبول هبة الوحدة السماوية بقلوب منفتحة لتصبح شهادتهم لحقيقة الإنجيل أكثر إقناعًا، وخدمتهم للكنيسة الواحدة الجامعة المقدسة الرسوليّة أكثر ثمارًا.

⭕️ هذا وقد بدأت الزيارة باستقبال حافل ثم صلاة مسكونية في الكاتدرائية، حيث شارك نحو 500 مؤمن أرمني في الصلاة، تلتها كلمات رسمية لكل من البابا لاون الرابع عشر وغبطة البطريرك ساهاك الثاني ماشاليان، قبل تبادل الهدايا الرمزية وخروج الجانبين إلى ساحة الكاتدرائية للمشاركة في احتفال تدشين حجر تذكاري رخامي باسم البابا.

🔻 وقد رأى مراقبون أن زيارة البابا تحمل رمزية مسكونية كبيرة، كما تمثّل إشارة هادئة لتشجيع جهود المصالحة بين تركيا وأرمينيا، في وقت ما تزال فيه آثار الأحداث التاريخية الأليمة التي شهدها الشعب الأرمني منذ عام 1915، حيث تُقدّر أعداد الضحايا بنحو مليون ونصف المليون، وتصفها بعض المصادر بأنها إبادة جماعية، في حين تنكر تركيا هذا الوصف.

🔹️وأشار ريتشارد غيراغوسيان، مدير «مركز الدراسات الإقليمية» في يريفان، إلى أن:

«الزيارة لا تحمل فقط رمزية التقارب بين الفاتيكان والكنيسة الأرمنية في الشرق، بل تمثّل في جانب منها دعمًا لمسار التطبيع بين تركيا وأرمينيا».

🔻 و تأتي هذا الزيارة لقداسة بابا روما في سياق الذكرى الـ1700 لمجمع نيقية في مدينة إزنيق الحالية، حيث أقرّت الكنيسة الأولى قانون الإيمان النيقاوي، كما تتزامن مع مسار تفاوضي بدأ منذ عام 2021 لتطبيع العلاقات بين تركيا وأرمينيا وإعادة فتح الحدود المغلقة منذ التسعينيات، بالتوازي مع جهود خفض التوتر بين أرمينيا وأذربيجان.

🔻 حيث أشار الخبراء إلى أن البابا لاون الرابع عشر عاش سنواته التكوينية في شيكاغو، حيث كانت الجالية الأرمنية الأمريكية حاضرة بقوة، ما أكسبه فهمًا عميقًا للتراث الروحي الأرمني. وذكرت الصحفية التركية من أصل أرمني فيرجيهان زيفليوغلو:

«لا يُتوقع أن يستخدم البابا مصطلح "الإبادة" في الوقت الحالي، خاصةً في ظل المرحلة الراهنة التي تشهد جهودًا ملموسة للتطبيع بين تركيا وأرمينيا».

🔻 و في يريفان، أعرب المواطن أرمن أرشاقيان (65 عامًا) عن اعتقاده أن زيارة البابا لن تغيّر سياسات تركيا، لكنه رأى فيها «خطوة مشرّفة تُعيد التذكير بقضية الشعب الأرمني، الذي يمر اليوم بظروف صعبة».

🔹️أما الشابة ماريا بيتروسيان (31 عامًا)، فرأت أن الزيارة «قد لا تكون ذات أهمية عالمية كبيرة»، لكنها شدّدت على أهميتها في الحفاظ على الحوار بين الكنائس المختلفة.

🔹️من جهته، رأى الأرشمندريت باروير شرنيزيان، عميد المعهد اللاهوتي الأرمني في لبنان، أنّ الزيارة تُظهر أن تركيا جزء من التراث العريق للكنائس المسيحية الشرقية، بما فيها الكنيسة الأرمنية.

🔻و جاءت الزيارة في وقت يشهد فيه جنوب القوقاز توترًا داخليًا، بعد احتجاجات بعض رجال الدين الأرمن على مسار التطبيع مع أذربيجان، واعتقال عدد منهم، بينهم المطران ميكائيل أجاجابهيان، الذي حُكم عليه بالسجن عامين بتهمة «الدعوة لقلب نظام الحكم».

وفي الوقت نفسه، وقّع الفاتيكان اتفاقًا مع أذربيجان حول الحوار بين الأديان، ما أثار اعتراضات لدى بعض الجماعات الأرمنية، في حين واصلت الفاتيكان ممارسة «دبلوماسية خلف الكواليس» للإسهام في إطلاق سراح المعتقلين الأرمن، والذين بلغ عددهم وفق وسائل إعلام نحو 23 معتقلًا.

📍لقد شكلت زيارة البابا لاون الرابع عشر محطة فريدة في تاريخ العلاقات المسكونية، إذ جمعت بين الروحانية العميقة، والشهادة التاريخية للشعب الأرمني، والمساعي الرامية إلى الوحدة والشركة بين الكنائس. إن هذه الخطوة لا تعكس مجرد طقوس ومراسم، بل دعوة حية لكل المسيحيين للتفكر في إرث الإيمان النيقاوي، واستلهام قوة الروح القدس لتعزيز الحوار، والعمل معًا من أجل أن تكون الكنائس واحدة في الشهادة، قوية في الخدمة، ومضيئة في الطريق نحو الشركة الكاملة في المسيح.

Pope Leo XIV at the Armenian Cathedral in Istanbul: “May the Language of Love Blossom for the Sake of Dialogue!”
A spiritual, ecumenical, and historic visit carrying dimensions that transcend time and space

— Istanbul, November 30, 2025

⭕️ In an exceptional ecumenical scene that bridges history and the present, a profound encounter between the Eastern and Catholic Churches unfolded in Istanbul on Sunday, as His Holiness Pope Leo XIV visited the Armenian Orthodox Cathedral. The Armenian Christian witness and the centuries-old Christian presence in Turkey were manifest in all their dignity and spirituality. This visit was far more than a symbolic gesture; it was a message of hope and unity, vibrant with the spirit of the shared Christian testimony. It reflected a sincere desire to strengthen dialogue between the Churches and to support Christian minorities amid a history marked by trials and tribulations.

🔻 On the fourth day of his visit to Turkey, His Holiness Pope Leo XIV paid a historic visit on Sunday to the Armenian Orthodox Cathedral in Istanbul, where he met His Beatitude Patriarch Sahak II Mashalian, Patriarch of Constantinople of the Armenian Orthodox Church. The Pope delivered a deeply moving address before the members of the Armenian Church, whose community numbers approximately fifty thousand believers, most of whom reside in Istanbul.

🔻 This visit formed part of a symbolic initiative aimed at enhancing inter-church dialogue and supporting Christian minorities in Turkey. It stood as an ecumenical and spiritual gesture to strengthen the fraternal ties between the Armenian Apostolic Church and the Catholic Church, and as a reminder of the historical witness of the Armenian people through the centuries, especially in light of the tragic circumstances they have endured.

🔻 His Holiness the Roman Pontiff extended heartfelt greetings to His Holiness Catholicos Karekin II, Catholicos of All Armenians and Patriarch of the Mother See of Holy Etchmiadzin, expressing his gratitude for the fraternal visit recently made to the Apostolic See. The Pope stated:

“By the grace of God, the dialogue of love continues to flourish.”

🔻 The Pope also highlighted the profound witness of faith borne by the Armenian people throughout history, and expressed his deep appreciation for the growing fraternal bonds between the Armenian Apostolic Church and the Catholic Church.

🔻 He also recalled the historic moment following the Second Vatican Council, when Catholicos Khoren I in May 1967 became the first head of an Eastern Orthodox Church to visit the Bishop of Rome and exchange the Kiss of Peace, followed by the historic step of signing the first joint declaration between Catholicos Vasken I and Pope Paul VI in May 1970, inviting the faithful to regard each other as brothers in Christ to promote unity. Since then, the dialogue of love between the two churches has continued to flourish.

🔻 The Pope explained that this visit, marking the 1700th anniversary of the first Ecumenical Council, represents an opportunity to celebrate the Nicene Creed. From this shared apostolic faith, we should draw strength to restore communion between the Church of Rome and the ancient Eastern Churches, affirming:
“Unity is neither fusion nor domination, but the exchange of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.”

🔻 Pope Leo XIV emphasized the importance of resuming the work of the International Joint Commission for Theological Dialogue between the Catholic Church and the Eastern Orthodox Churches to explore a model of full communion, citing the message of Saint John Paul II: “That they may be one.”

🔻 He referred to the “cloud of witnesses” preceding us on the path of unity, recalling from the Armenian tradition Saint Nerses IV Shnorhali, the Catholicos and poet of the 12th century, who devoted his life to reconciliation between the churches, striving to fulfill Christ’s prayer: “That they may all be one.”

🔻 In concluding his address, the Pope thanked Patriarch Sahak II for the warm reception, reaffirmed his commitment to the cause of Christian unity, and urged all to embrace the gift of heavenly unity with open hearts so that their witness to the truth of the Gospel may be more persuasive and their service to the one, holy, catholic, and apostolic Church more fruitful.

At 16, Gulalai Ismail started teaching girls about leadership in conservative Pakistan. By her 30s, she was underground, hunted by her own government. She escaped to America—but didn't stop speaking. Some voices refuse to be silenced, even in exile.
In 2002, in Swat Valley, Pakistan—a conservative region where girls' education was controversial and women's public activism was almost unthinkable—a 16-year-old girl named Gulalai Ismail started teaching workshops.
She gathered young women and girls to talk about leadership, rights, self-worth, and peacebuilding.
In a place where the Taliban would later ban girls' education entirely, where women were expected to remain invisible in public life, Gulalai was telling girls they had power, voice, and the right to shape their own futures.
She called the organization Aware Girls.
What started as small workshops grew into a movement—training young women in leadership, documenting human rights abuses, countering extremist narratives, and advocating for peace in a region torn by violence.
For years, Gulalai worked in increasingly dangerous conditions. The Taliban opposed her. Conservative communities saw her as a threat to traditional values. And eventually, the Pakistani government decided she was a problem.
Because Gulalai didn't just advocate for women's education. She criticized military operations that displaced civilians. She spoke out about enforced disappearances—people taken by security forces and never seen again. She documented human rights violations.
And in Pakistan, criticizing the military or security establishment is one of the most dangerous things you can do.
By her late 20s and early 30s, Gulalai Ismail was one of the most visible human rights activists in Pakistan—and one of the most targeted.
Her passport was confiscated repeatedly. She was placed on Exit Control Lists, preventing her from leaving the country. Security forces raided her family home, terrorizing her parents and siblings.
She was charged with sedition, treason, and other crimes that could carry life imprisonment or death penalty.
The message was clear: stop speaking, or face consequences.
Gulalai kept speaking.
In 2019, the pressure intensified. The charges escalated. The threats became more specific and credible.
Gulalai made a decision: if she stayed, she would be arrested, imprisoned, possibly killed. Her organization would be destroyed. The activists she worked with would be endangered.
So she went underground.
For months, she lived in hiding, moving secretly, unable to contact most people, communicating sporadically with trusted allies to let the world know she was still alive.
It's hard to imagine that existence—being hunted in your own country, unable to go home, unable to trust most people, knowing that being discovered could mean prison or death.
But Gulalai endured it. Because staying silent would have meant letting the government win, letting fear silence the work she'd built.
In late 2019 or early 2020, Gulalai managed to escape Pakistan.
The exact details remain vague for security reasons and to protect the people who helped her. But she made it first to Sri Lanka, then eventually to the United States, where she was granted asylum.
She was safe. Finally, after months underground, after years of threats and persecution, she was in a country where speaking out wouldn't result in arrest.
Most people in her situation would rest, recover, try to build a quiet new life.
Gulalai kept speaking.
From exile in the United States, she continues documenting human rights abuses in Pakistan. She advocates for activists who remain in Pakistan, facing the same persecution she escaped. She speaks at international forums, writes articles, uses social media to amplify voices that Pakistan's government tries to suppress.
She refuses to let exile mean silence.
In 2019, Amnesty International awarded her the Ambassador of Conscience Award—their highest honor, recognizing individuals who show exceptional courage in standing up for human rights.
She shared the award with Greta Thunberg, the climate activist. Two young women, from completely different contexts, both refusing to be silenced despite enormous pressure.
But while Greta faces criticism and online harassment, Gulalai faced state persecution, potential imprisonment, and credible threats to her life.
The courage required is different in scale.
Gulalai Ismail's story matters because she represents thousands of human rights defenders—particularly women—who risk everything to speak truth in authoritarian contexts.
She didn't come from wealth or international privilege. She grew up in Swat Valley, in a region where women's public activism was dangerous and rare.
She started teaching workshops at 16 not because it was safe or easy, but because she believed girls deserved education, leadership skills, and the knowledge that they mattered.
And she never stopped—even when the Taliban controlled her region, even when the Pakistani government targeted her, even when she had to go underground, even in exile.
Her father, Muhammad Ismail, is also a human rights defender who faced harassment and detention for his work. The entire family paid a price for refusing to be silent.
Today, Gulalai continues her advocacy from the United States. She works with organizations supporting Pakistani activists. She documents abuses. She speaks at conferences and universities. She uses her platform to amplify voices of those still in Pakistan who can't speak as openly.
She's also processing trauma—years of persecution, months underground, the loss of being able to safely return to her home country.
But she's still fighting.
Because Gulalai understands something crucial: if she stops speaking just because she's safe now, then the Pakistani government won. They succeeded in silencing a critic by forcing her into exile.
So she refuses to be silenced, even from thousands of miles away.
Her message to other activists, particularly women in dangerous contexts: "Your voice matters. Your work matters. And you're not alone."
She knows what it costs to speak out. She's paid that price personally.
And she's still speaking.
Gulalai Ismail proves that courage isn't the absence of fear—it's acting despite fear.
She was afraid when she started teaching workshops at 16 in conservative Swat Valley. She was terrified when security forces raided her home. She was hunted when she went underground.
But she kept working. Kept speaking. Kept believing that her voice and the voices of the women she advocates for matter more than her personal safety.
At 16, she taught girls about leadership in a region that told girls they had no place in public life.
At 33, she was underground, hunted by her own government for defending human rights.
Now, in her late 30s, she's in exile—but still fighting for the activists who remain in Pakistan, facing what she faced.
Some voices refuse to be silenced.
Not by the Taliban. Not by state persecution. Not by exile.
Gulalai Ismail is one of those voices.
And as long as she has breath, she'll keep using it—for herself, for Aware Girls, for the activists still fighting in Pakistan, for all the women told they should be silent.
Because borders can contain a person.
But they can't contain truth, courage, or a voice that refuses to stop speaking.

The National Commission on Muslim Filipinos – Northern Mindanao (NCMF-X), led by Regional Director Dr. Abdulnasser P. Masorong Jr., CESO III, conducted the program “Threads of Peace: Interfaith Lunch and Culmination of the Mindanao Week of Peace” in partnership with SIRAJ Muslim Religious Organization of Xavier University – Ateneo de Cagayan on December 1, 2025 at Cucina Higala, Cagayan de Oro City.

This activity marked the formal conclusion of the week-long celebration of the Mindanao Week of Peace (MWOP) 2025. Participants included students and youth leaders from different faiths and cultures, and officers and members of the Xavier-Ateneo Central Student Government (CSG), all coming together to affirm their shared commitment to peace and interfaith understanding.

The program opened with an interfaith prayer, followed by the welcome message of Regional Director Dr. Masorong. In his message, he emphasized that peace is a daily commitment that must be practiced beyond events such as the MWOP. He challenged the youth to take the lead in peace advocacy, recognizing them as the next generation who will continue the work of building understanding and unity in Mindanao.

During the sharing session, Mr. Najir Allamahul shared his experiences in joining the SALAAMindanao program, while MWOP 2025 organizers Mr. Edward Miguel Sunga and Ms. Jynnika Denice Ocat of CSG narrated their experiences and challenges in organizing activities for the Mindanao Week of Peace 2025.

This was followed by the interfaith dialogue “Conversations on Moving Forward,” facilitated by Miss Mona Lisa Pangan, convenor of the Interfaith Forum for Peace, Harmony and Solidarity. Participants were asked to suggest concrete ways to sustain the momentum of interfaith and peacebuilding initiatives. The proposed ideas included organizing cultural and religious immersion, youth camps, the use of social media to spread understanding, the development of an interfaith and peace-focused podcast, and other collaborative activities.

In response to these recommendations, Regional Director Masorong clearly committed that NCMF-X will support and take an active role in the realization of the suggested ideas, in partnership with the school, youth groups, and peace organizations. The program concluded with
the closing remarks of the Xavier-Ateneo CSG MWOP Project Head A.R. Mamutuk, who expressed appreciation to all those who contributed to the successful culmination of this year’s celebration.

This activity was coordinated and facilitated by the Peace Building and Conflict Resolution Division (PBCRD) under the leadership of Chief Jamaloddin P. Muti, JD, SCL, with the support of staff Hannan Sangcopan, Aisha Camal, and Aliah Derogongan.

Bridging the Faithful: Pope Leo’s Call for Unity Among Muslims, Christians, and Jews
By Dr. Gholam Mujtaba

Pope Leo XIV’s deeply moving reflection on witnessing Muslims at prayer is more than a personal sentiment — it is a historic call for interfaith understanding among the world’s major monotheistic religions: Islam, Christianity, and Judaism. During a time when global tensions often overshadow the shared spiritual roots of these faiths, his words resonate as a call for renewed dialogue, mutual respect, and a rediscovery of the sacred values that unite us.

Pope Leo expressed himself with heartfelt sincerity:
“When I first witnessed Muslims praying, I found myself unexpectedly moved in a way I had not anticipated… As I watched millions bow their heads in unity… I felt a silence inside me—deep, profound, almost overwhelming… I realized that for centuries, many of us have misunderstood Islam… When I saw men and women standing shoulder to shoulder… I saw a reflection of something humanity deeply craves equality before the Almighty… no thrones, no crowns, no titles—just souls standing in harmony before God.”

This statement captures the core of Islam’s egalitarian spirituality — a faith rooted in humility, unity, and devotion, where kings and commoners are indistinguishable before their Creator. Pope Leo’s words honestly acknowledge that misunderstandings between religions often come not from doctrinal disputes but from distance — from failing to see each other with open hearts.
Islamic Teachings: Unity, Humility, and Our Shared Divine Origin

The Pope’s reflection closely aligns with Islamic teachings. The Qur’an consistently reminds humanity of its common origin:

“O mankind, we created you from a single male and female and made you into nations and tribes so that you may know one another.”
(Qur’an 49:13)

When he speaks of “equality before the Almighty… no thrones, no crowns, no titles”, he describes exactly what the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) taught in his Farewell Sermon: that no Arab is superior to a non-Arab, nor a white to a Black, except by righteousness.

The image of millions bowing together reflects the Qur’anic idea of a community united not by race or status, but through a common spiritual humility.

Christianity’s Message of Love and Brotherhood
Pope Leo’s sentiment also aligns with the teachings of Jesus (AS), who emphasized the purity of worship rooted in sincerity rather than status. In the Gospels, Christ consistently dismantles social hierarchies, lifts up the humble, and encourages all believers to love one another.

The Pope’s acknowledgment that Islam’s beauty was often “misunderstood” reflects Christ’s own challenge against prejudice and ignorance in his time.

Judaism: (Bani Israel) The Original Monotheistic Covenant
Judaism, the earliest of the Abrahamic faiths, teaches the oneness of God and the sacred equality of all human beings created in His image (B’tzelem Elohim). The Hebrew Bible stresses justice, humility, and walking humbly with God—values that resonate deeply with both Christian and Muslim spirituality.
When the Pope describes a moment when “the world had paused,” he refers to something the Jewish sages called “kavanah”—a deep inner intention and presence before God.
A Shared Spiritual Map

Islam, Christianity, and Judaism are branches of the same divine tree. Each faith teaches:
• One God
• Reverence for Abraham (Ibrahim AS)
• Prayer as a path to humility
• Justice as a moral obligation
• The equality of all humans before the Creator

The Pope’s heartfelt statement reminds the world that beneath theological differences, there’s a shared spiritual core.
Toward a New Era of Interfaith Understanding

Pope Leo’s words should motivate Muslims, Christians, Jews, and all faithful communities to reconnect—not through political stories, but through shared truths of devotion, humility, and compassion.

His reflection represents a turning point: a Christian leader publicly, courageously, and lovingly acknowledging the spiritual beauty of Islam.
This is more than just an interfaith gesture; it’s a move toward healing centuries of misunderstanding.
In a world broken by ideological splits, his message reminds us that:
Humanity cannot afford separation when our scriptures teach unity.

We cannot preach peace while practicing distance.
And we cannot build civilizations without building understanding.

Conclusion: A Shared Destiny
As Muslims bow in prayer, Christians raise their hands in worship, and Jews recite the Shema, all affirm the same eternal truth:
The Lord our God is one.
Pope Leo’s heartfelt words remind us that the road to global peace starts with recognizing our shared Creator and the dignity of every human soul.
May his message serve as a foundation for stronger connections—between mosques, churches, and synagogues; between nations; and ultimately, between hearts.
 
About the Author
Dr. Gholam Mujtaba is a Pakistani American scholar and interfaith advocate, and the Chairman of the Pakistan Policy Institute USA. He writes extensively on global peace, monotheistic harmony, and the shared moral foundations of the Abrahamic traditions.

The Pope delivered his main speech at the Presidential Palace National Library flanked by President Erdoğan, all Cabinet members, the diplomatic corps, Patriarch Bartholomew I of Istanbul, head of the Eastern Orthodox church and other Christian Patriarchs, archbishops and bishops of the region representing other Christian denominations.  This was an ecumenical historic diplomacy-rich trip, that highlighted Türkiye’s rich civilizational role.  The Pope’s visit was greeted positively and his message put emphasis on peace, interfaith dialogue and Türkiye’s historic Christian roots. The Pope’s visit to Iznik marked also the 1,700th Anniversary of the first Christian council there that defined tenets of the faith.

At the National Presidential Library Ambassador Farrugia had the opportunity to meet and exchange views with various Patriarchs. While in Istanbul she had the unique opportunity to meet the Pope during a prayer service at the Little Sisters of the Poor Residence for senior citizens.  The Pope was expressively delighted to learn that Ambassador Farrugia was from Malta, and a warm handshake was exchanged in spiritual friendship.

This week, Life & Peace Institute joined partners from across Ethiopia, Kenya, South Sudan, and Uganda in Nairobi for the East Africa Borderlands Civil Society Platform’s 2nd General Assembly and Capacity Enhancement Workshop. 

The three-day gathering has brought together 12 borderland CSOs and regional actors including AUBP, IGAD's Conflict Early Warning and Response Mechanism, Embassy of Sweden, Addis Ababa, and GIZ to deepen collaboration, share experiences, and shape a common agenda for advancing peace and development in the region’s border areas.

Over the coming days, the participants will review the platform’s progress, explore cross-border programming successes and challenges, and work toward finalizing a five-year strategic plan and the 2026 annual work plan.

LPI contributed to discussions on resource mobilization and financial management, reaffirming our commitment to strengthening locally rooted and locally owned peacebuilding in the Horn of Africa.

Together, we continue to build a stronger, inclusive better coordinated voice for borderland communities, ensuring they are not left behind.

Promoting Cross-Border Peace in Moyale
As result of recent hostilities along the Moyale Kenya–Ethiopia border, including violent incidents, underscore the need for coordinated, community-driven responses.
The Mobility & Movement (M&M) Project facilitated a joint cross-border peace committee meeting at the IGAD-CBDFU office in Moyale, bringing together local authorities and community leaders from both sides of the border to:
• Address immediate security concerns
• De-escalate tensions within the border communities
• Develop sustainable, locally led solutions to enhance peace and security
This initiative reflects the importance of collaboration, local ownership, and structured dialogue in strengthening peace and stability along the Moyale border corridor. European Union in Kenya

Clara Thalmann was a Swiss anarchist who had been expelled from the Communist Party because of her outspoken views on Stalin. She had hitch-hiked to Barcelona at the beginning of July 1936, to participate as a swimmer with the Swiss delegation in the Popular Olympiad - the games being cancelled with the outbreak of the war. When the fascist military coup occurred on July 17th, she was integrated into a Durutti Column and fought on the Aragon Front.

Kauli ya Waziri Mkuu Dkt. Mwigulu Nchemba, kwamba kiasi cha Dola za Marekani milioni mbili (sawa na takribani Shilingi Bilioni 4.5) zimetolewa kwa ajili ya kuchochea chokochoko na vurugu nchini, limezua mjadala mkali mtandaoni.
Watumiaji wa mitandao ya kijamii wamejikita katika kuchambua chanzo cha vurugu, maslahi ya mataifa ya kigeni, na umuhimu wa busara katika kushughulikia masuala ya kitaifa.
Waziri Mkuu alisema kuwa wachochezi wamelenga kuharibu uchumi wa nchi na kurudisha nyuma maendeleo, huku lengo kuu likiwa ni kunyakua rasilimali adimu za Tanzania kama vile madini ya Uranium na maendeleo ya miradi ya gesi asilia.
Baada ya ufichuzi huo, maoni yamegawanyika kati ya wale wanaosisitiza umuhimu wa kufahamu maslahi ya Taifa na wale wanaotilia mkazo umakini wa vijana kujitambua.
Mchangiaji Oliver Kibua alikaribisha ufichuzi wa Serikali, akisisitiza umuhimu wa wananchi kujua chanzo na sababu ya vurugu hizo:"Afadhali kama inaweza kuwaambia wananchi sababu na chanzo cha yote wajue kipindi watu wanatumika na kuhadaika kuwa wapiganie haki kumbe wenzao wana wanachokitaka, na vurugu ikiwepo waumiao ni wananchi waliopo nchini na sio nje ya nchi."
Kibua pia alisisitiza kuwa wananchi wanapaswa kufahamu kuwa hakuna taifa linaloingilia kati masuala ya nchi nyingine bila maslahi yao binafsi. Alihimiza, "Hao wanaojitambua waamke maana wanajitambua wao hawatambui ukweli wa mambo... think before you act."
Mchangiaji mwingine alitumia nafasi hiyo kukosoa matumizi ya lugha ya matusi na mihemko katika mijadala ya kitaifa, hasa kwa wale waliowahi kushika nyadhifa za uongozi.
"...Nikuona watu waliowahi kuwa madarakani mahali fulani wakakosana na waliowaweka madarakani wanavyokuwa hawajui kutumia lugha ya ushawishi na badala yake wanatukana... Maumivu ya Oktoba 29: Taifa Laitwa Kujifunza na Kuilinda Heshima ya Tanzania

Baada ya matukio yaliyotokea Oktoba 29, 2025, kiongozi wa Kanisa la Maombezi (GRC), Mchungaji Anthony Lusekelo (‘Mzee wa Upako’), ametoa wito kwa Watanzania kutafakari na kujifunza kutokana na tukio hilo, akieleza kuwa lilitikisa sana heshima ya Taifa na halipaswi kurudiwa kamwe.
Kauli hii inatolewa huku Wito wa Kitaifa wa Rais Dkt. Samia Suluhu Hassan wa kulinda amani ukiendelea kusambaa kwa kasi miongoni mwa wananchi na vijana.
Mchungaji Lusekelo ameeleza kuwa tukio hilo limekuwa uzoefu mchungu ambao Watanzania hawakuwahi kuupitia, akifananisha hali iliyotokea Oktoba 29 na "vita ya wenyewe kwa wenyewe," na kulifananisha na mazingira ya vita ya 1977/1978 dhidi ya Idd Amin.
Akitoa pole kwa wakazi wa Dar es Salaam, Arusha, Songwe na Mwanza walioathirika, amesisitiza kuwa hali hiyo iligusa Watanzania bila ubaguzi, akitaja hata baadhi ya waumini wake maeneo ya Kimara waliathirika.
Alisema ipo haja viongozi wa dini, wazazi, viongozi wa serikali na kisiasa kutafakari namna heshima ya nchi ilivyotikisika na umuhimu wa kurejea kwenye misingi ya umoja na ustaarabu.
Amewaonya Watanzania kuwa ni muhimu yale yaliyotokea yakawa funzo, kwani huenda Taifa likakumbana na tukio kubwa zaidi baada ya miaka michache ijayo endapo amani haitalindwa.
Maoni haya ya viongozi wa dini yanaungana na msimamo thabiti wa Mheshimiwa Rais Dkt. Samia Suluhu Hassan, ambaye alitoa wito kwa Watanzania wote kulinda amani.
"Serikali Haitaruhusu Nchi Ivurugwe: Tutailinda Nchi kwa Nguvu Zote."
Wito huu umeelekezwa hasa kwa vijana, kuwakumbusha kuwa Amani ndiyo mtaji mkuu wa elimu, ajira, na biashara yao. Wamehimizwa kukataa kauli yoyote yenye nia ya kutugawa au kuvuruga utulivu tulionao.
Kauli za wananchi zilizotolewa mtandaoni baada ya tukio zinaonesha jinsi ujumbe huu unavyopokewa:Kujifunza na Kusamehe: Raia wengi wanakubaliana kwamba, "Ni kuelewana tu, tukikaa chini kila kitu kitakuwa sawa," huku wakisisitiza: "Tujitolee kusamehe, lakini tusisahau umuhimu wa kujifunza kutoka kwa makosa ya zamani."
Wananchi wamehimiza kuwa amani lazima idumishwe, lakini iambatane na haki kwa kila Mtanzania.
Ujumbe wa Rais umeeleza wazi kuwa kulinda nchi si kazi ya vyombo vya ulinzi pekee: "Ni jukumu la kila mmoja wetu, tukiwa na uzalendo na upendo kwa Taifa letu. Tuwe walinzi wa Amani katika familia, vitongoji, na maeneo yetu ya kazi."
Watanzania kwa ujumla wanakubaliana kwamba tukio la Oktoba 29 ni "kidonda tusichopaswa kuingiza tena mdudu", na kwamba suluhisho la kudumu linaanzia kwenye umoja, upendo na mazungumzo ya kiungwana.

In-Depth: UN COP30 Climate Summit Unites World Religions Under The Cult Of ‘Earth Worship’ by Alex Newman

Unlike carbon dioxide in the air, the spiritual feeling at the UN COP30 climate summit was so dark and thick you could cut it with a knife. Indeed, the Chinese Communist Party’s demonic “Dragon-Jaguar Guardian Spirit” with the world in its hands symbolized the spiritual reality behind the summit well. This official gift masquerading as “art” from the CCP to Brazil was really a perfect representation of the whole climate process.

Beneath the veneer of unity and moral purpose, critics warned the religious dimension of COP30 revealed a long-term shift that is increasingly out in the open: the re-paganization of the West and the sidelining of Christian civilization. In effect, COP30 shined the light on a growing spiritual realignment: a globalist, syncretistic, Earth-centered ethic replacing the historic Christian understanding that shaped Western civilization and gave birth to the United States and its ideas on liberty.

This religious element is much more than just moral cover for a global power grab. It is a profound re-structuring of the way people see reality, nature, life, the world, and their place in the cosmos. Climate change activism is more than just saving the environment — it is portrayed by this growing legion of religious activists as a shared spiritual mission that unites all decent and honorable people in a holy cause. Obviously, this has profound implications for humanity.

In addition to the political and economic agendas advanced at COP30, one of the least reported but most consequential developments in Belém was, in fact, the increasingly religious and spiritual framing of the global climate movement. Far from being a secular, science-driven assembly, COP30 brought together an unprecedented coalition of world religions. This alliance included everything from Catholics and Protestants to Buddhists, Muslims, Hindus, Jews, and Indigenous pagans and spiritualists. They all rallied under a reinvented global moral consensus built largely around climate action and CO2 emissions.

Even before the COP30 began, the tone was set during the Faith in Climate 2025 event this summer touted by the UN and Brazilian authorities. COP30 CEO Ana Toni was in attendance and praised the religious fervor. “We have called this great collective effort to fight climate change a ‘mutirão,’” she said, using the Indigenous word for collective effort that became a rallying cry for the summit. “But after this event, I would say that COP30 is not only a great ‘mutirão’ but also a great communion.”

Two crucial spiritual elements long documented by The New American about this environmental holy war were on full display in Belém. First, COP30 showed unprecedented religious convergence — a “spiritual coalition” bringing all the major religions and religious movements of the world together behind the UN climate program. The unity revolves around an emerging new moral framework that replaces historic biblical understandings of sin with a new vision, where CO2 emissions and other alleged offenses against “Mother Earth” are the real moral evil. COP30 culminated with a virtual interfaith climate liturgy.

Second, COP30 and the broader climate movement are now increasingly and openly integrating pagan and pantheistic spirituality into everything — all while marginalizing the biblical worldview. This was on full display throughout the summit. At official events throughout COP30, Indigenous rituals and pagan earth-worship symbolism were not only present — they were center stage in discussions about the damage humans are supposedly doing to “Mother Earth.”

Religious Convergence and Unity

Supposed man-made climate change has for years served as the perfect pretext for uniting the religions of the world behind a common cause. As The New American reported in 2022 from the COP27 in Egypt, a global interfaith coalition worked with the UN to unveil a new “Ten Commandments” on Mount Sinai. Meanwhile, the George Soros and UN-funded group Religions for Peace, an outfit described by its leader as the “UN of religions,” brings together virtually all major religious organizations and traditions behind the UN and its agenda.  

At COP30 in Belém, these trends were clearer than ever. For instance, the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) unleashed its Interfaith Liaison Committee (ILC) to inject spirituality into everything. Purporting to represent dozens of religions ranging from Christianity, Islam, and Judaism to paganism and Earth worship, the ILC’s fingerprints were ubiquitous. Its official Prayers and Meditations for COP30 spiritual event brought in imams, rabbis, and even Indigenous shamans from around the world to pray for bold “climate action.”

Meanwhile, a coordinated Interfaith Talanoa Dialogue, an Indigenous term from Fiji meaning process of discussion, featured representatives from countless religions. They stated they were all united in “climate justice” ethics and in supporting global climate targets. In their COP30 Interfaith Call to Action, the religious leaders called for restructuring global society and the global economy around “sustainability” and “climate justice.” Pointing to the recent ruling by the International Court of Justice, the religious leaders also claimed “all UN member states” were bound by supposed international law to submit.

“Climate justice necessitates a rapid and equitable phase out of fossil fuels,” reads the 2025 Interfaith Talanoa Call to Action for COP30. “Achieving a better future requires ambitiously addressing the root causes of climate change…. We as faith communities support economic and societal changes in solidarity with the bold political decisions necessary to build a just and sustainable path forward.”

Ironically, after berating generations of American Christians for being involved in politics, the leftist religious leaders argued that “faith communities call collectively on our moral and ethical foundation to guide, urge, and support governments” in making strong pledges to rein in CO2 emissions. “Governments must exercise political will, leadership, and moral courage to raise ambition and create firm and transparent timetables to ensure targets are met,” the interfaith declaration declared.

Islamic leaders also provided a major push. Omar Lakis with Brazil’s Instituto de Estudos da Religião (Institute for Religious Studies), speaking at the Faith in Climate 2025 event for COP30, said the Muslim Prophet Muhammad taught his followers environmental preservation. “They would save water, even when it was abundant, and conserve resources,” Lakis declared, calling it a “lifestyle that coincides” with fighting global warming. “There’s a word for this, ruma, which means the habit of using only what is necessary. It’s about using water as needed, food as needed, and planting a tree.”

‘Christians’ Join Forces, too

Even ostensibly Christian churches and denominations have been jumping on the bandwagon, and they were out in force at COP30. One of the key “Christian” players, known as the ACT Alliance, purports to represent more than 140 Christian denominations around the world. In its COP30 statement, the group was blunt: “Climate justice is a faith imperative that unites us across traditions.”

The World Council of Churches, long under the sway of Soviet-aligned church leaders, pretended to speak on behalf of churches worldwide. “We have launched an Ecumenical Decade of Climate Justice Action at our central committee meeting in Johannesburg in June. And the reason that the word ‘justice’ is part of this title is very important,” said WCC central committee moderator Bishop Professor Dr. Heinrich Bedford-Strohm. “It cannot be that those who have contributed least to climate change are the first victims. There needs to be reparatory justice for those who are now the victims.”

His theological views were interesting, to put it mildly. “When we say God created us, we also affirm that God created us together with nonhuman creation,” argued Bedford-Strohm. “That gives us a sister and brother-relationship with the whole of nonhuman creation.”

The Roman Catholic Church was out in force, too, featuring its largest delegation ever to attend a UN climate summit with what insiders called an “unprecedented number” of cardinals and bishops. Now under the leadership of Pope Leo XIV, who famously blessed a large ice block as part of a recent climate event, the Vatican doubled down on the late Pope Francis’ eco-religiosity this year. Catholic clergy issued endless pronouncements urging humanity to repent and embrace the “moral duty” to protect Earth.

Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin, who led the delegation and spoke at the opening leaders’ summit on behalf of Pope Leo XIV, called for united global action. “Collective selfishness and disregard for the common good prevent nations from taking the action that morality demands,” Parolin declared on behalf of the new pontiff. “Climate change is a global problem demanding a global vision.”

The pope himself even released a video encouraging the religious leaders gathered in the Amazon for COP30. Celebrating a “global community that works together,” he lamented that it has “delivered progress, but not enough.” It is time for “concrete actions” rather than just hope and determination, the pope continued.

“The creation is crying out in floods and droughts, storms and relentless heat,” Leo added, claiming without citing a source that one in three people “live in great vulnerability because of climate change.” There is still time to prevent too much warming, “but the window is closing,” he said, touting the Paris Accord as the “strongest tool” for protecting the planet. “Stronger climate action,” he said, will create “fairer economic systems.”

The Laudato Si’ encyclical by Pope Francis was a groundbreaking development for the UN, as it provided a religious pretext for the UN’s environmental agenda. And despite Francis’ passing, it reverberated all the way to the COP30. Indeed, COP30 President André Corrêa do Lago said the papal document was regarded by the Brazilian government as “both an ethical compass and a pragmatic guide for this global mobilization” as it prepared its Global Ethical Stocktake for COP30.

Laudato Si’ Movement COP30 representative Susana Moreira, a green-haired activist with tattoos, explained more in an interview with The New American. “We brought together different faith leaders from different religions to really talk about this ethical dimension,” she said. “Because we’re all part of this common home and different religions in different ways, they’re all connected to this grounding of how the earth helps us not only to sustain our bodies, our foods, everything that we need, but also how we practice our religions…. We can really find ways to create this interreligious dialogue, to create stronger bonds between the religions, to help care for this common home of ours.”

While there was plenty of “Christian” representation and rhetoric, genuine Christian ideas rooted in the Bible or even tradition were almost entirely absent — except when selectively invoked, usually out of context, to support UN climate mandates.

“Christianity” that affirmed global governance was praised as “prophetic.” Christianity that questioned climate orthodoxy was derided as regressive, anti-science, or dangerous.

Re-paganization of the West

At the heart of this whole climate process is the often-implicit but sometimes explicitly stated argument that biblical Christianity is the reason for the “climate crisis” and environmental damage more broadly. In his landmark 1967 essay “The Historical Roots of Our Ecological Crisis,” academic Lynn White, Jr. argued that the Western Christian tradition — especially its interpretation of the Genesis “dominion mandate” — was the root of environmental problems.

The reason this biblical view is so problematic, the professor argued, is because it caused people to think of nature and the planet as a resource for human benefit. This line of thinking has had enormous influence over decades of ecological thought. As one summary puts it: Many environmental writers contend that “Christian dominion theology” conditioned people to undervalue non-humans, thus laying ideological foundations for exploitation of nature.

White, who taught at Princeton, UCLA, and Stanford, blasted Christianity as “the most anthropocentric religion the world has seen.” Among other concerns, he argued that it “insisted that it is God’s will that man exploit nature for his proper ends.” As such, he concluded that because modern science and technology grew out of these Christian views, “Christianity bears a huge burden of guilt” for the supposed “ecological crisis.”

The solution to this problem: Indigenous and tribal wisdom and spirituality. And there were plenty of Indigenous “folx” in feathered headdresses and beads to shower wisdom upon the post-Christian government, media, and non-profit heavyweights at COP30. Guarani leader Mirim Ju Yam, for instance, opened a COP30 event with ancestral ritual songs. “The forest is alive,” he chanted. “The spirits of the land speak. We must listen.”

“In our culture lies the seed of preservation, of life in harmony with the Earth, and the understanding that nature is not something out there,” Ju Yam continued, painting a picture of an idyllic past before the arrival of Christian civilization in which his ancestors enjoyed a “sacred relationship” with land and nature. “Nature is not an object. Nature is everything that exists. We are part of that nature.”

Another religious leader involved in the COP30, “Mother Cícera of Oshun,” with a traditional Afro-pagan religion known as Candomblé, explained her take. “Fresh water belongs to Oshun, rainwater to Iansã, lagoon water to Nanã, which represents decomposition — it falls into the lagoon, the lagoon decomposes, becomes fossil, sinks to the depths, and starts anew,” she said. “We have the god of the forests, Oshosi. All our gods are from nature.” These nature gods must be honored and appeased with sacrifices to save the world.

Multiple COP30 documents and side events promoted the pagan and animistic idea that rivers, forests, ecosystems, and nature have “rights” that must be protected. Pagan shamans in full regalia literally offered prayers to various deities referred to clearly in the Christian scriptures (Deuteronomy 32:17; 1 Corinthians 10:20) as demons. Sessions opened with ancestral chants, invocations of forest spirits, and affirmations that the Earth is a living spiritual being — language rooted not in the biblical worldview but in animistic and polytheistic traditions.

Indeed, multiple “Indigenous leaders” at the summit told The New American that “Mother Earth” and “Father Sky” were upset with humanity over climate change and other real and imagined abuses. Because of that, these deities were taking action against mankind. “Indigenous wisdom and spirituality” were repeatedly touted as the solution to placating these angry planetary deities.   

Even the UN’s own official messaging was permeated with this overall worldview. For instance, the UN’s top officials and even its agreements repeatedly refer to “Mother Earth,” “the spirit of the forest,” and “healing our relationship with the planet,” all clear echoes of the anti-Christian cosmologies that are increasingly being seen as essential to saving the world.

None of this is new. In 2010, the COP16 in Cancun opened with a prayer by UN climate chief Cristiana Figueres, executive secretary of the UNFCCC. But it was not a Christian prayer. Rather, she prayed to Ixchel, whom she described as the Mayan goddess of “creativity” and “tapestries.” Figueres requested divine wisdom from this being to weave a “creative tapestry” of “climate solutions.” A quick online search, however, revealed that Ixchel has traditionally been associated with cannibalism, war, and human sacrifice. No doubt the CCP’s “Dragon-Jaguar Guardian Spirit” would approve.   

Going back further, TNA Senior Editor William Jasper watched as the UN Earth Summit in 1992 in Rio de Janeiro unveiled the same dark spiritual agenda. “From start to finish, the Rio Earth Summit was suffused in pagan-pantheist-New Age ‘spirituality,’ and enshrined a new dogma of the ‘Sacred Earth’ and ‘Divine Nature,’” he wrote.

Indeed, in his opening statement, Earth Summit Secretary-General Maurice Strong directed the world’s attention to the Declaration of the Sacred Earth Gathering. “The changes in behavior and direction called for here,” said Strong, “must be rooted in our deepest spiritual, moral and ethical values.”

Using tools such as the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous People (UN DRIP), the UN and globalists have been using Indians as a battering ram against Western civilization — especially the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and Latin America. In fact, the UN agreement, approved by Obama, is being used to seize vast quantities of land worldwide under the guise of returning it to “Indigenous” peoples, while delegitimizing countries such as the United States.  

Critics Respond

While almost no critics were on scene at the COP30, there are powerful voices speaking out. One of those is Dr. E. Calvin Beisner, Ph.D., president of the Cornwall Alliance for the Stewardship of Creation, a Christian environmental organization working to apply biblical truth to these issues. Speaking to The New American, Dr. Beisner argued that the religious and spiritual views being promoted throughout the UN climate process are deeply unbiblical.

“The Bible clearly places man, made in the image of God, at the pinnacle of creation, and gives man authority, under God, to rule over the rest of the earth,” he explained. “That doesn’t mean, as some environmentalists falsely assert, that Scripture justifies abusing nature. Instead, man’s being made in God’s image means man’s use of nature should reflect God’s as revealed in Genesis 1:1-25.”

“God made everything from nothing, brought light out of darkness, order out of chaos, life out of nonlife, and great abundant variety of life, and instructed each kind to multiply,” continued Dr. Beisner. “Man’s rule over the earth, mandated in Genesis 1:26-28, should reflect that: maximizing productivity by bringing more and more out of less and less; improving our knowledge (‘light’) to bring greater order out of lesser order; and increasing life.”

Unfortunately, those gathered at COP30 buy into predictions of catastrophic environmental consequences from the use of fossil fuels, explained Beisner. Sound science and economics show the predictions to be inaccurate, with the benefits of fossil fuels far outweighing whatever minor harms might come from their use, he said, adding that CO2 is good for the planet. “In short, COP30 is fighting the wrong enemy with the wrong means,” he concluded.

Some Brazilian Christians became fiercely critical, too. In response to the CCP’s “Guardian Spirit” statue, many Brazilian Christians from across denominations expressed outrage, saying the horned statue was clearly “demonic.” Across social media, numerous commentators argued that Brazil — famous for its iconic Christ the Redeemer statue on Mount Corcovado — belongs to Jesus Christ, not the CCP’s “Guardian Spirit.”

Brazilian evangelical Christian leader Estevam Hernandes, with the Renascer (Rebirth) church, was quoted in the Brazilian press noting that “the horned dragon is the biblical symbol of deception and power contrary to God.” He also noted that the statue suggests “a fusion of national identity with values that do not reflect our Christian tradition.” Pointing to Revelation 12:9, Hernandes suggested the figure may be a representation of “the great dragon … who is called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world,” who “was thrown down to the earth.”

Sheila Zilinsky, a former Canadian environmental official turned critic and author of the popular book Green Gospel, has long argued that the real agenda is in fact spiritual. “The ‘Church of Climate Change’ is not a trend — it’s a global religious takeover redirecting believers from the Gospel of Jesus Christ to the Gospel of Earth Worship; pantheism/Gaia,” she told The New American. “Its language — ‘sustainability,’ ‘harmony with nature,’ ‘saving the earth’ — is not biblical but rooted in Occultism, satanism and paganism.” 

Blasting the blasphemous notion of Mother Earth as the goddess Gaia, Zilinsky also pointed to writings by the Apostle Paul in Romans 1. He warned that when people suppress the truth in their unrighteousness, they “exchange the truth of God for a lie, and worship and serve the creation more than the Creator.” The Green movement, warned Zilinsky, is the “ultimate fulfillment” of this warning. “It is not about saving the planet,” she said. “It is about replacing God. Green theology is the greatest spiritual deception of our era!”

Fortunately, the American people — and American Christians in particular — can deal a deadly blow to this subversive agenda. But it will require action. BY LUGETE MUSSA LUGETE.

Vita ya kiuchumi ni mgongano kati ya nchi na nguvu kubwa za kimataifa zinazofanyika si kwa matumizi ya silaha za kijeshi, bali kupitia zile njia za kiuchumi, kifedha, kiteknolojia na kibiashara zinazolenga kudhoofisha au kutawala uchumi wa upande mwingine. Kwenye vita ya kiuchumi, mataifa  makubwa hutumia mbinu kama:

Vikwazo vya kiuchumi (sanctions) ili kudhoofisha uchumi wa mpinzani.

Kudhibiti masoko ya kimkakati kama madini adimu, nishati, au teknolojia.

Kufadhili makundi ya kiraia, vyama, harakati za mitandaoni, au taasisi ili kuathiri maamuzi ya kisiasa ndani ya nchi lengwa.

Ujasusi wa kiuchumi na udhibiti wa taarifa muhimu.

Kupandikiza propaganda za kimataifa, hasa kupitia mitandao ya kijamii.

Kuweka masharti ya mikopo, misaada au uwekezaji yanayofunga mikono ya nchi inayolengwa.

Kudhibiti njia za usafirishaji, bandari, na usambazaji wa bidhaa muhimu.

Vita ya kiuchumi ni mapambano ya ushawishi wa kiuchumi kati ya mataifa makubwa, yanayolenga kupata udhibiti wa rasilimali, masoko, na maamuzi ya sera za nchi zingine bila kutumia jeshi, bali kupitia nguvu ya uchumi.

Katika miongo ya hivi karibuni, Tanzania imejikuta katikati ya mchakato mpana wa kijiografia na kiuchumi unaovuka mipaka ya utaifa, ukihusisha ushindani mkali kati ya China na Urusi kwa upande mmoja, dhidi ya Marekani na Umoja wa Ulaya kwa upande mwingine. Chanzo kikuu cha mvutano huu ni rasilimali muhimu na adimu zinazopatikana nchini Tanzania hususan madini ya kimkakati kama vile rare earth elements, graphite, helium, kobalt, nikeli, lithium, na gesi asilia kutoka Lindi na Mtwara ambapo dunia ya leo inayahitaji kwa teknolojia za kisasa, silaha za kisasa, nishati mbadala, na uzalishaji wa vifaa vya umeme.

Katika mazingira haya ya ushindani, Tanzania haipo tu kama mwangalizi wa siasa za maziwa makuu, bali imekuwa kiini cha mapambano mapya ya kiuchumi na kijiintelijensia, ambapo mataifa makubwa hutumia sera, diplomasia, mashirika ya kimataifa, kampuni za teknolojia, mitandao ya kiraia, pamoja na mbinu chafu kuimarisha ushawishi wao. Ndani ya mgongano huu, kumeshuhudiwa pia kuibuka kwa harakati za vijana hususan kundi linaloitwa Gen Z ambalo mara nyingi limehusishwa na mikondo ya nje kupitia ufadhili wa taasisi, mashirika ya kimataifa, na kampeni za kidijitali zinazolenga kutengeneza mazingira ya kisiasa na kijamii yanayoweza kuathiri sera za kiuchumi na usimamizi wa madini.

Kwa mantiki hiyo, kile kinachoonekana kama maandamano ya kawaida ya vijana au mitikisiko ya kisiasa ndani ya nchi, katika macho ya wataalam wa geopolitics, ni sehemu ya mchezo mpana zaidi: vita ya kimya kimya ya kiuchumi, yenye mizizi katika ushindani wa kimataifa wa utajiri wa Madini. 

Tanzania ikiwa na amani, rasilimali nyingi, na nafasi ya kimkakati Afrika Mashariki imekuwa uwanja muhimu wa kupimwa nguvu kati ya mabavu ya mashariki yaani Urusi na China dhidi ya magharibi yaani Marekani, Umoja wa Ulaya na NATO.

Utangulizi huu unaweka msingi wa kuchambua kwa undani namna mgongano wa kimaslahi ya kimataifa unavyoathiri siasa, uchumi, diplomasia, na mienendo ya kijamii nchini Tanzania, pamoja na jinsi vijana wanavyokuwa chombo kinachotumiwa au kinachojikuta katikati ya mivutano ya mataifa makubwa.

this is emma, named after emma goldman (1869–1940), a midwife and anarchist revolutionary who helped shape anarchist political thought as we now know it. she came to the US from present-day lithuania in 1886, and was drawn to anarchism and political struggle after the haymarket affair that same year. after a brief, failed marriage, she moved to new york city in 1889, where she met alexander berkman and johann most. with berkman she had a decades-long relationship that took many forms, and most trained her in public speaking. she gave many speeches around the country over the next 30 years, and founded the anarchist journal “mother earth” in 1906. speaking out on issues like prisons, atheism, freedom of speech, militarism, capitalism, marriage, free love, and homosexuality, she came to be labeled “red emma” by her admirers and “the most dangerous woman in america” by everyone else.

in 1919, goldman and berkman had their citizenship revoked and they were sent to russia. finding repression, mismanagement, and corruption instead of the workers' paradise they expected, they ended up leaving for germany. from there, goldman spent time in several european countries and canada, supporting various causes and speaking out against others. in the late 1920s, she wrote her autobiography, "living my life." the video clip in the last slide is perhaps the only recording of her, and it was from her speaking tour in the US in 1934 to promote her book. her fame faded after her death in 1940, but it was revived in the 70s when a collection of her writing was published. it was around this time when t-shirts appeared with a quote attributed to emma: "If I can't dance, I don't want to be in your revolution." though there is no record of her ever saying or writing this, she did make some similar statements and i believe she would have agreed with the sentiment.

since anarchism is largely misunderstood, here's an explanation in emma's words: "Anarchism, then, really stands for the liberation of the human mind from the dominion of religion; the liberation of the human body from the dominion of property; liberation from the shackles and restraint of government. Anarchism stands for a social order based on the free grouping of individuals for the purpose of producing real social wealth; an order that will guarantee to every human being free access to the earth and full enjoyment of the necessities of life, according to individual desires, tastes, and inclinations."

emma is part of the matriarch series, made from white stoneware clay. she is available for purchase through Florida CraftArt Gallery. side note that i completed emma on june 27, which i later learned was emma goldman’s birthday.

In 2002, in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan—a conservative region where girls' education was controversial and women's public activism was almost unthinkable—a 16-year-old girl named Gulalai Ismail started teaching workshops.
She gathered young women and girls to talk about leadership, rights, self-worth, and peacebuilding.
In a place where the Taliban would later ban girls' education entirely, where women were expected to remain invisible in public life, Gulalai was telling girls they had power, voice, and the right to shape their own futures.
She called the organization Aware Girls. She founded it with her 15-year-old sister Saba.
One of their early program attendees was a girl named Malala Yousafzai, who participated in 2011—a year before she was shot by the Taliban for advocating girls' education.
What started as small workshops grew into a movement—training young women in leadership, documenting human rights abuses, countering extremist narratives, and advocating for peace in a region torn by violence.
For years, Gulalai worked in increasingly dangerous conditions. The Taliban opposed her. Conservative communities saw her as a threat. Her organization was labeled one of five "agents of the CIA" in Pakistan.
In May 2014, four armed gunmen came to her family home in Peshawar, shouting her name, demanding her father open the door. They started shooting into the air when he refused. Gulalai wasn't there—she'd been delayed at the airport because her luggage was lost. That accident may have saved her life.
But the danger wasn't only from extremists. Gulalai didn't just advocate for women's education. She criticized military operations that displaced civilians. She spoke out about enforced disappearances. In January 2019, she documented allegations that security forces had sexually assaulted Pashtun women.
In Pakistan, criticizing the military is one of the most dangerous things you can do.
The government response was swift. Her passport was confiscated. Her name was placed on Exit Control Lists. Security forces raided her family home repeatedly. She was charged with sedition and terrorism-related offenses.
The message was clear: stop speaking, or face consequences.
Gulalai kept speaking.
In 2019, the pressure became unbearable. The charges escalated. The threats became more specific.
She made a decision: if she stayed, she would be arrested, imprisoned, possibly killed.
So she went underground.
For four months, she lived in hiding—moving between safe houses, timing her movements carefully, stepping out only with a scarf covering her face, relying on an underground network of fellow activists who risked everything to hide her.
Security forces raided homes. Friends were interrogated. Her family was under constant surveillance.
In September 2019, she managed to escape. First to Sri Lanka, then to the United States. She arrived in New York and applied for asylum. How she slipped past the exit controls remains unknown—she won't say, to protect those who helped her.
When she left, she bent down and touched Pakistani soil. "This is where I belong," she said. "This is my country."
Most people in her situation would rest, recover, try to build a quiet new life.
Gulalai kept speaking.
From exile in New York, she continues documenting human rights abuses in Pakistan. She advocates for activists facing persecution. She speaks at international forums, uses social media to amplify voices that Pakistan's government tries to suppress.
Her courage has been recognized internationally. In 2016, French President François Hollande presented her organization with the Chirac Prize for Conflict Prevention. In 2017, she received the Anna Politkovskaya Award for campaigning against religious extremism—an award previously given to Malala Yousafzai.
But her family continues to pay the price.
Her father, Muhammad Ismail—himself a human rights activist and retired professor—was arrested in 2021 on terrorism charges. He spent months in prison. Both her parents have faced ongoing judicial harassment. The accusations are widely seen as retaliation for raising an activist daughter.
Gulalai understands something crucial: if she stops speaking just because she's safe now, then the government succeeded in silencing a critic.
So she refuses to be silent, even from thousands of miles away.
She was 16 when she started teaching girls they had rights worth fighting for.
Now, approaching 40, she's in exile—unable to safely return to her homeland, watching her parents face persecution, processing years of trauma.
But she's still fighting. Still speaking. Still believing that her voice, and the voices of the women she advocates for, matter more than her personal safety.
Some voices refuse to be silenced.
Not by extremists. Not by governments. Not by exile.
Gulalai Ismail is one of those voices.

I'm excited to share that I've received my results for my annotated bibliography on "Unsilencing Trauma, Documenting Peace: The Representation of Women's Mental Health and Agency in the Historiography of the Nigeria-Biafra War" – and I earned a 75/100!
This project challenged me to ask difficult questions: Where are the women in our historical narratives? Whose voices have been erased, and how can we recover them?
Working with memoirs, literature, and oral histories, I explored how historians are finally giving voice to the women who survived the Nigerian-Biafran War (1967-1970) – women whose trauma, resilience, and agency were systematically excluded from official records.
My lecturer's feedback affirmed that the critical analysis and methodological approach were strong, which means so much to me. This is just the beginning.
To anyone working on their research, tackling difficult topics, or feeling uncertain about their academic journey: keep going. Your voice matters. Your questions matter. The stories we choose to tell and recover—they matter.
Onward! 📚✨

MAZAN JIYA: Takaitaccen Tarihin Marigayi Alhaji Abdu Fari (AAF) Katsina 1919-2014

Daga Dakta Sani Abdu Fari

Asalin Suna Da Shekarar Haihuwa

Marigayi Alhaji Abdu Fari sunansa na yanka Abdullahi kuma sunan mahaifinsa Kafarda Muhammadu Gidado Dan Kusada Muhammadu Bello Dan Bebeji Muhammadu Gidado Dan Sarkin Katsina Malam Umarun Dallaje, Dan Abdulmumin Abubakar (Mummuni), Dan Abubakar Muhammadu (Garba Madambacin Gabas), Dan Muhammadu Magoshi. An haifi marigayi Alhaji Abdu Fari a shekarar 1919 a Unguwar Madawaki cikin garin Katsina. Yayi makarantar koyon karatun Al’qur’ani a makarantar Liman Malam Audi da ke unguwar Liman a garin Katsina.

Takaitaccen Yawon Kasuwanci, Abokan Hudda Da Kuma Iyayen-gidansa

Ya fara kasuwanci tun yana dan shekara goma sha biyar yana daukar goro daga gidan Uwar-dakinsa Hajia Baika (mahaifiyar su Alhaji Raben Baika, Iron Baba da Dahiru Saude), a lokacin Hajiya Baika tana kiranshi da suna ‘Danhamsin Dan’albarka’ marigayin ya kasance yana bin kasuwanni dayawa kaman kasuwar Danmusa, Dutsinma da sauransu. A wannan lokaci ne kuma yake sayen dinkakkun riguna yana sayarwa shida yayansa Marigayi Alhaji Musan Kafarda. Baccin Hajiya Baika kuma marigayin yana da wani maigidan wanda ake kira Alhaji Gani (Mahaifin Alhaji Musa Gani) wanda yake bashi huhunan goro yana sayarwa, a wancan lokacin idan yakai kaya Dutsinma yana zama gidan wani attajiri da ake kira Wowon Labon-Didi yana koyon dinki, bayan wani lokaci likkafar kasuwanci tayi gaba sai ya yi hijira ya koma garin Jos yana dinkin Jikkuna da sauran aikace aikace na sana’arsa, yana nan yana wannan kasuwanci a garin na Jos.

A lokacin zamansa garin Jos jarinsa ya habaka wannan ya sanya ya nemi matsawa gaba domin fadada cinikayya fannin saye da sayerwa, likkafa ta kara gaba inda ya koma garin Ile-Ife na Jihar Oyo a yau, a shekarar 1943 ya kama harkar tankun goro, Allah yayi mashi kwazo da jijircewa ta fuskar kasuwanci da kokarin nema, alokacin sai ya fara sayen huhunan goro yana kawowa a garin Ibadan inda mutanen arewacin Nigeria suke zuwa sari. 
Marigayin ya tafi zuwa aikin Hajjinsa na farko tare da mahaifinsa a shekarar 1956 lokacin yana dan shekara 36, a wannan tafiyar ne suka hadu da Ahmadu Bello Sardauna lokacin da suka hau jirgin sama mai cin zango a kasar Khartoum kan hanyarsu ta zuwa kasa mai tsarki.

Ba da jimawaba marigayin yayi fice wajen sana’ar ta goro har ya kasance ya koma a garin Iteku inda shima babbar kasuwace ta saye da sayarwar goro, sanda ya koma garin Iteku ne alokacin ya rika aikowa da huhunan goron zuwa arewacin Nigeria a cikin jirgin kasa har zuwa Funtua, Gusau, Sokoto da Kano. Bayan yan shekaru marigayin ya koma garin Ibadan da zama, zamantakewarsa a wadannan wurare ne ya sanya marigayin ya kware da harshen Yarbanci hatta da Iyalinsa suma suka nakalci yaren na Yarbanci. Yayi Shekaru Ashirin a unguwar Sabo cikin garin Ibadan a inda sukayi zamantakewa da huddodi na arziki da wasu mutanen Arewacin Nigeria.

Wasu daga cikin abokanen huddarsa sun hada da Alhaji Mamman Fari Kano, Alhaji Tanko (Mahaifin Alhaji Labo Tarka), Alhaji Barau Mai Fanka, Alhaji Jibrin na Madugu, Alhaji Ali Bagobiri, Alhaji Sani Mashal, Alhaji Mamman Mai kekune Kano, Alhaji Bako Jagindi, Alhaji Lawal na Kadiri Kura Kano, Alhaji Abdu na Idi Gora, Alhaji Mamman Dan Mai-Teba, Alhaji Dan-Baba Mijin Maigari, Alhaji Mamman Alabura Bamalle, Alhaji Mamman Ifo (Sarkin Yakin Katsina), Alhaji Ubaidu, Alhaji Danlami Na-mai-kalango Ibadan, Alhaji Dauda Kambari, Alhaji Kari Borno, Alhaji Garba Sagadan, Alhaji Mudi dan-Zaki (shugaban jam’iyyar NPC a Ibadan), Alhaji Garba na Bara Dan Sukuwar Dawaki, Alhaji Dikko dan Sarkin Hausawa Ibadan da sauransu Kafin ya dawo gida Katsina a lokacin da fitina tayi yawa sanadiyyar kashe Ahmadu Bello Sardauna.

Dawowa Gida Katsina

Alhaji Abdu Fari ya dawo gida Katsina a cikin shekarar alif da dari tara da sittin da bakwai (1967) a lokacinne ya fadada kasuwancinsa da harkokinsa wanda ya kunshi sufuri tun lokacin ‘MAN DIESEL mai Uwa da Diya’, Marsandi(Mercedes) da Bilhodu(Bedford) wanda alokacin Alhaji Halliru Kafur(Hali Brother) abokinsa kuma amininsa yana Janar Manaja na kanfanin UTC a Kano, sauran sana’o’insa sun hada da kwangila, noma, Kamfanin sayar da kaya(spare parts) na manyan motoci Automotive Parts Industry (API) a Kano da sauran harkoki. Wasu daga cikin manyan kwangilolin da ya farayi sune yin kwangilar magudanan ruwa daga Ajiwa Dam zuwa sassan garin Katsina da kewaye, aikin Dam na Bakori, da Dam din Bakolori, da gidajen Mafara sai kwangilar ginin makarantu masu yawa irin su makarantar sakandare ta Gangara, Ministry of works ta Mani, GGSS Kankiya, WTC Katsina, Fertilizer stores masu yawa a fadin Katsina Kaman na Safana, Dutsinma, Katsina, da dakin koyon aiki (workshop) na makarantar BATC a nan garin Katsina da sauransu. 
Alhaji Abdu Fari ya zama fitaccen mai sufuri (transporter) a Afrika da Duniya baki daya wanda za’a iya gani a shafunan yanar gizo yanzu da zaran an rubuta sunansa a GOOGLE wanda har ya zuwa yanzu kanfunnan kerawa da sayar da manyan motoci da injina wadanda yayi hudda dasu na kasashen Germany, Holland, America da England suna aiko da littattafai(catalogue) da wasiku zuwa ga adireshinsa, ya kasance mai sufuri na takin zamani, kayan gona, Shanu da kayan man fetur a duk fadin Nigeria. Marigayin shine shugaba (chairman) na farko na masu sufuri (NARTO) a Katsina, kuma yayi sshugaba na farar hula na hukumar kare hadurra (Road Safety) a Katsina, yayi zama mamba(member) na hadin kan yansanda da mutanan gari (Police Community Relations Committee) a Katsina.
Wasu daga cikin ayyuka da kasuwancinsa a Katsina
Marigayi Alhaji Abdu Fari ya zama babban mai sufuri (transporter) kuma wakili na kamfanin mulmula karafa (Katsina Steel Rolling Mill), babban dealer na gidan simintin Sakkwato (Sokoto Cement), Gidan simintin Ashaka (Ashaka Cement), kamfanin kayan masarufi na Lever Brothers, Kamfanin lemun sha na Brahma Guarana da dai sauransu. Alokacinnan marigayin yayi gine gine masu yawa tare da taimakon addini ta fannoni daban daban wajen gina Islamiyoyi, rijiyoyi da manyan masallatai na jumu’a akarkashin kulawar babban yaronsa kuma amininsa Alhaji Sani Danballaje.
Marigayin ya kasance Dan-majalisar Sarkin Katsina tun bayan nadin marigayi Maimartaba Sarkin Katsina Alhaji Muhammadu Kabir Usman saboda kauna da aminci dake tsakaninsu da Sarki tun da dadewa, wannan kauna ta zarce har ya zuwa Mai Martaba Sarkin Katsina Alhaji Abdulmummuni Kabir Usman wanda alokacin da Alhaji Abdu Fari ya rasu Sarkin yataso ya taho gidan marigayin ya zauna na tsawon lokaci har akayi masa sutura da salla kuma alokacin Mai Martaba Sarki yake nuna jimamin rashin mutun irin Alhaji Abdu Fari ga masarautarsa da kasar Katsina baki daya. Sannan kuma marigayin ya kasance mamba na Gidauniyar Jihar Katsina tun da aka kafata a karkashin jagorancin Janar Muhammadu Buhari har ya zuwa lokacin da ya rasu.

Bai Wa Ilimi Mahimmaci

Neman ilimi na addini da na zamani wani al’amari ne mai matukar muhimmance a wajen marigayi Alhaji Abdu Fari wanda a lokacin rayuwarsa zakaji yana yawaita fadin “WANDA BASHI DA ILIMI KO A GIDANSU ICCEN DARNI NE, A BAYA YAKE”, hakan ya sanya cewa babu wani abu da yayansa, dangi da masu jibantarsa suka fi samun romon tallafi a wurinsa sama da harkar Ilimi. Ya kasance mai tsare yayansa suna karatun Allo da na littafan addinin musulunci a cikin Gidansa, sannan kuma ya sama wa yayansa guraben neman ilimi a makarantu Kaman su BUK, UDUS, ABU, UNIMAID, Zoom technologies India, Linton University College Malaysia da sauran makarantu a Nigeria da kasashen ketare. Hatta almajirai masu yin hidima a Gidansa suna da kaso na tallafin neman ilimi wanda mafi yawancinsu ya sanya su makarantar ATC a Katsina, sakamakon yin hakan, a yanzu haka akwai kimanin mutum guda a cikin almajiransa wanda yake da PhD, guda hudu suna da Master Degree sannan misalign guda 47 suna da Degree na farko kuma mafi yawancinsu suna aikin koyarwa ko kuma aikin ofisoshi a jihohin Katsina, Zanfara, Kebbi, Sokoto da Jigawa. Wannan ba karamin kokari ba ne tare da hangen nesa da kokarin taimakon al’umma. 

Ayyukan Addini

Marigayi Alhaji Abdu Fari ya kasance mai hazaka da kula da addini a duk inda yake kuma yana kokarin taimakawa da inganta lamurra na addinin musulunci ta fannoni daban daban irin su gina Islamiyyoyi da masallatai na hamsu salawatu da kuma na sallar Jumu’a masu yawa a fadin jihar Katsina da wasu wuraren ta hanyar samun labarin bukatuwar yin hakan daga malamai masu da’awa a duk sassan kasar Nigeria da Niger Republic. Wadansu daga cikin malamai da mutanen da suka taimaka wajen yinwadannan ayyuka sun hada da Marigayi Liman Lawal na babbab masallcin Katsina, Malan Abbate, malan Muttaka Unguwar Liman, Malan Sulaiman Dutsin-Amare, Malan Yakubu Musa Hassan, Alhaji Sani Danballaje, da sauransu. Marigayin kuma yana daya daga cikin mutane na farko da suka rika gyaran makabartu da dukiyarsu ciki da wajen Jihar Katsina.
A fannin ruko da addini kuwa marigayin ya zama abun nuni da kuma koyi, saboda harkokinsa na kasuwanci basu hanashi kula da sallolinsa Hamsu salawatu ba a cikin Jam’i kullun kuma a babban masallacin jumu’a na garin Katsina, wanda hakan ya sanya marigayin ya zama tamkar agogon da ke nuna lokacin salla, har ya kasance limamin babban masallcin Katsina yakan bashi ratar mintina kafin ya tada salla idan bai ganshi ba, sanin cewa lallai akwai lalurin da ya dan rikeshi amma yana kan hanyar sa ta zuwa masallacin. Livelihood Support Grant Disbursement in Mandera County 

Dr Lynette Ochuma, Acting Secretary of the Directorate of Social Development | State Department for Social Protection, and Mandera County Deputy Governor, H.E Dr. Ali Maalim Mohamud, graced the KUZA JAMII grant disbursement cheque signing ceremony at AMARA BLUE RESORT in Mandera Town today. They were joined by the GENCAD Team, headed by our CEO, Abdirashid Ali and representatives from the KUZA JAMII Consortium members, Village Enterprise(VE), the consortium lead, Smart Regional Consultants - SRC, CHASP Advisory and Echo Network Africa Foundation.

A total of KSh 40 million in livelihood support grants were successfully disbursed in Mandera County. The funds reached 2,000 households who are grouped into 658 business groups, 86 Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLA), and 5 cooperatives. These grants were allocated across three wards in Mandera East, Mandera South, Khalalio, and Kutulo Sub-Counties.

The primary goal of this initiative is to strengthen household incomes, foster local entrepreneurship, and enhance sustainable economic resilience among vulnerable communities in Mandera County. By supporting these groups and associations, the programme aims to create lasting economic empowerment and stability within the region.

This disbursement is the first phase of a comprehensive KSh 60 million grant package, which will be delivered in two stages. The remaining KSh 20 million is scheduled for disbursement in January 2026. This phased approach ensures ongoing support for beneficiary groups through training and mentoring, which encourages the sustainable growth of community-led enterprises in Mandera County.
