June 1943. Occupied France.

A young woman parachuted into darkness over the French countryside, carrying a radio transmitter and false identity papers.

Her code name was "Madeleine." Her real name was Noor Inayat Khan. She was 29 years old, a published children's author and musician who'd grown up in Paris speaking French, English, and studying Sufi philosophy.

She was also a British spy, trained as a wireless operator for the Special Operations Executive—one of the most dangerous jobs in the entire war.

Radio operators in occupied France had an average life expectancy of six weeks. The Gestapo hunted them with direction-finding equipment, tracking their transmissions, closing in with every signal sent.

Noor knew this. She went anyway.

The Only One Left

Noor Inayat Khan shouldn't have been there at all.

She was the daughter of Hazrat Inayat Khan, a renowned Indian Sufi teacher, and Ora Ray Baker, an American woman. Born in Moscow, raised in France, educated in England—she was a citizen of the world who wrote fairy tales and played the harp.

When France fell to the Nazis in 1940, Noor fled to Britain. She could have stayed safe. Instead, she joined the Women's Auxiliary Air Force, then volunteered for the SOE—Churchill's secret army of saboteurs and spies operating behind enemy lines.

Her trainers had doubts. She was gentle, idealistic, emotional—not the cold, calculating profile they looked for in agents. Some recommended she not be sent to the field.

But she was also fluent in French, skilled with radio equipment, and desperately needed. Britain was short on wireless operators.

In June 1943, she was dropped into France to join the Prosper network, the SOE's largest operation in Paris.

Within weeks, disaster struck.

The Prosper network collapsed. Mass arrests swept through the resistance. Safe houses were raided. Agents were captured. The entire Paris organization was decimated.

Noor's colleagues were in Gestapo custody or dead. Support networks vanished. The underground railroad that moved agents and equipment ceased to exist.

London sent word: Come home. You're the only operator left. It's too dangerous.

Noor refused.

If she left, London would have no radio contact with Paris—no way to coordinate resistance operations, no intelligence from the French capital, no link to what remained of the underground.

So she stayed. Alone. The only SOE wireless operator still transmitting from Paris.

Transmitting into Darkness

For months, Noor operated solo in one of the most surveilled cities in occupied Europe.

She moved constantly, never staying in one location long. She transmitted messages, received instructions, coordinated what remained of resistance activities—all while German direction-finding trucks prowled the streets, triangulating radio signals.

Every time she powered up her transmitter, she knew she was broadcasting her location to hunters who wanted her dead or captured.

She kept transmitting.

London repeatedly offered extraction. Each time, Noor refused. As long as she could send messages, the resistance had eyes and ears in Paris. People's lives depended on that communication.

She maintained this impossible situation for over three months—far longer than the six-week life expectancy for operators.

Then, in October 1943, she was betrayed.

The exact betrayal remains disputed—possibly a French woman seeking reward money, possibly infiltration of the network. Either way, the Gestapo came for her.

The Prisoner Who Wouldn't Break

Noor was arrested and interrogated at Gestapo headquarters on Avenue Foch in Paris.

She refused to cooperate. No codes. No names. No information.

Even in captivity, she attempted escape—trying to reach the roof with fellow prisoners. Recaptured, she was labeled "highly dangerous" and placed in chains.

The Gestapo had captured other agents who, under torture or threat, had broken. Some agreed to work for the Germans. Some provided information.

Noor gave them nothing.

She was transferred to Pforzheim prison in Germany, held in solitary confinement, shackled hand and foot. For ten months, she endured isolation designed to break her spirit.

It didn't work.

On September 12, 1944—as Allied forces were liberating France—Noor and three other female SOE agents were transported to Dachau concentration camp.

Early the next morning, September 13, 1944, they were executed by gunshot.

Witnesses later reported that Noor's final word was "Liberté"—Freedom.

She was 30 years old.

The Long Silence

After the war, Noor Inayat Khan's story wasn't widely told.

She didn't fit the expected narrative. She was a Muslim woman of Indian heritage serving Britain. She was gentle and idealistic, not the hardened spy of popular imagination. She wrote children's stories about animals and spirituality, not manifestos about resistance.

History preferred simpler stories. Male heroes. Clear narratives. Noor's complexity—her spirituality, her background, her choice to stay when leaving was possible—didn't fit neatly into post-war mythology.

In 1949, she was posthumously awarded the George Cross—Britain's highest civilian decoration for gallantry. France awarded her the Croix de Guerre.

But for decades, few knew her name.

Only gradually did recognition grow. Books were written. Memorials were erected. In 2012, a bronze bust of Noor was unveiled in London—the first memorial to a Muslim war heroine in the West, and the first to an Asian woman in the UK.

Schools, streets, and exhibitions now bear her name. Her story is taught to new generations.

But all the recognition came too late to change what happened in Dachau on September 13, 1944.

The Legacy

Noor Inayat Khan was not a soldier. She never carried a gun. She didn't lead troops or blow up bridges.

Her weapon was communication. Her battlefield was radio waves. Her courage was measured in transmissions sent when silence would have meant safety.

She understood something profound: in war, information is as powerful as ammunition. A radio operator connecting resistance networks, coordinating operations, transmitting intelligence—that person becomes as dangerous to the enemy as any commando.

That's why they hunted operators so relentlessly. That's why the life expectancy was six weeks. That's why Noor knew staying in Paris meant eventual capture.

She stayed anyway. Because communication meant coordination. Coordination meant lives saved. Her life for many lives—she made that calculation and accepted it.

What makes Noor's story remarkable isn't just her courage under fire. It's her courage in darkness, alone, for months, knowing no rescue was coming, knowing each transmission brought hunters closer, and choosing to keep transmitting anyway.

No glory. No recognition. No witnesses to her bravery except the Gestapo agents who tried to break her and failed.

She resisted not with violence but with silence—refusing to speak when speaking might save her life. She fought with stubbornness, with principle, with the conviction that some things mattered more than survival.

Her Sufi upbringing taught her about spiritual devotion and sacrifice. Her life demonstrated both.

Remembering Noor

Noor Inayat Khan challenges our assumptions about heroism.

Heroes don't all look the same. They aren't all soldiers. They aren't all men. They come from different faiths, different backgrounds, different paths.

Courage doesn't always roar. Sometimes it whispers into a radio transmitter night after night, sending messages into darkness while waiting for the inevitable knock on the door.

Bravery isn't always surviving. Sometimes it's choosing not to survive—accepting capture, refusing to break, dying rather than betray.

Noor proved that a children's author who wrote about Jataka tales could become one of WWII's most determined resistance fighters. That a Sufi Muslim woman could serve Britain with unwavering loyalty. That gentleness and strength aren't opposites—they can exist in the same person making impossible choices.

Her story waited decades to be fully told. But it was always there, transmitted across time like those radio signals she sent across occupied France.

Now we hear it. Now we remember.

A woman who could have stayed safe chose danger. Who could have left chose to stay. Who could have broken chose silence. Who could have collaborated chose death.

Noor Inayat Khan. Code name Madeleine. Britain's first Muslim war heroine. The radio operator who wouldn't stop transmitting. The prisoner who wouldn't break.

Her final word was freedom. Her legacy is courage that transcends time, faith, and borders.

Rest in peace, Noor. Your transmission was received. Your sacrifice remembered. Your courage honored. 🕊️

She fought an abuser with her fists, became a doctor to help the poor, went to prison for opposing war, and loved women openly when it could destroy her—they tried to silence her, so she got louder.
The Dalles, Oregon.
A young woman named Marie Equi did something that would change her life: she physically attacked her partner's abusive employer.
The incident was violent enough to make the local papers. The scandal could have destroyed her—a working-class woman of Italian and Irish immigrant descent, living openly with another woman in rural Oregon, assaulting a man of higher social standing.
The public attention should have ruined her.
Instead, Marie Equi looked at the wreckage of what could have been and made a decision:
She would become a doctor.
Born in 1872 in New Bedford, Massachusetts, Marie grew up in a world that told her exactly what she couldn't be: educated, independent, openly queer, politically radical.
She proceeded to become all of those things with a defiance that would define her entire life.
After defending Bessie Holcomb—her partner—from her employer's violence, Marie enrolled in medical school at the University of Oregon. In 1903, she graduated and became one of the few women physicians in the Pacific Northwest.
But Dr. Marie Equi wasn't interested in treating wealthy patients in comfortable parlors.
She opened a practice serving working-class and immigrant women, specializing in obstetrics and pediatrics—the people who couldn't afford most doctors, the people who had nowhere else to go.
And then she went further.
She became a vocal advocate for birth control and women's reproductive rights at a time when even discussing such topics publicly could land you in prison. Margaret Sanger was being arrested for the same advocacy across the country.
Marie Equi did it anyway.
She believed women deserved control over their own bodies, and she used her medical license to make that happen—legality be damned.
But medicine was never going to be enough for Marie Equi. She saw too much suffering, too much injustice that couldn't be fixed one patient at a time.
She threw herself into the labor movement, marching alongside striking workers, using her medical skills to treat injured protesters, speaking at rallies about workers' rights and fair wages. She aligned herself with socialists and anarchists—the most radical voices of her era—calling for fundamental changes to American society.
She was five feet tall and absolutely fearless.
When authorities tried to break up strikes, Marie was in the crowd. When workers were beaten by company thugs, Marie was there treating their wounds and documenting the violence. She made herself impossible to ignore.
And through it all, she lived openly with women—first Bessie Holcomb, then later Harriet Speckart—at a time when lesbian relationships were not just socially unacceptable but could result in forced institutionalization, loss of professional license, or outright violence.
Marie Equi didn't hide. She didn't apologize. She didn't perform heterosexuality for public consumption.
She lived her truth in full view of a society that despised it.
Then came World War I, and Marie Equi found her most dangerous cause yet.
While most of America rallied around the war effort with patriotic fervor, Marie spoke out against it with equal passion.
She called it imperialist butchery. A rich man's war that would kill poor men's sons. She organized anti-war protests, gave fiery speeches condemning U.S. involvement, and refused to be silenced even as the government passed the Espionage Act specifically to criminalize the kind of dissent she was spreading.
In 1918, federal agents arrested her.
She was convicted under the Espionage Act for her anti-war activism and sentenced to prison. In 1920, Dr. Marie Equi—a respected physician who had spent her career healing the poor—entered San Quentin, one of the few women imprisoned under this law, held in a facility designed for violent male criminals.
But here's where Marie Equi's story becomes almost impossibly contradictory:
While she was being prosecuted by the U.S. government as a dangerous radical and criminal threat to national security, her medical skills were so widely respected that she had served in humanitarian capacities during public health crises, her expertise valued even by those who despised her politics.
This was a woman simultaneously considered a traitor and a healer whose services were desperately needed.
After serving a year in San Quentin, Marie was released in 1921, her health damaged by the harsh conditions but her spirit fundamentally unbroken.
She returned to Portland and continued practicing medicine, though her public activism quieted somewhat in her later years—whether from exhaustion, strategic retreat, or simply the natural slowing of age.
But she never apologized. Never recanted. Never pretended to be anything other than what she was:
A radical. A lesbian. A doctor who believed healthcare was a human right. A woman who thought war was murder. A person who refused to live quietly while injustice flourished around her.
Marie Equi continued practicing medicine into her seventies, serving the poor and marginalized communities she'd dedicated her life to helping.
She lived to see some of the causes she fought for gain ground—women's suffrage achieved in 1920, labor rights gradually expanded, though never as far as she wanted.
She lived to see other causes remain frustratingly, painfully distant—LGBTQ+ rights wouldn't begin to advance significantly for decades after her death.
When she died in 1952 at age eighty, she left behind a legacy that challenges easy categorization.
She was a healer who fought with her fists.
A doctor who went to prison.
A patriot who opposed her country's wars.
A woman who loved women when it could cost her everything.
For decades after her death, Marie Equi was largely forgotten—too radical for mainstream history books, too complicated for simple heroic narratives, too queer for a society that wanted to erase LGBTQ+ people from the historical record.
But recent years have seen renewed interest in her extraordinary life.
LGBTQ+ historians have reclaimed her as an early queer pioneer who lived authentically when it was profoundly dangerous to do so.
Feminist historians celebrate her advocacy for reproductive rights decades before Roe v. Wade.
Medical historians recognize her commitment to serving marginalized communities when most doctors sought wealthy patients.
Labor historians honor her solidarity with workers fighting for basic dignity.
Marie Equi's life reminds us that progress doesn't come from people who play it safe.
It comes from people willing to lose everything for what they believe in—their freedom, their reputation, their comfort, their safety.
She was imprisoned for her beliefs. She was ostracized for her identity. She was attacked for her advocacy.
And she never stopped. Never quieted. Never compromised who she was or what she believed.
In an era that demanded women be demure, Marie Equi was defiant.
In a profession that served the wealthy, she served the poor.
In a society that insisted on heterosexuality, she loved women openly and without shame.
In a time of war fever and blind patriotism, she preached peace and questioned authority.
They tried to silence her with prison. She came out and kept talking.
They tried to shame her for her sexuality. She lived her truth even louder.
They tried to discredit her radicalism. She radicalized more people.
Marie Equi's message was simple but revolutionary:
Fight for what's right. Live as you truly are. And never, ever apologize for refusing to accept injustice.
She fought with everything she had—her fists when necessary, her medical skills when possible, her voice always.
And now, decades after being forgotten, history finally remembers.
Dr. Marie Equi (1872-1952):
The five-foot-tall doctor who took on the U.S. government and never backed down.
Who defended her lover with violence, then spent her life healing.
Who went to prison for peace.
Who loved women in an era that criminalized it.
Who served the poor when she could have gotten rich.
Who got loud when they tried to silence her.
They wanted her quiet, compliant, invisible.
She gave them defiance instead.
And that makes all the difference.

Counter-terror drill, echoes of gunfire at the border: Fears of active militants in Jammu under the shadow of US-Pakistan joint exercise

Special Correspondent | Jammu | January 12, 2026

On one hand, there is a message of counter-terror cooperation on the international stage. On the other, there are renewed fears of infiltration and militant activity along India’s borders. It is against this backdrop of contradiction that the United States and Pakistan have begun a joint counter-terrorism exercise in Pakistan’s Punjab province, titled “Inspired Gambit 2026”. At the same time, Indian security forces have intensified counter-infiltration and anti-terror operations along the Line of Control and the International Border in Jammu and Kashmir.

According to defence sources, around 35 Pakistani militants are currently active in the Jammu region alone. This figure is not merely a statistic. It is linked to growing concerns that attempts are underway to revive militancy south of the Pir Panjal range. Security agencies believe that an area which had remained relatively calm for a long period is now being deliberately destabilised once again.

This has raised serious questions about the credibility of Pakistan’s claim of being a counter-terror partner on the international stage. Simultaneously, reports have emerged of drone activity from across the border, attempts at infiltration, and the presence of militants lying low in forward areas.

The joint exercise is being held at Pakistan’s National Counter Terrorism Centre and focuses primarily on urban counter-terror tactics, close-quarters battle, and operational coordination between the two armies. Teams from the US and Pakistani forces are conducting drills under various simulated scenarios. Pakistan maintains that the objective of the exercise is to enhance capabilities against global terrorism and to facilitate the exchange of operational experience.

Indian security analysts, however, argue that the ground reality tells a different story. They point out that if Pakistan were genuinely committed to eliminating terrorism, the presence of such a large number of militants along the Jammu and Kashmir border would be difficult to explain. Some experts believe Pakistan is projecting two contrasting narratives at the same time. On one side, it is strengthening military cooperation with Washington. On the other, it has failed to dismantle the infrastructure of proxy warfare directed against India.

At present, the Indian Army, the Border Security Force, and the Jammu and Kashmir Police are jointly conducting multiple search operations across the Jammu region. Surveillance has been stepped up in forested and mountainous terrain as well as in villages close to the border. Additional troop deployments have been made, and technological monitoring has also been significantly reinforced.

Political observers note that the situation is not only militarily sensitive but also diplomatically significant. India has long highlighted Pakistan’s duplicity on terrorism in international forums. If credible information about militant activity in Jammu emerges during the period of the US–Pakistan joint exercise, it further strengthens New Delhi’s position.

For now, the reality along the border remains tense rather than calm. On one side are counter-terror drills and official assurances. On the other are fears of infiltration and renewed violence. Standing between these two contrasting images is Jammu and Kashmir, prompting a fundamental question within the security establishment: is the fight against terrorism truly shared, or is it merely a language of international diplomacy.

Royal Commissions Must Be Above Suspicion — Process Matters
By Michael Kennedy

Royal Commissions do not exist merely to uncover facts. They exist to restore public confidence when trust has been shaken. That is why perception matters almost as much as integrity itself.

The appointment of former High Court Justice Virginia Bell AC to lead the Royal Commission into the Bondi terror attack and the broader issue of antisemitism has prompted legitimate public debate. Not because of any allegation of bias or impropriety — there is none — but because of relationships, optics, and process.

Let’s be clear at the outset: Virginia Bell is a distinguished jurist. She served on the High Court of Australia from 2009 to 2021, was previously a judge of the NSW Supreme Court, and has been entrusted with sensitive inquiries before, including the investigation into former Prime Minister Scott Morrison’s secret ministerial appointments. Her legal credentials are not in dispute.

However, Royal Commissions are not ordinary inquiries. They operate in politically charged environments, often intersecting with national security, social cohesion, and government accountability. In such circumstances, confidence in independence must be unquestionable.

Ms Bell was appointed to the High Court by a Labor government under Kevin Rudd in 2009. She was formally recognised under another Labor government in 2012 for her service to the law and public policy. She has now been appointed by the Albanese government to lead one of the most sensitive Royal Commissions in recent years.

None of this establishes bias. Appointment by governments of the day is standard constitutional practice. But it does establish proximity, and proximity creates perception — especially when the appointing government is itself a stakeholder in the outcomes, policy responses, and narrative framing of the inquiry.

That perception risk is heightened by the Prime Minister’s public insistence that Ms Bell is “the most qualified person” for the role. This claim is unnecessary and unconvincing. Australia has no shortage of eminent, independent, and nationally respected figures capable of leading such an inquiry.

Among those widely regarded as equally qualified are:

Robert French, former Chief Justice of the High Court

James Allsop, former Chief Justice of the Federal Court

Dennis Richardson and Duncan Lewis, former national security chiefs with deep counterterrorism expertise

Justice Michael Lee, a Federal Court judge respected across communities, including within parts of the Jewish community

The existence of multiple credible candidates does not diminish Ms Bell — but it does raise an important question: why was there no transparent or consultative selection process?

In other Westminster democracies, appointments to inquiries of this sensitivity often involve parliamentary consultation or confirmation mechanisms. In Australia, the executive alone decides. That may be lawful, but it is no longer sufficient in an era of declining trust.

A Senate-based or bipartisan selection process would not weaken Royal Commissions — it would strengthen them. It would shield commissioners from politicised attacks, reassure affected communities, and protect findings from claims of narrative management or institutional self-interest.

Some critics have mocked concerns about perception as “politicisation.” In fact, the opposite is true. Ignoring perception is what politicises an inquiry. Transparency disarms suspicion; secrecy feeds it.

This debate is not about Virginia Bell’s integrity. It is about process integrity.

If Royal Commissions are to retain their authority in a divided and sceptical society, governments must accept a simple principle: being independent is not enough — independence must be seen to be beyond question.

That is not an attack on the commissioner. It is a call to modernise how Australia appoints those entrusted with its most serious national inquiries.

A late post — and honestly, that feels right.

I am grateful that I completed the Multicultural Peace Learning Hub and the IEP Ambassador Program with the Institute for Economics & Peace in December. 

I didn’t rush to share because I wasn’t done learning when the program ended.

From a Ugandan perspective, this experience made me uncomfortable in a good way. We often say we are peaceful — and in some ways we are. 

But peace isn’t just about the absence of conflict. It shows up in everyday moments:
📌
when a young person can’t access a job despite having skills,
when a community struggles to be heard,
or when justice feels slow or out of reach.

That’s when you realize that stability alone isn’t enough. Positive peace lives in systems, opportunities, and trust — not just calm streets.

What stayed with me most is this: 
learning doesn’t stop at certificates, and peace doesn’t stop at silence. Both require honesty, reflection, and consistent work, especially from those of us working around policy, youth, and community spaces.

I’m open to conversations and collaborations with people doing grounded work in peacebuilding, policy, and youth engagement — not for applause, but for progress.

Still learning. Still questioning. Still showing up. 🌱🕊️

Tahadhari! Wizi wa Taarifa za Instagram, Jilinde Usibofye Link Usiyoijua

Mapema Januari 2026, kumetokea jambo kubwa kwenye Instagram! Idadi kubwa ya watu  wanasema kuwa taarifa za watumiaji zaidi ya milioni 17.5 zimevujishwa. Ambapo data hizi zinajumuisha majina ya watumiaji (usernames), namba za simu, barua pepe, hata anwani za nyumbani kwa baadhi yao. Habari hizi zimeanza kuuzwa au tolewa bure kwenye mitandao ya giza (dark web) tangu tarehe 7 Januari 2026.

Baada ya data hizo kuvujika, wavamizi wameanza kufanya vitendo vya ujanja. Wengi wenu mmeshapokea barua pepe nyingi sana kutoka Instagram zinazokuambia "Reset password yako sasa!" au "Mtu anajaribu kuingia kwenye akaunti yako!" Hizo barua pepe zinaweza kuwa za kweli (Instagram wenyewe wanakubali kuwa kuna tatizo lililosababisha reset nyingi), lakini wengi wao ni mtego wa wizi!

Wavamizi wanatumia taarifa zako ili kuomba reset ya password yako mara kwa mara. Kama mkiwa mna bahati mbaya na mkibonyeza link iliyomo kwenye barua pepe hiyo, wanaweza kuiba akaunti yenu kabisa.

Instagram (Meta) wamesema "Hakuna uvamizi wa mfumo wetu. Akaunti zenu ziko salama. Tatizo lilikuwa la nje tu, tumelishughulikia. Barua pepe hizo za reset msizifanyie kitu – zipuuze tu. Samahani kwa usumbufu."

Lakini wataalamu wa usalama wa mtandao wanasema:  
Hata kama hakuna "breach" ya moja kwa moja kwenye Instagram, data hii iliyovujika inaweza kuwafanya wavamizi kuwashambulia watu kwa urahisi zaidi. Wanaweza kutuma barua pepe za uongo zinazoiga za Instagram, au hata kujaribu kudanganya ili wapate password yenu.

Ushauri wa haraka kwa Watanzania wote wanaotumia Instagram:

- Weka two-factor authentication (2FA) mara moja – tumia app (kama Google Authenticator) badala ya SMS.
- Usibonyeze link yoyote kwenye barua pepe ya "reset password" isipokuwa ukiingia Instagram moja kwa moja kupitia app au www.instagram.com.
- Badilisha password yako iwe ngumu(mchanganyiko wa herufi kubwa, ndogo, namba na alama).
- Kama umepokea barua nyingi za reset bila kutarajia – angalia akaunti yako mara moja, angalia "Login Activity" na "Connected Devices" kwenye settings.

My Message of Solidarity and Best Wishes to Bobi Wine as Uganda Approaches Elections

Dear Bobi WineWine(Kyagulanyi),

As Uganda stands on the threshold of a historic moment, I extend my heartfelt wishes of courage, strength, and unwavering hope to you ,an icon of resistance and a true voice of the people. With just two days remaining before the general election, the eyes of Africa and the world are watching, hopeful for a peaceful and democratic transition in Uganda.

@BobiWine , your courage throughout this journey has inspired millions not just in Uganda, but across the continent. You chose to speak truth to power, to stand for justice, for the youth, for the marginalized, and for the dream of a better, freer Uganda. Even in the face of brutality, you have remained resilient.

We remember vividly the violence, harassment, arrests, and intimidation that you and your supporters have endured under the authoritarian regime of Yoweri Museveni and his son. Your movement has been met with tear gas, bullets, media blackouts, and censorship. Yet, the spirit of freedom has refused to be silenced. The pain and oppression suffered during the campaign season are evidence of a leadership that fears the voice of its own people.

As the country prepares to vote, we stand with you in solidarity. We pray for safety for you, your family, your team, and every Ugandan who dares to vote for change. We echo the voices calling for an end to military rule, for dignity, and for the right of the people to decide their future.

May justice prevail. May peace win. May the ballot be stronger than the bullet. And may the spirit of a free Uganda rise above all intimidation.

Best wishes, @BobiWine. Africa stands with you.
In solidarity and hope. 
Joel K Meitaya

Statement on Insecurity, Boundary Disputes, and Encroachment in Tana River County
The Somali communities living in parts of North Eastern Kenya, particularly within Garissa County, have for years subjected riverine communities in Tana River County to persistent insecurity and hostility. These tensions arise mainly from an ongoing boundary dispute, where claims are made that the River Tana itself is the boundary, in total disregard of the three-mile provision as established in the 1992 constitutional and administrative framework.
As a result, indigenous riverine communities—including the Pokomo, Wailwana, Munyoyaya, and Watta—have been systematically demonized, intimidated, and exposed to a hostile living environment. Historical injustices dating back to the Shifta era, alongside more recent killings and displacements, point to a deliberate and sustained pattern aimed at weakening and ultimately relocating these communities from their ancestral lands.
Of grave concern is the continued encroachment into Tana River County community land, marked by the construction of public institutions and settlements without lawful boundary resolution. These include:
Schools and government offices built in Diram and Furaha villages (Chewele Ward)
The construction and subsequent claim over Bura East
Establishment of Hajj Girls School in Kinakomba Ward
A school built near Majengo village, adjacent to Boji Farmers Minor Irrigation Scheme
Encroachment into Baratiro area in Ndera Location, among others
These actions not only violate land rights but also escalate tensions and undermine peaceful coexistence.
We therefore call upon the Government of Kenya, through the Ministry of Interior, the Ministry of Lands, the National Cohesion and Integration Commission (NCIC), and all relevant constitutional bodies, to intervene decisively and conclusively. There is an urgent need to:
Enforce legally established county boundaries
Halt further encroachment on Tana River County land
Protect vulnerable riverine communities
Address historical injustices and insecurity
Restore trust and peaceful coexistence among neighboring communities
Peace cannot be achieved through intimidation, forced displacement, or historical denial. Justice, rule of law, and mutual respect must prevail.

Kutokea moja kwa moja Mjini Tehran, mamlaka za ulinzi nchini Iran zimethibitisha kukamatwa kwa kundi kubwa la watu wanaotuhumiwa kuhusika na vurugu zilizotikisa taifa hilo usiku wa kuamkia leo.

Kwa mujibu wa taarifa rasmi kutoka vyombo vya usalama, watu waliokamatwa si raia wa Iran, bali ni raia wa India na Afghanistan, waliokuwa wakihusika na uchomaji wa Misikiti na majengo ya serikali kwa kutumia mabomu ya petrol.

Taarifa hizo zinaeleza kuwa, baada ya mahojiano ya kina, wahusika hao walikiri kuwa wametumwa na Shirika la Kijasusi la Israel (Mossad) kwa nia ya kuchochea machafuko nchini humo.

Mamlaka za ulinzi zimelieleza tukio hili kama jaribio la wazi la kuharibu amani ya Iran kupitia vibaraka wa mataifa ya kigeni. Uchunguzi zaidi unaendelea huku taifa likiimarisha ulinzi wake mipakani na maeneo nyeti.

Mamlaka zinasisitiza: "Hatutaruhusu Waasi wa nje kuja na kuharibu misingi ya amani na utulivu wetu. Wale wote waliohusika watafikishwa mbele ya sheria.”

☢️ Enhancing Central Asia’s capacity to counter radiological and nuclear (RN) terrorism

⚙️ Strengthening preparedness against RN threats requires expertise and cooperation across borders.

🇺🇳 UNICRI and the United Nations Office of Counter-Terrorism (UNOCT), convened a regional tabletop exercise in Tashkent, bringing together national authorities from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.

The three-day, scenario-based exercise strengthened regional cooperation to counter the trafficking and potential terrorist use of RN materials, in line with the International Convention for the Suppression of Acts of Nuclear Terrorism.

 🔎 Key highlights
🔹 Cross-border, scenario-based simulation testing responses to a complex radiological incident
🔹 Enhanced interagency coordination among security services, law enforcement, nuclear regulators and prosecutors
🔹 Practical application of international legal frameworks to counter nuclear terrorism
🔹 Strengthened information-sharing and intelligence exchange mechanisms at regional level
🔹 Expert contributions from the EU CBRN Risk Mitigation Centres of Excellence, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) 
and the EU Science Hub - Joint Research Centre of the European Commission.

🔖 The exercise was conducted within the framework of CONTACT – Central Asia, implemented by UNICRI, and the EU–UN joint project supporting the universalization and implementation of ICSANT, jointly implemented by UNOCT and UNODC - United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime.

🧭 Together, these efforts demonstrate how regional and international partnerships and targeted training can significantly enhance collective preparedness and resilience against RN terrorism threats.

To make a delicious omelette, you need simple ingredients and follow a few easy steps. Here is a step by step guide on how to make an egg omelette: Ingredients Required:2 or 3 large eggs,1 tablespoon water or milk , Salt and pepper to taste,1 tablespoon butter or cooking oil , Optional fillings (grated cheese, chopped ham, sliced ​​mushrooms, diced peppers, chopped onions, spinach, etc.)Tools: small bowl , Wire fork or whisk , Non-stick frying pan (about 8 inches in diameter for 2-3 eggs) , Spatula . Instruction: Prepare the Filling (Optional): If you're using a filling that requires cooking time (such as mushrooms or raw onions), cook it first in a separate skillet or in your omelet pan before proceeding to the next step. Set aside. Beat the Eggs: Crack the eggs into a small bowl. Add water or milk, salt, and pepper. Beat with a fork or wire whisk until the egg whites and yolks are well combined and no white streaks are visible. Do not overbeat until foamy. Heat the Pan: Melt the butter or heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Make sure the entire surface of the pan is coated with the butter/oil. Cook the Eggs: Pour the egg mixture into the hot pan. The eggs will begin to cook quickly around the edges. Shape the Omelette: While the eggs are cooking, use a spatula to push the cooked parts of the egg at the edges of the pan toward the center. Tilt the pan so that the uncooked parts of the egg flow into the empty spaces on the hot surface. Repeat this process several times until the top of the egg is mostly solid but still slightly wet or shiny in the center. Add Filling and Cheese: Sprinkle the filling you have prepared and grated cheese on one side of the omelette (half). Fold the Omelet: Using a spatula, fold the omelette in half (into a semicircle) over the filling. Serve: Let the omelet sit in the pan for about another minute to allow the filling to warm and the cheese to melt. Then, carefully slide the omelet from the pan onto a serving plate. To make a delicious omelette, you need simple ingredients and follow a few easy steps. Here is a step by step guide on how to make an egg omelette: Ingredients Required:2 or 3 large eggs,1 tablespoon water or milk , Salt and pepper to taste,1 tablespoon butter or cooking oil , Optional fillings (grated cheese, chopped ham, sliced ​​mushrooms, diced peppers, chopped onions, spinach, etc.)Tools: small bowl , Wire fork or whisk , Non-stick frying pan (about 8 inches in diameter for 2-3 eggs) , Spatula . Instruction: Prepare the Filling (Optional): If you're using a filling that requires cooking time (such as mushrooms or raw onions), cook it first in a separate skillet or in your omelet pan before proceeding to the next step. Set aside. Beat the Eggs: Crack the eggs into a small bowl. Add water or milk, salt, and pepper. Beat with a fork or wire whisk until the egg whites and yolks are well combined and no white streaks are visible. Do not overbeat until foamy. Heat the Pan: Melt the butter or heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Make sure the entire surface of the pan is coated with the butter/oil. Cook the Eggs: Pour the egg mixture into the hot pan. The eggs will begin to cook quickly around the edges. Shape the Omelette: While the eggs are cooking, use a spatula to push the cooked parts of the egg at the edges of the pan toward the center. Tilt the pan so that the uncooked parts of the egg flow into the empty spaces on the hot surface. Repeat this process several times until the top of the egg is mostly solid but still slightly wet or shiny in the center. Add Filling and Cheese: Sprinkle the filling you have prepared and grated cheese on one side of the omelette (half). Fold the Omelet: Using a spatula, fold the omelette in half (into a semicircle) over the filling. Serve: Let the omelet sit in the pan for about another minute to allow the filling to warm and the cheese to melt. Then, carefully slide the omelet from the pan onto a serving plate. To make a delicious omelette, you need simple ingredients and follow a few easy steps. Here is a step by step guide on how to make an egg omelette: Ingredients Required:2 or 3 large eggs,1 tablespoon water or milk , Salt and pepper to taste,1 tablespoon butter or cooking oil , Optional fillings (grated cheese, chopped ham, sliced ​​mushrooms, diced peppers, chopped onions, spinach, etc.)Tools: small bowl , Wire fork or whisk , Non-stick frying pan (about 8 inches in diameter for 2-3 eggs) , Spatula . Instruction: Prepare the Filling (Optional): If you're using a filling that requires cooking time (such as mushrooms or raw onions), cook it first in a separate skillet or in your omelet pan before proceeding to the next step. Set aside. Beat the Eggs: Crack the eggs into a small bowl. Add water or milk, salt, and pepper. Beat with a fork or wire whisk until the egg whites and yolks are well combined and no white streaks are visible. Do not overbeat until foamy. Heat the Pan: Melt the butter or heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Make sure the entire surface of the pan is coated with the butter/oil. Cook the Eggs: Pour the egg mixture into the hot pan. The eggs will begin to cook quickly around the edges. Shape the Omelette: While the eggs are cooking, use a spatula to push the cooked parts of the egg at the edges of the pan toward the center. Tilt the pan so that the uncooked parts of the egg flow into the empty spaces on the hot surface. Repeat this process several times until the top of the egg is mostly solid but still slightly wet or shiny in the center. Add Filling and Cheese: Sprinkle the filling you have prepared and grated cheese on one side of the omelette (half). Fold the Omelet: Using a spatula, fold the omelette in half (into a semicircle) over the filling. Serve: Let the omelet sit in the pan for about another minute to allow the filling to warm and the cheese to melt. Then, carefully slide the omelet from the pan onto a serving plate. To make a delicious omelette, you need simple ingredients and follow a few easy steps. Here is a step by step guide on how to make an egg omelette: Ingredients Required:2 or 3 large eggs,1 tablespoon water or milk , Salt and pepper to taste,1 tablespoon butter or cooking oil , Optional fillings (grated cheese, chopped ham, sliced ​​mushrooms, diced peppers, chopped onions, spinach, etc.)Tools: small bowl , Wire fork or whisk , Non-stick frying pan (about 8 inches in diameter for 2-3 eggs) , Spatula . Instruction: Prepare the Filling (Optional): If you're using a filling that requires cooking time (such as mushrooms or raw onions), cook it first in a separate skillet or in your omelet pan before proceeding to the next step. Set aside. Beat the Eggs: Crack the eggs into a small bowl. Add water or milk, salt, and pepper. Beat with a fork or wire whisk until the egg whites and yolks are well combined and no white streaks are visible. Do not overbeat until foamy. Heat the Pan: Melt the butter or heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Make sure the entire surface of the pan is coated with the butter/oil. Cook the Eggs: Pour the egg mixture into the hot pan. The eggs will begin to cook quickly around the edges. Shape the Omelette: While the eggs are cooking, use a spatula to push the cooked parts of the egg at the edges of the pan toward the center. Tilt the pan so that the uncooked parts of the egg flow into the empty spaces on the hot surface. Repeat this process several times until the top of the egg is mostly solid but still slightly wet or shiny in the center. Add Filling and Cheese: Sprinkle the filling you have prepared and grated cheese on one side of the omelette (half). Fold the Omelet: Using a spatula, fold the omelette in half (into a semicircle) over the filling. Serve: Let the omelet sit in the pan for about another minute to allow the filling to warm and the cheese to melt. Then, carefully slide the omelet from the pan onto a serving plate. Steps to Make Crispy Chicken
Making crispy chicken with a lasting crispiness isn't difficult. Here are the steps: Optimally marinate the chicken by soaking it in the marinade. A well-seasoned marinade will give the chicken a more savory flavor while still retaining its juiciness after frying. Double-coat the breading. Many crispy chicken recipes overlook this step. However, double-coating the breading helps the breading adhere better and crispier. Pay attention to the temperature and time when frying, use the deep frying technique and fry the chicken for 10-15 minutes so that it cooks evenly. Use double frying for extra crispiness. This is done by re-frying the chicken after it has rested for a few minutes. This ensures the chicken retains its crispiness for longer. Tips to Keep Crispy Chicken Crispy . There are other tips you can use to keep your chicken crispy and crunchy. Starting with paying attention to your draining technique, try draining the chicken on a wire rack to allow air to circulate around all sides. This method also allows excess oil to drain into the pan while still maintaining the crispy skin. After draining the chicken, store it in an open container or line it with paper towels. Store it at room temperature, or let it cool if you want to store it in the refrigerator. To reheat it, use the reheating method in the oven or air fryer, or you can also fry it in a non-stick pan over low heat. Troubleshooting Crispy Chicken Problems . The correct technique for frying crispy chicken can be the solution to a lack of crispiness. Often, fried chicken isn't crispy because the oil is too hot or too cold. Ensure the oil is at the correct temperature and avoid frying too much chicken in one pan. Similarly, if the problem is that crispy chicken becomes mushy when fried, careful attention must be paid to the marinating and draining techniques to ensure the skin doesn't become soggy or mushy after frying. However, if the problem is the flour not sticking, double-coating can be solved for a crispier coating. Crispy Chicken Seasoning Variations. Original Crispy Chicken . This is a chicken marinade with a naturally savory flavor. It often uses a marinade of garlic, pepper, and salt, giving it a delicious flavor. This type of crispy chicken can be served as a simple side dish with chili sauce or mayonnaise. Spicy Crispy Chicken . This crispy chicken recipe uses chili powder as an additional coating for the flour. Other popular variations of spicy crispy chicken include coating it with chili sauce, hot sauce, balado sauce, and many more, depending on your preference. Crispy BBQ Chicken . This type of crispy chicken has a sweet, savory, and smoky flavor combination typical of BBQ sauce. The fried crispy chicken is coated in a BBQ sauce made from tomato sauce, sweet soy sauce, honey, and a touch of vinegar. This crispy chicken variation is typically served with French fries and salad. Crispy Cheese Chicken
It's crispy chicken with cheese sauce as a topping. It's savory and creamy, making it perfect as a snack. Steps to Make Crispy Chicken
Making crispy chicken with a lasting crispiness isn't difficult. Here are the steps: Optimally marinate the chicken by soaking it in the marinade. A well-seasoned marinade will give the chicken a more savory flavor while still retaining its juiciness after frying. Double-coat the breading. Many crispy chicken recipes overlook this step. However, double-coating the breading helps the breading adhere better and crispier. Pay attention to the temperature and time when frying, use the deep frying technique and fry the chicken for 10-15 minutes so that it cooks evenly. Use double frying for extra crispiness. This is done by re-frying the chicken after it has rested for a few minutes. This ensures the chicken retains its crispiness for longer. Tips to Keep Crispy Chicken Crispy . There are other tips you can use to keep your chicken crispy and crunchy. Starting with paying attention to your draining technique, try draining the chicken on a wire rack to allow air to circulate around all sides. This method also allows excess oil to drain into the pan while still maintaining the crispy skin. After draining the chicken, store it in an open container or line it with paper towels. Store it at room temperature, or let it cool if you want to store it in the refrigerator. To reheat it, use the reheating method in the oven or air fryer, or you can also fry it in a non-stick pan over low heat. Troubleshooting Crispy Chicken Problems . The correct technique for frying crispy chicken can be the solution to a lack of crispiness. Often, fried chicken isn't crispy because the oil is too hot or too cold. Ensure the oil is at the correct temperature and avoid frying too much chicken in one pan. Similarly, if the problem is that crispy chicken becomes mushy when fried, careful attention must be paid to the marinating and draining techniques to ensure the skin doesn't become soggy or mushy after frying. However, if the problem is the flour not sticking, double-coating can be solved for a crispier coating. Crispy Chicken Seasoning Variations. Original Crispy Chicken . This is a chicken marinade with a naturally savory flavor. It often uses a marinade of garlic, pepper, and salt, giving it a delicious flavor. This type of crispy chicken can be served as a simple side dish with chili sauce or mayonnaise. Spicy Crispy Chicken . This crispy chicken recipe uses chili powder as an additional coating for the flour. Other popular variations of spicy crispy chicken include coating it with chili sauce, hot sauce, balado sauce, and many more, depending on your preference. Crispy BBQ Chicken . This type of crispy chicken has a sweet, savory, and smoky flavor combination typical of BBQ sauce. The fried crispy chicken is coated in a BBQ sauce made from tomato sauce, sweet soy sauce, honey, and a touch of vinegar. This crispy chicken variation is typically served with French fries and salad. Crispy Cheese Chicken
It's crispy chicken with cheese sauce as a topping. It's savory and creamy, making it perfect as a snack. Steps to Make Crispy Chicken
Making crispy chicken with a lasting crispiness isn't difficult. Here are the steps: Optimally marinate the chicken by soaking it in the marinade. A well-seasoned marinade will give the chicken a more savory flavor while still retaining its juiciness after frying. Double-coat the breading. Many crispy chicken recipes overlook this step. However, double-coating the breading helps the breading adhere better and crispier. Pay attention to the temperature and time when frying, use the deep frying technique and fry the chicken for 10-15 minutes so that it cooks evenly. Use double frying for extra crispiness. This is done by re-frying the chicken after it has rested for a few minutes. This ensures the chicken retains its crispiness for longer. Tips to Keep Crispy Chicken Crispy . There are other tips you can use to keep your chicken crispy and crunchy. Starting with paying attention to your draining technique, try draining the chicken on a wire rack to allow air to circulate around all sides. This method also allows excess oil to drain into the pan while still maintaining the crispy skin. After draining the chicken, store it in an open container or line it with paper towels. Store it at room temperature, or let it cool if you want to store it in the refrigerator. To reheat it, use the reheating method in the oven or air fryer, or you can also fry it in a non-stick pan over low heat. Troubleshooting Crispy Chicken Problems . The correct technique for frying crispy chicken can be the solution to a lack of crispiness. Often, fried chicken isn't crispy because the oil is too hot or too cold. Ensure the oil is at the correct temperature and avoid frying too much chicken in one pan. Similarly, if the problem is that crispy chicken becomes mushy when fried, careful attention must be paid to the marinating and draining techniques to ensure the skin doesn't become soggy or mushy after frying. However, if the problem is the flour not sticking, double-coating can be solved for a crispier coating. Crispy Chicken Seasoning Variations. Original Crispy Chicken . This is a chicken marinade with a naturally savory flavor. It often uses a marinade of garlic, pepper, and salt, giving it a delicious flavor. This type of crispy chicken can be served as a simple side dish with chili sauce or mayonnaise. Spicy Crispy Chicken . This crispy chicken recipe uses chili powder as an additional coating for the flour. Other popular variations of spicy crispy chicken include coating it with chili sauce, hot sauce, balado sauce, and many more, depending on your preference. Crispy BBQ Chicken . This type of crispy chicken has a sweet, savory, and smoky flavor combination typical of BBQ sauce. The fried crispy chicken is coated in a BBQ sauce made from tomato sauce, sweet soy sauce, honey, and a touch of vinegar. This crispy chicken variation is typically served with French fries and salad. Crispy Cheese Chicken

I am back at my desk, in my pod, for the first time in over three weeks. And I am feeling good about it. 

A week ago I was so not ready. Like many, when I finally downed tools back in December, I was pretty burnt out. That last week or two, I was working 12 hour days. A combination of several bigger projects all winding up before the break, family needs and the fallout from the shit-show that was the Girlguiding and Women’s Institute decisions all piled up. I started to drop balls and was running on empty.

It’s been a glorious break. I was very aware, a week ago, as my feed started filling up with everyone else’s ‘back at it’ posts, I was not ready. But seeing all those posts - witnessing your energy, enthusiasm, plans for products, launches, growth and adventures - was actually incredibly helpful. It made me realise that this year, I am not going to do any of that. 

This year I do not intend to grow my business. 

I have zero plans to launch new, shiny things. 

I am not planning to add a zero to my revenue or break into any new marketplaces. 

This year I am going to do the things I already do. I am going to do them well. I am going to share about them, be excited about them. Invite you to work with me in them if they feel right for you. I’m not going to stop selling or delivering. 

But I am going to stop trying to be or do more. 

It’s such a simple decision, that feels so easy, but it’s taken four years of hustle for me to realise that what I am right now is enough. 

Now, if you have time for a big read, the back story is here...

In 2017 my annual income was a smidge UNDER £5k. Yup. I didn’t really have a business, I had a hobby masquerading as a business.

I was a single parent, working part-time, on benefits, not yet delivering online or using social media professionally. 

That all changed in 2018. I received some excellent support and mentorship (shout outs to Dan Meredith and Helen Tudor), figured out how real, meaningful visibility could change everything, and Ruth started to help out behind the scenes. She then became a co-director in 2019 making us equal partners in business and in life, and then, between 2018 and 2021, our business pretty much tripled its revenue year on year.

In 2022 we found our fantasy forever home and amazingly, our accounts stacked up in just the right way at just the right time (helped in no small way by the genius that is Laura Powner) to get a mortgage on it. 

We went from renting a boxy, 4 bed terrace with a tiny garden to owning what is now a 6 bed, 3 bath home, with a couple of acres of gardens and woods, outbuildings, incredible views, an energy that has to be experienced to be believed, backing right onto the Montgomery canal and with bags of as-yet untapped potential.

From two single parents on benefits to building a business that facilitated all our dreams coming true. 

In four years. 

It was pretty epic. 

But here is what’s happened since. 

The businesses have evolved. A couple of side quests have closed down and a new one has begun, but despite all the changes, all the big ideas, all the successes, overall, our financial picture has changed very little. Our annual revenue has been in the low 6 figures every year since 2022. 

And I’ve always been disappointed in that. 

Because it’s always felt like there’s been the potential for so much more. I’ve seen other people doing more. On paper, it’s seemed like more was entirely feasible, but it never quite happened.

There is more we want to do to the house and land - some of which could be income-generating. There is more we’d love to do as a family. Having more of a financial buffer than we do would be nice. 

For the last four years I have hustled, hard, to make these things happen. I have, every year, had a goal of growing the businesses more. And although they have evolved, they haven’t grown much. I have worked 12 hour days, missed family dinners and school assemblies, and still we hover at the same approximate level. And I’ve been disappointed. 

And this is why having this extended break has been so helpful to me. It has given me space to reflect more.

Because I may not have generated more revenue in the last four years but there have been many successes.

🔥 We have successfully parented four amazing neurodivergent kids. We have ridden every bump in the road, every assessment, review, SENCO meeting, accommodation and meltdown. They have gone from being 7, 9, 11 and 14 to 11, 13, almost 15 and 18 and they are bloody brilliant young people.

🔥 I have had top surgery. I also spent 18 months severely limited by a worsening heart condition before having (successful) heart surgery. I have recovered from both these things. 

🔥 We have funded and managed two significant home renovations as well as having part of the garden landscaped to house the lovely Hully pod from which I am currently writing this post. 

🔥 I’ve spoken on loads of stages, been nominated for multiple awards and grown a wonderful, vibrant audience. 

🔥 I’ve branded hundreds of incredible businesses, people and charities, the majority of them being from or for marginalised communities. 

🏳️‍🌈 We’ve created Rainbow Wise.

❤️ I have made so many amazing new friends in the online business space who have changed my life in so many beautiful ways. 

💷 And I have successfully generated six figures in revenue every single year since 2022. 

And you know what? That’s pretty damn amazing. 

You know what it also is?

It’s enough. 

I very nearly went into this year once again with the intention to do more. 

But I took some extra time and realised, finally, that I don’t need to do that.

It is the simplest thing, but it feels like such a revelation.

Doing more would require more long days, more time on the road, more hustle, more pressure on myself, more expectations and more compromises.

But my kids are 11, 13, almost 15 and 18. I’m going to blink a few times and they will be flown. (Or they will stay living with us until we die - who can say?) 

We live in a home we adore. 

I know, having done this for years, that if I turn up, I generate business. I just need to be present, to keep reminding you all how I can help you and then delivering that help well and I know I will make sales and the bills will get paid. 

So this year is a new experiment. 

My goal is to do enough to keep us financially exactly where we are now.

I have no plans to launch anything new - although I do give myself permission to run with something new spontaneously if it comes along, because I enjoy that and it usually does fairly well.  

I will do everything I do and I will do it well. In fact, I will probably do it even better because I will not be spread so thin. 

And I will stop missing dinners and assemblies. 

I will still generate those 6 figures in revenue (just watch me) but that will be enough. 

2026, I am now ready for you.

And if you need permission to not have big growth plans this year too, please take this post as having it. Success is what we choose it to be. This year, success will be ending the year living the same blessed, beautiful life I live now, accepting the things that could be better as payment for the peace and time I will have created. Feel free to join me.

@rigobertamenchu ​​is a Maya K’iche’ activist from Guatemala, born in 1959. She became an activist because her entire family turned a battleground.

She is the first Indigenous woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992. After living through the Guatemalan Civil War, one of the most brutal conflicts in Latin America, marked by state violence and genocide against Indigenous peoples, she became a staunch advocate for Indigenous rights worldwide.

Her activism contributed to UN-backed truth commissions; she helped frame the genocide not only as murder, but as cultural destruction; and she challenged colonial narratives that portrayed Indigenous peoples as passive or voiceless.

Menchú emphasizes the need to seek unity through the diversity of peoples, thereby strengthening solidarity, fraternity, and reciprocity to fight against social exclusion and discrimination. I recommend reading her book: I, Rigoberta Menchú: An Indian Woman in Guatemala.

Good morning! Like you, I had hoped for a quiet Sunday where the biggest crisis involved stale bagels or the eternal mystery of missing socks. Instead, we wake up to a Trump administration that somehow manages to be both wildly incompetent and terrifyingly efficient at destabilizing the planet. It’s almost impressive, in the way a toddler with a flamethrower might be.

Let’s start at home, where the United States is very much not “great again,” unless your definition of greatness includes militarized federal agents shooting American citizens and then daring the country to do something about it.

The killing of Renée Nicole Good by an ICE officer in Minneapolis has detonated into one of the largest protest waves we’ve seen in years. Tens of thousands flooded the streets in Minneapolis this weekend, chanting her name, while coordinated protests erupted in all 50 states. Philadelphia alone saw multiple marches converging on federal detention centers, with demonstrators explicitly linking ICE violence at home to Trump’s foreign adventurism abroad. The message from the streets has been blunt: this regime is willing to kill its own citizens to maintain power.

That framing didn’t come from cable news chyron writers or Twitter radicals. It came from teachers, union members, parents, older liberals, young organizers, and people who frankly look exhausted but no longer willing to swallow the “please move on” routine. Protesters aren’t just angry about one shooting. They’re angry about impunity, about the fact that federal authorities immediately seized control of the investigation, blocked state access to evidence, and wrapped themselves in the language of “self-defense” before the blood was even dry. Accountability, apparently, is something we only discuss in theory now.

And yet, in the middle of all this domestic unrest, the administration’s priority appears to be… punishing Minnesota. While Minneapolis mourns and protests, the Trump administration froze food assistance funding to the state, citing vague fraud allegations with an unmistakable racial dog whistle attached. If you don’t accept the official narrative, we will starve your people.

When courts blocked Trump’s broader attempt to freeze billions in social services to Democratic-led states, the administration simply narrowed the target and tried again. Think authoritarianism with a workaround.

While Trump demonstrably cannot manage unrest in his own country, he is once again positioning himself as the world’s self-appointed chaos coordinator. In Venezuela, the situation has gone from illegal to surreal. After a U.S. special forces operation seized Nicolás Maduro, an act Trump openly bragged about, the State Department is now urging Americans to flee the country immediately. Armed paramilitaries are reportedly setting up roadblocks and searching vehicles for U.S. citizens. This, of course, comes after Trump declared Venezuela “safe,” “rich,” and effectively under U.S. control. The reality on the ground suggests otherwise, unless your idea of safety includes armed militias and emergency evacuation advisories.

Trump’s promises of order and dominance are not just reckless, they are staggeringly expensive. They depend on taxpayer-funded militarization at home and abroad, flowing to industries that already receive lavish public subsidies, particularly oil. What he’s really promising is this:you take the profits, the public takes the risk, and the Treasury picks up the tab.

In Iran, the picture is even darker. The country is experiencing its most significant unrest in years, sparked by economic collapse and rapidly expanding into demands for political change. Iranian authorities have responded by arresting protest leaders, imposing a nationwide internet blackout, and reportedly killing hundreds of demonstrators with live ammunition. Protesters are being charged as “enemies of God,” a designation that carries the death penalty.

Trump’s response? Threats. More threats. Vague declarations that the U.S. is “ready to help,” paired with reports that he has been briefed on military strike options against Iran. He cannot stop ICE from killing Americans in Minneapolis, or refuses to, yet he is apparently itching to posture as the global protector of protesters abroad. It’s a neat trick, morally speaking: condemn repression elsewhere while defending and glorifying it at home.

This brings us to Greenland, because apparently the Arctic is having a moment. Trump’s fixation on Greenland has escalated from embarrassing curiosity to full-blown alliance stress test. An opinion piece in the New York Times this week laid out, in chilling detail, how the administration has normalized the idea of seizing Greenland, by force if necessary, despite the fact that Greenland is part of Denmark, a founding NATO member, and already hosts U.S. military installations under long-standing defense agreements.

The reporting is careful, but the implications are stark: if the United States treats allied territory as something it can simply take, NATO ceases to function as a defensive alliance and becomes a punchline. Layered on top of that are more alarming reports circulating in British tabloid media, specifically the Daily Mirror, and amplified by commentators like Shaun King. These claims, which have not been independently confirmed by major outlets, allege that Trump has asked the Joint Special Operations Command to prepare contingency plans for an invasion of Greenland, only to be met with resistance from senior military leaders who view the idea as illegal and catastrophic. One attributed diplomatic quote describes dealing with Trump on the subject as “like dealing with a five-year-old.”

To be absolutely clear: this sourcing is thin, tabloid-based, and should be treated with caution. But the reason it’s circulating, and resonating, is that it aligns disturbingly well with observable behavior. Even if the specifics are unverified, the mindset they describe is painfully plausible: war discussed as impulse management, force as distraction, catastrophe as an option to redirect attention.

Perhaps the most morally bankrupt detail in that reporting is the suggestion that “less controversial” alternatives to invading Greenland might include striking Iran. Less controversial than invading a NATO ally! Sit with that for a moment.

If all of this weren’t bleak enough, we get a reminder that Trump is still fighting the past as ferociously as he’s gambling with the future. This week, the Smithsonian’s National Portrait Gallery quietly removed language noting Trump’s two impeachments from its wall text. The sentence had “long bothered” the White House. After Trump threatened the museum’s leadership, compiled grievance lists, and loomed over the institution’s federal funding, the offending historical fact disappeared. Bill Clinton’s impeachment remains on display. Andrew Johnson’s remains on display. Trump’s? Magically erased.

This follows earlier moves to soften and sanitize official government descriptions of the January 6 insurrection, scrubbing references to Trump’s lies and incitement while urging the country to “move forward.” And here’s the tell: Trump’s MAGA movement is relentlessly nostalgic when it flatters him, and aggressively amnesiac when it implicates him.

“Make America Great Again” is a backward-facing slogan. It worships an imagined past. But the moment that past demands accountability, for January 6, for impeachments, for state violence, suddenly we’re told that dwelling on history is divisive, unhealthy, immature. Healing, we’re informed, requires forgetting.

Real national healing requires accountability. It requires naming harm, assigning responsibility, and drawing lines that cannot be crossed again. The protesters in Minneapolis, Philadelphia, Boston, Portland, San Francisco, and beyond understand this instinctively. That’s why they aren’t asking us to “move on.” They’re asking us to stop pretending nothing happened while it keeps happening.

Finally, because the universe apparently has a sense of humor so dark it needs a wellness check, we arrive at today’s schadenfreude. Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, last year’s Nobel Peace Prize laureate, announced she would like to share her prize with Donald Trump in gratitude for his role in removing Maduro. Trump, who has coveted a Nobel Prize like a raccoon covets shiny objects, said this would be “a great honor.”

The Norwegian Nobel Institute responded with the diplomatic equivalent of a raised eyebrow and a firm “absolutely not.” Nobel Prizes, they reminded everyone, cannot be revoked, transferred, or shared, ever. It’s a small thing, but deeply satisfying: while Trump bullies museums into rewriting wall labels, the Nobel Committee politely declines to rewrite reality.

So here we are. A president who cannot manage unrest in his own cities threatens wars abroad. A regime obsessed with nostalgia erases history while demanding amnesia. An administration allergic to accountability insists it alone can restore order, even as the streets fill with people refusing to forget.

Trump may be incompetent, but he has destabilized the world with stunning efficiency. And it’s worth saying plainly: none of Trump’s grand promises of dominance come free. Every threat, every ICE surge, every foreign “operation,” every vow of “total safety” for oil companies is underwritten by U.S. tax dollars.  We’re told there’s no funding for food assistance, childcare, healthcare, or housing, but there is always money for war, repression, and fossil fuel fantasies. Strength, in this administration, is just austerity for the public paired with endless subsidies for power.

By the end of the night, after all of this, the protests, the erasures, the threats, the absurdities, Marz joined me for an extra-long moonbeam vigil by an outdoor fire. The winter chill, the night sky, and the steady warmth of the blaze felt unexpectedly soothing. It was a reminder that even as institutions buckle and leaders flail, there are still small acts of care, presence, and intention that matter. I hope our warmth, literal and otherwise, made its way to the people who need it most right now. Nostalgia won’t heal this country, but honesty just might.

Baking: Baked in an oven, often a wood-fired oven for authentic flavor. Origins: Its historical roots lie in the ancient flatbreads of Egypt, Rome, and Greece. Modern pizza was born in Naples, Italy, in the 18th century as a cheap food for poor workers. THE NATION: ANTIFA IS REAL, IT’S COMBATING FASCISM, BUT IT IS NOT A CENTRALIZED ORGANIZATION

From The Nation Magazine: “…the truth about antifa—what it actually is, where it comes from, what it’s accomplished—is still spectacular. ‘Antifa,’ a shortening of the word ‘antifascist,’ refers to a decentralized, underground network of radical leftists dedicated to destroying the far right. Its activists are mostly anarchists, communists, and socialists, and, though they might differ in ideology, they all subscribe to a specific militant tradition of antifascism holding that fascists need to be fought ‘by any means necessary.’

“Although antifa groups are very real, and often collaborate, there is not an overarching organization. There are no leaders. No hierarchies. No org chart or headquarters. Decisions are arrived at locally and collectively, with no rich donors to appease. What little money antifa needs is taken from the shallow pockets of its practitioners, mostly working- and middle-class Americans who keep their activism a secret to prevent reprisals from the fascists they fight...”

Statement by Youth for Peace and Dialogue Between Cultures – Morocco

In Solidarity with the Iranian People

Youth for Peace and Dialogue Between Cultures   Morocco unequivocally condemns the ongoing violence and intensifying repression perpetrated by the authorities of the Islamic Republic of Iran against peaceful nationwide protests.

We affirm that the Iranian people’s aspirations for freedom, dignity, and justice are not only legitimate they are universal. These protests must not be dismissed as isolated disturbances or narrowly framed as economic discontent. They are a courageous, collective uprising for fundamental human rights, accountability, and an end to decades of systemic oppression.

After nearly fifty years of authoritarian rule, the people of Iran especially women and youth are rising with extraordinary bravery. Despite grave risks to their lives and liberties, they are demanding a future rooted in liberty, equality, and human dignity. Their voices echo the timeless and borderless call for justice.

As a youth-led organization devoted to peacebuilding, intercultural dialogue, and the defense of human rights, we stand in unwavering solidarity with the Iranian people. We honor the courage of civil society actors, human rights defenders, and legal advocates who continue to speak truth to power in the face of brutal repression.

We call upon the international community, youth movements, and peace organizations around the world to act with moral clarity. We urge them to support accountability for human rights violations, to amplify the voices of the oppressed, and to stand firmly on the side of justice, nonviolence, and human dignity.

Peace is inseparable from freedom. Dialogue cannot flourish where repression reigns.  
The voices of the Iranian people must be heard, protected, and respected.

Mnamo mwaka 1940, China na Urusi—mataifa mawili makubwa—waliungana kwa lengo la kumwangamiza mtu mmoja tu…!!

Imeandaliwa na Fikratul Muhibb 
Ni nani huyu mtu ambaye aliwalazimisha mataifa mawili makubwa kama China na Urusi kuunda muungano dhidi yake, na kuhamasisha jeshi la wapiganaji 300,000, wakiwa na silaha za kisasa zaidi za wakati huo?
Ni shujaa miongoni mwa mashujaa wasiojulikana wa Umma, ambaye kumbukumbu yake ilifutwa kimakusudi kutoka katika historia yetu.
Shujaa huyo ni: Othman Batur Islam Oghlu.
Wakati majeshi ya China na Urusi yalipovamia Turkestan ya Mashariki ili kuwatiisha Waislamu, hayakusita kufanya uhalifu wa kutisha zaidi: kuua, kupora, kubaka, na kuvunja heshima za watu.
Walikuwa wanamkamata kila mtu aliyekuwa na silaha, iwe ni bunduki, mshale, au hata kisu cha uwindaji.

Lakini Othman, shujaa jasiri wa Kizak, anayejulikana kwa jina la “Batur” (yaani shujaa), aliasi na kukataa kuinamia wavamizi hawa.
Alichagua maisha ya milimani, akiwa amebeba silaha yake, na akaanza kupinga muungano huu wa kikatili uliokuja kuzuia kuanzishwa kwa dola itakayowaunganisha Waislamu katika eneo hilo.

Othman alijulikana kwa ujanja na hekima yake ya kijeshi. Alibuni mbinu ya kipekee ya kuvizia adui. Vizingiti vyake vilikuwa vya ngazi nyingi: aliwavuta maadui kwenye mtego ambapo kikosi kizima kiliangamia, na vikosi vya msaada vilipokuja, navyo pia vilianguka kwenye mtego mwingine mkali zaidi.
Aliendelea na mkakati huu hadi akaangamiza majeshi kamili, jambo lililosababisha hofu kubwa katika nyoyo za adui.
Hofu ya Othman na wenzake ilifikia kiwango ambacho wanajeshi wa Urusi na China waliwapa rushwa makamanda wao ili wasipelekwe katika maeneo aliyokuwa akipigana shujaa huyo.
Hata gavana wa kijeshi wa China alifikia hatua ya kukata tamaa kiasi cha kusema: “Yeyote atakayoniletea kichwa cha Othman, akiwa hai au amekufa, nitampa mke wangu kwa siku 70 afanye naye apendavyo.”

Lakini mke huyo alitorokea katika kambi za Waislamu, ambako alisilimu baada ya kushuhudia maadili ya jeshi la Kiislamu.
Baadaye aliolewa na mmoja wa makamanda wa Othman, na akaishi miongoni mwa Waislamu kwa heshima na utu.
Kambi za Othman zilikuwa na sifa njema miongoni mwa watu; hazikujulikana kwa dhulma wala uvamizi dhidi ya wanawake, watoto, au wazee, bali zilifuata maadili bora ya vita vya Kiislamu.

Kitabu “Layali Turkestan” kinamwelezea kiongozi huyu kwa kusema:
“Othman Batur alikuwa na macho makali, ndevu nzito, masharubu marefu, mtulivu katika mienendo yake, mwenye maneno machache, na fikra nzito.
Alivaa mavazi mazito kumkinga dhidi ya baridi kali ya milimani, na kauli mbiu yake iliyotikisa milima ilikuwa: Allahu Akbar… Allahu Akbar.”
Hata hivyo, pamoja na ushujaa wake wote, haikuwezekana kumkamata isipokuwa kwa usaliti.

Msaliti mmoja aliwaongoza majeshi ya adui hadi mahali alipokuwepo. Majeshi ya China yalivamia kambi yake kwa jeshi kubwa sana.
Othman alipigana pamoja na wapiganaji 200 katika vita kali, lakini farasi wake alijikwaa mwishowe.

Baada ya silaha yake kuharibika, aliendelea kupigana kwa kisu, hadi alipojeruhiwa vibaya na kuanguka.
Mnamo 29 Aprili 1951, Othman Batur alikamatwa.
Hakusalimisha roho yake, bali alikabiliana na kifo kwa heshima na utukufu, akitamka takbira.
Aliuawa huku sauti ya Allahu Akbar ikiendelea kusikika, akitembea kuelekea kifo kwa uthabiti.
Habari zilipomfikia mama yake, alisema kwa fahari: “Kwa jambo kama hili nilimlea.”
Mwenyezi Mungu amrehemu Othman Batur, awarehemu mashujaa wenzake, na amrehemu mama aliyemzaa na kumlea shujaa huyu jasiri.
Allahu Akbar ☝🏽

----------------
По воле <пославшей мя (зачеркнуто)> ставшего моей второй натурой интереса к британской политике, я читаю (и слушаю) массу публицистических (а то и академических) текстов. И очень устал от авторов (в том числе, а может и особенно, от уважаемых и популярных), которые преуспевают в интерпретации любых событий в жестких рамках той идеологии или партийной политики, которые им близки. Что ныне считается вполне органичным в условиях выраженно поляризованного общества и отражающих эту поляризацию медиа.

Вот и хочу воспроизвести в своей рубрике текст колумниста Telegraph Тима Стэнли. Который (текст) сопротивляется попыткам втиснуть его в прокрустово ложе идеологизированных аргументов и выводов.

Не буду пересказывать (и даже давать свою интерпретацию) этого текста – френды, интересующиеся политикой (особенно британской и американской) смогут сделать выводы сами. Дам перевод короткого заключительного абзаца: 

----«Давайте попытаемся сымитировать Томаса Джефферсона, оставим имперские амбиции и построим республику  - с королем – где будет цениться свобода и честный труд, не интересуясь соблазнами иностранных дел. Давайте станем нацией, живущей в мире с собой и с окружающим миром.»

Замечу от себя: в нынешних условиях это звучит утопично.
