Trans Nzoia County stands to reap major commercial and economic benefits as Kenya moves closer to commercial oil production in the northwest, the county’s deputy governor said on Wednesday, citing the county’s strategic location along the planned crude transportation corridor.

Deputy Governor Philomenah Kapkory said increased business activity would follow once crude oil transportation begins through Kitale, boosting local trade and investment.

“After commencement of oil transportation via Kitale, our residents will gain economically due to increased business activities,” Kapkory said after hosting members of the Senate and National Assembly energy committees who were in the county to collect views from residents and stakeholders.

She said the county government would continue working with all stakeholders to ensure local communities benefit from the project, including fast-tracking supportive infrastructure.

“We want to ensure that our people benefit immensely, and that is why we want the setting up of infrastructure like roads that will support this to be accelerated,” Kapkory said.

Lawmakers are seeking public input on the proposed commercial development of six oil discoveries in the South Lokichar Basin, focusing on infrastructure plans, environmental safeguards, community obligations and expected national benefits. The fields are set to be developed under new contracts with Gulf Energy E&P BV, which has taken over blocks previously held by Tullow Oil.

The delegation was led by Sen. William Kipkemoi Kisang of Elgeyo Marakwet, the deputy chair of the Senate Standing Committee on Energy, who said the consultations were aimed at ensuring Kenyans play a central role in managing their natural resources.
“We are here to ensure that we have captured what you have to say because your opinion matters,” Kisang said.

Local leaders welcomed the initiative but raised concerns over infrastructure readiness. Matisi ward MCA Obed Mwale said the Eldoret–Kitale road lacked the capacity to handle heavy trucks expected to transport crude oil and called for urgent upgrades.

Hospital Ward MCA Erick Wafula urged the Kenya National Highways Authority, KENHA, to dual the road from Maili Saba and increase the number of flyovers, warning that increased truck traffic would pose safety risks.

“Trucks already transporting raw materials from West Pokot have caused accidents. Failure to expand the road will lead to more,” Wafula said.

He added that the county had not benefited from corporate social responsibility initiatives linked to the highway authority and called for the establishment of a truck parking bay to support local businesses.

Trans Nzoia Senator Alan Chesang said the national government would continue working with county residents by rolling out additional development projects to improve livelihoods.
“The government remains committed to bringing more development projects to Trans Nzoia to better the lives of our people,” Chesang said.

HISTORIA YA MTEMI WA WANYAMWEZI MILAMBO (Sehemu Ya Sita)

Kulingana na masimulizi kutoka kwa Wazee wa Kinyamwezi na Dk. Southon aliyekuwa mmishionari
wa kanisa la kijamii, yeye alikuja Urambo kwenye miaka ya 1879, na kujenga kanisa la kimishionari maili chache kutoka ikulu ya Isela-Magazi. Yeye alifanikiwa kutoa masimulizi jinsi ikulu ya Isela-Magazi ilivyokuwa.

 Alisema kuwa ngome au ikulu ilikuwa imezunguukwa na mfereji mkubvwa, ndani kukiwa na vijumba zaidi ya mia mbili ambavyo vimejengwa kwa miti imara. Na kila nyuma ilikuwa na uwezo wa kuchukua watu wasiopungua kumi. Dk Southon alieleza zaidi jinsi nyumba ya Mtemi Mirambo ilivyokuwa. Alisema kuwa, MtemiMilambo alikuwa na wajenzi ambao walitoka Zanzibar, wafua vyuma na mafundi selemara ambao kwa pamoja walifanikisha kujenga nyumba ya Mtemi Milambo iliyofanana na zile za kiarabu. 

Na hii ilitokana na kuwa waliofia wazungu kuchukua nyumba ile kwani , endapo madirisha yangekuwa makubwa wazungu wangeitamani nyumba ile na kuichukua. Kwa upande mwingine kutokana na masimulizi kutoka kwa mzee Bulemo, alisema kuwa ikulu ya Isela-Magazi ilikuwa imezunguukwa na mfereji, na juu ya mfereji huo kulikuwa na miti
migumu iliyochongwa na kuwa na ncha kali kisha  ikasimamishwa. 

Na hii ilitokana na kuwa walinzi walinde ikulu huku wakijilinda wao wenyewe. Ndani kulikuwa na yumba iliyoitwa NGONG’WA nyumba ambayo ndiyo ilikuwa ya Mtemi Milambo. Wale vijana waliohitimu mafunzo ya kijeshi waliofahamika kama Bakoboko walikuwa

To create a "systematic system" that promotes harmony without infringing on religious freedom, a mix of legal regulation, professionalization, and community-led dialogue is required.

1. Unified Registration & Financial Oversight
Currently, many mosques operate as independent entities with no paper trail. A structured system would include:

Mandatory Registration: 
All mosques and prayer halls should be registered under the KPK Auqaf Department or the Societies Registration Act. This creates a formal database of who is in charge of which facility.

Masjid Boards: 
Instead of a single "Mulla" or caretaker having total control, every mosque should have a notified Masjid Board consisting of 5-10 local residents of good standing. This board should oversee the mosque's administration and finances, ensuring the Imam is accountable to the community.

Audit of Funds: Systematic auditing of mosque/Madrassah donation boxes (Chanda) can prevent funds from being misused or diverted to extremist causes.

2. Professionalizing the Role of Imams
Treating the role of a mosque leader as a professional career rather than an informal position can increase accountability:

Standardized Certification: 
Implementation of a "License to Preach." Imams could be required to hold a degree from a recognized Wafaq (Educational Board) and pass a basic course on Constitutional Rights and Interfaith Harmony.

 Minimum Wage & Benefits: 
Many Imams are underpaid, which makes them vulnerable to external influence. Bringing them into the provincial social security net (EOBI) and ensuring a minimum wage can provide them with the dignity that reduces radicalization.

 Unified Sermon Guidelines: 
While the government cannot dictate every word of a prayer, it can provide weekly themes focusing on social issues (cleanliness, honesty, anti-fraud, rights of neighbors) to ensure the pulpit is used for community building.

3. Sectarian Harmony & Conflict Resolution
To stop the "ideology wars" and disrespect toward other sects:

District Peace Committees: 
For Example. Swat should have a representative "Ulema Council" including scholars from all major schools of thought (Deobandi, Barelvi, Ahl-e-Hadith, Shia). They must sign a Code of Conduct (Paigham-e-Pakistan) promising not to use loudspeakers for "Takfir" (declaring others non-believers).

 Loudspeaker Regulation: 
Strict enforcement of the Sound System Regulation Act. Loudspeakers should only be used for the Azan and internal sermons, never for broadcasting hateful rhetoric that can be heard in the streets.

Joint Community Projects: 
Encourage mosques of different sects to collaborate on non-religious community service, such as blood donation drives or cleaning campaigns. This "humanizes" the other side.

4. Technological Monitoring
 Digital Portal: A centralized app where citizens can report "Hate Speech" or "Illegal Construction" of mosques directly to the Deputy Commissioner’s office.

 QR Code IDs: Each registered mosque can have a QR code displayed at the entrance. Scanning it would show the names of the registered committee members and the authorized Imam.

Unified Sermon Guidelines, 

 as a "weekly theme" or a shared roadmap for the Friday prayer.
Right now, in places like Swat, every Imam decides on their own what to talk about.

 Sometimes they talk about beautiful things, but sometimes they use that time to criticize other sects or focus on topics that don't help the community's daily life.
The goal isn't to tell them "what to believe," but rather to guide them on "how to help the people." Here is how it would work in simple terms:

1. The "Theme of the Week"
Instead of everyone talking about different things, the local administration and a group of respected scholars (from all sects) agree on a common social topic for Friday.

Example: One week, every mosque in Swat talks about "Cleanliness and the Swat River."

Another week: They talk about "The Sin of Financial Fraud and Ponzi Schemes."

Result: The whole district hears the same positive message at the same time. It creates a massive wave of public awareness.

2. The "No-Go Zones" (The Boundary)
The guidelines would have a very simple rule: Use the microphone to build, not to break.

No "Takfir": No Imam is allowed to call another sect "wrong" or "infidels" over the loudspeaker.

Focus on Character: 
The guidelines encourage talking about the Prophet's (PBUH) kindness, honesty in business, and rights of neighbors—things that everyone agrees on.

3. Solving Real-World Problems
Usually, sermons are about history or very abstract religious points. Unified guidelines bring the sermon into the modern world.
 
If there is an outbreak of a disease, the guideline asks Imams to talk about vaccines and health.

 If it's tourist season, they talk about being hospitable and not overcharging visitors.

 This makes the "Mulla" a community leader who helps people live better lives, rather than just a person who leads prayers.

4. How to make it "Stick"?
You can't just give a piece of paper to an Imam and expect him to follow it. It works better like this:

The Friday Bulletin: 
A simple, 1-page bullet-point sheet is sent to every mosque via WhatsApp on Thursday.

 The "Honor" System: 
Instead of "policing" them, the government can reward Imams who follow the guidelines with titles like "District Peace Ambassador" or small grants for mosque repairs/or some extra grant in wages. 

Why this helps Peace?
When Imams follow a guideline, they spend less time focusing on what makes their sect "different" and more time on what makes the community "better." It takes the "ego" out of the pulpit and replaces it with service.

To make this work in a place like Swat, the language needs to be respectful, inclusive, and focused on the common good. Instead of sounding like "government orders," these rules should feel like a social contract—an agreement between neighbors to protect their peace.

A Mohalla Committee could print this, have the Imam and local elders sign it, and display it at the mosque entrance.

The "Masjid-e-Aman" Charter

Our Goal: 
To keep this house of Allah a sanctuary of peace, respect, and service for every resident of this neighborhood, regardless of their personal views.

1. The Rule of the Tongue (Sermon & Speech)

Respect for All: 
No person shall use the mosque’s microphone to criticize, insult, or name-call any other sect or religion. We focus on what unites us, not what divides us.

Constructive Sermons:
 Friday sermons will prioritize character-building (Akhlaq), cleanliness, rights of neighbors, and protection against local issues like drugs and financial frauds.

No Political Campaigning: 
The mosque is for the community and the Creator. It shall not be used as a platform for any political party or candidate.

2. The Sound of Peace (Loudspeaker Policy)

Volume Control: External loudspeakers are for the Azan and short Arabic announcements only.

 Internal Learning: 
Sermons and prayers should be kept to internal speakers so as not to disturb the sick, the elderly, students studying, or neighbors of other faiths/views.

3. The "Community Hub" Activities
The mosque is more than a prayer hall; 
it is a center for life. We agree to use this space for:

The "Mohalla Baithak"/Place for NIKAH. 
Once a month, the mosque courtyard will host a meeting where residents can discuss local problems like water shortages, electricity, or street security.

Student Study Zone: 
During exam seasons, the mosque (or an attached room) can be opened as a quiet, safe place for local students to study if they don't have electricity or space at home.

Conflict Resolution: 
The mosque will serve as a neutral ground for the Jirga or committee to settle small disputes between neighbors peacefully.

Disaster Relief: 
In case of floods, earthquakes, or emergencies, the mosque will automatically become the collection and distribution center for the neighborhood.

4. Financial Transparency
Public Record: 
Every penny collected in the Chanda (donation) box will be recorded by the Mohalla Committee.

Monthly Disclosure: 
A simple one-page summary of "Money In" and "Money Out" (Electricity bills, repairs, Imam’s salary) will be posted on the mosque notice board every month.

5. Oversight & Accountability

The Committee: 
The mosque will be managed by a 5-7 member committee of residents. This committee must include at least one educator (teacher), one elder, and one youth representative.

 Open Door Policy:
 Any resident who feels a sermon was hateful or the mosque is being misused has the right to bring it to the committee for immediate discussion.

The Signature Ceremony: 
Don't just post the rules. Hold a small tea gathering at the mosque. Invite the Imam and the elders to sign the Charter together as a "Pledge of Honor."

 Youth Involvement: 
Give the young boys of the neighborhood the "duty" of keeping the mosque library or study area clean. When they feel it’s their space, they protect it.

To transform Madrassas from isolated religious centers into modern Community Resource Hubs, 
The KPK government and the local public must collaborate on a "Safety & Modernization Framework." 
The goal is to ensure students receive a balanced education that includes market-driven skills while staying protected from extremist ideologies.

Here are the recommended safety measures and procedures:
1. Government Initiatives (Policy & Regulation)
Mandatory "Madrassa Plus" Curriculum

The government should incentivize Madrassas to adopt a dual-curriculum model.

Equivalency Mapping: 
Align Madrassas with the Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE). A student studying Dars-e-Nizami should also pass standard exams in English, Math, and General Science.

 Technical Integration: 
Partner with KP-TEVTA to establish small vocational labs within Madrassas. Students should spend 30% of their time learning skills like Mobile Repairing, Electrician Work, Solar Panel Installation, or Basic Coding, IT skills. 

The "Integrated Screening" System
Teacher Certification: 
Like regular schools, Madrassa teachers should undergo a "Character & Competence" verification process.

No-Hate-Speech Monitoring:
 Use the District Intelligence Committees to ensure that the literature taught is the official curriculum and does not contain sectarian or radical content.

Financial Formalization
Direct Aid over Private Donations: 
Government should provide grants for libraries, computers, and science labs. In exchange, the Madrassa must maintain transparent audit trails. This reduces dependence on "blind donations" that often come with ideological strings attached.

2. Safety & Child Protection Measures
Physical & Mental Safeguarding
Child Protection Units (CPU): Every Madrassa must be linked to the provincial Child Protection and Welfare Commission.

 Anonymous reporting helplines (like 1121) should be prominently displayed.

 Anti-Corporal Punishment Policy: Strictly enforce the ban on physical punishment. The government should provide training to Mohtamims (Heads) on Positive Discipline techniques.

Surveillance & Environment
CCTV in Common Areas: To prevent physical or psychological abuse, common halls and corridors should have camera coverage accessible to the Madrassa Board.

 Open-Door Policy: Encourage a "Day Scholar" model where children spend evenings with their families. For boarders, weekly "Parent-Teacher Meetings" (PTMs) should be mandatory.

3. The Role of the Local Public (Community Oversight)
The public is the most effective "neighborhood watch" for Madrassas.

Community Management Boards
A Madrassa should not be run by a single person. 
The 70/30 Board: 70% of the board should consist of local parents and respected professionals (doctors, engineers, retired teachers), while 30% are religious scholars.

Transparency: 
This board must review the guest speakers and ensure no radical outsider is allowed to address the students.

Public "Exposure Trips"
Local communities should organize trips for Madrassa students to visit universities, software houses, and industrial zones.
 
The Goal: Break the "us vs. them" mentality by showing students that they are part of the modern world and that their technical skills are valued.

4. Countering Radicalization through "Realistic Islam"
To prevent radicalization, the teaching of Islam must shift from "Polemic" to "Ethical":

 Focus on 'Huquq-ul-Ibad' (Rights of People): Shift the focus of Friday sermons and daily lessons toward honesty in trade, protection of the environment, and rights of minorities and women.

Interfaith & Intra-faith Dialogue: 
Host joint sports events or community cleaning drives where Madrassa students work alongside students from private/government schools. This humanizes the "other" and kills the root of radicalization.

To make Madrassas financially independent of private (and often opaque) donations, 
The government needs a transition strategy that shifts them from a Charity-Based Model to a State-Subsidized & Performance-Linked Model.

Here is a 5-point policy framework for the KPK government:

1. Establishment of a "Provincial Madrassa Endowment Fund"
The government should create a dedicated, transparent fund specifically for registered Madrassas.
Seed Capital: 
The government provides initial funding, supplemented by Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) contributions from local industries.

Zakat & Ushr Integration:
 Instead of individuals giving Zakat directly to Madrassas without oversight, the provincial Zakat department can distribute a portion of collected funds to registered Madrassas based on their student strength and facilities.

2. The "Voucher-Based" Student Support System
To ensure money follows the student rather than the institution's leadership:

Education Vouchers: The government issues monthly vouchers to students from low-income families enrolled in registered Madrassas.

Direct Payment: 
The Madrassa redeems these vouchers from the government. This makes the Madrassa financially stable while giving the government leverage to monitor attendance and quality of education.

3. Vocational Outsourcing & Income Generation
The government can help Madrassas become "Social Enterprises":

Production Units: 
Use the vocational labs (TEVTA) mentioned earlier to create production units. For example, a Madrassa with a tailoring lab can take government contracts to stitch school uniforms or hospital bedsheets.

Agri-Madrassa Model:
 In rural KPK, the government can lease small patches of state land to Madrassas for modern tunnel farming or olive groves. The profit stays with the Madrassa to cover its operational costs.

4. Performance-Linked Grants (The Star Rating System)
Financial support should be tied to transparency and modern standards.

Grading System: 
Madrassas should be rated (1 to 5 stars) based on:
Financial audit transparency.
Inclusion of Science and English in the curriculum.
Teacher-to-student ratio and hygiene.
Tiered Funding: 5-star Madrassas receive full government coverage for utility bills (electricity/gas) and teacher salaries, while lower-rated ones receive less until they improve.

5. Mandatory Digital Audit & Reporting
To eliminate "hidden" private donations that might carry radical agendas:

Dedicated Bank Accounts: 
Every registered Madrassa must have a single, official bank account. All donations (public or private) must be deposited there.

Digital Ledger: 
The government should provide a simple accounting software/app. Any expenditure above a certain limit (e.g., 50,000 PKR) must be documented digitally to be eligible for future government grants.

What this achieves:
 
Security: By controlling the purse strings, the government ensures no "dark money" enters the system for radicalization.

Dignity: Teachers receive a regular, honorable salary through the bank instead of relying on unstable charity.

Mainstreaming: Students feel part of the formal national economy.

To create a truly skilled workforce from the Madrassa system, 
The KPK government should move toward a "Dual-Education Policy." 

This policy would treat religious studies as the "Major" and a technical trade as the "Minor," ensuring every graduate has a professional license alongside their religious degree.

Here is an elaboration of these skills and a policy framework to implement them:

1. Skill Categorization (The Professional Tracks)
A. Hospitality & Tourism (The "Sawat-Hazara" Model)

KPK is a tourism hub. Madrassa students can be trained to lead this sector.

Eco-Tourism Guides: Training in local history, geography, and environmental protection.

Language Translators: Since they study Arabic, they can be trained in English and Chinese to serve as high-end translators for Gulf tourists and CPEC projects.

Hotel & Culinary Management: Professional certification in food safety, hospitality, and catering.

B. Medical & Emergency Services
Madrassas are often located in remote areas where doctors are scarce.

Paramedical Staff & Nursing: 
Training as Medical Technicians or Lady Health Visitors (for female Madrassas). They can run basic clinics in their villages.

First Aid & Rescue 1122 Volunteers: Certified training in emergency response, CPR, and disaster management.

Pharmacy Assistants: Training to manage local pharmacies with a focus on medicine safety and dosage.

C. Inspection & Quality Control

These roles are critical for the growing industrial and construction sectors in KPK.

Safety Inspectors: Training in Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) for construction sites and factories.

 Quality & Quantity Surveyors (QS): Teaching them to calculate material costs and verify the quality of construction/food products.

 Halaal Food Auditors: Combining their religious knowledge with scientific testing to certify food products for export to the Gulf.

D. Digital & Advanced IT

 IT Experts & Software Basics: Moving beyond data entry to Web Development, App Development, and Cyber Security.

 Mobile & Laptop Engineering: Advanced hardware repairing and software troubleshooting.

 CCTV & Smart Home Technicians: Designing and installing security systems and "Internet of Things" (IoT) devices.

2. The Policy Framework: "The Madrassa Empowerment Act"

The KPK government should adopt the following policy measures to make this a reality:

A.The "Skill-Credit" System
 
Policy: No Madrassa degree (Sanad) should be recognized by the government unless it is accompanied by a Level-3 Vocational Certificate from KP-TEVTA or a similar body.

  Implementation: Students earn "credits" for technical hours spent in the lab, just like they do for their religious books.

B.Mandatory "On-Campus" Workshops

 Policy: Large Madrassas must provide space for a "Mini-Vocational Center."

 Implementation: The government provides the machinery (lathe machines, solar kits, computers), and the Madrassa provides the building and the students.

C. The "Imam-Entrepreneur" Micro-Loans

 Policy: Graduates who hold both a religious degree and a technical certificate should be eligible for interest-free "Start-up Loans."

 Goal: To help a graduate open his own mobile repair shop, solar consultancy, or modern dairy farm, making him a job provider rather than a job seeker.

D. Public-Private Apprenticeships

 Policy: The government should mandate local industries (e.g., Marble factories in Mardan, Match factories in Risalpur) to take a specific quota of Madrassa apprentices for 6-month hands-on training.

Steps for the Government:
 * Pilot Project: Select 20 large Madrassas (5 in Peshawar, 5 in Swat, 5 in DI Khan, 5 in Abbottabad) to launch the "Dual-Track" pilot.
 * Mapping: Map the local industry near each Madrassa (e.g., if a Madrassa is near a forest area, teach them Forestry/Honey production; if near a city, teach them IT/Electronics).

AUSTRALIA 2026 EXPLAINED
On Monday the long-awaited Australia journey took off.  There was a lot of joy, and depending on where one stands, readers and viewers would like to know more – the reason for this post.
Australia did not come in isolation, but is a milestone in the seven evangelical pilgrimages or journeys that were prescribed by God last century. This was even before air travel was common. For Kenyans reading, remember that President Mwai Kibaki went to study in London using water transport. Many years ago. The seven journeys formally began in 1998, but a recap will be done for the benefit of readers.
Last year there were a few photos posted after the trip by three (3) pastors that started June 30th 2025. It was a planning journey that had been directed by the Holy Spirit. 
Australia had been in the drawing boards for a long time, compared to the other six – which were executed in a span of about 8 years. That was the cause of excitement because many grew up hearing about Australia. A child who was 6 years old when the second India Matiwimana took place is a 26-year-old adult today.  However, God had vowed that Australia would happen in his ways and terms – even if it would be done by a future generation. Some questions arose on:

1. Airport and Country
For those asking about the Airport and country, that was Jomo Kenyatta International Airport in Nairobi, Kenya.

2. Destination
The immediate destination was Sidney, Australia via Dubai. Australia is a big country that may require visits to other areas.

3. Number of Persons
All the 24 visas requested were granted – 12 Elders (or representatives) and 12 sisters from the House of Covenant.
A further question asked is whether the number had to be 24. That was the prescribed number, but again it depends on many factors. In the first Israel Journey there were 25 people. The elders were 13 – being the full council of 12 at the time, together with Pastor Macharia of Nakuru – who later became an Evangelist.
Someone also asked: Do women in the church who are not sisters included in these journeys? If you remember a number went to Ethiopia in 2024, and South Sudan in 2025 – they also have a lot of work – so eventually as Churches are established and the council sees it fit, they will also be included.

4. What were the other 6 Countries?
They were: Israel, Britain, Ethiopia, Germany, USA, and India. 
The 7 however, are only a launch of the global program – as our founder explained, the gospel should be spread throughout the world including South America. As a result, having a debt of Australia was a drawback – because God could not launch us fully into the next phase of evangelical work, without completing the work already assigned.

5. Who organized the Journey?
Apostles, especially those in Southern Africa will usually ask whether these were the Mai (Gandanzara) group or the Council of Jacob (Jeep).
Those who know the history of Gospel of God, from the South Africa days – even before there was a Jeep, there was the Evangelical Council or Dare rePitros (Council of Peter). This was Baba Johane’s Council and it was never dissolved. Together with the Council of Jacob they are key administrative organs of the Church. It is the reason two representatives from the Jeep came to Nairobi to witness the departure.  In addition, there was also a council in In Bulawayo (overseeing Matebeleland) and answered directly to the founder's council – while supporting missionary work. It is still in place.
The Dare Peter was never based in Zimbabwe – because in the days of the founder Evangelical work was one-way: Leave home and become a missionary and travel.
Those who are in Zambia today, were also part of the missionary group and that is the reason the late Evangelist Nyandoro of Zambia had been given some evangelical assignments that he was to in consultation with the Council in Nairobi. According to the founder, those who returned home from South Africa, were not to rejoin the missionary group again. 
Those ministered to by the Council of Peter – whether in South Sudan or elsewhere are also counted as missionaries.

6. Why was Baba Johane sent if Jesus is already ruling?
This question came as a misguided statement but it is good to address it for the benefit of learning. Gospel of GOD was established by God himself – the president. Not the deputy or vice president. There are many who do not know that this world has a boss, but there is no problem because going by where the world is headed, they will learn very well – whether the soft way or the hard way.
There is time for everything. There was time for the prophets, for the son, and for the father (Read Matthew 21:33-46). The crucifixion of Jesus was not the end. He posed a question to the 
vineyard tenants and when they replied he concurred: The owner of the vineyard will come himself and take the vineyard and give it to another people who will bear fruits.  
This is a process that began during the times of the Apostles of Jesus – but continues to happen in what they called the future. The reason John begins Revelations by saying: Blessed is he WHO is and WHO was and WHO is to come (Revelation 1:4). Who is this unnamed he? Why does he later say and the seven spirits in front of his throne and Jesus Christ the faithful witness. This is the overall boss. So even today when we talk of the Second coming of Jesus Christ, we are also aware about the coming of HE. Times change. That is why Enoch says, the most-high will descend in the southern quarter of the earth (Enoch 77:1). There is time for everything. It is the reason the last Gospel goes out to the world from Africa (Isaiah 19:23-24, Isaiah 18, Psalms 68:31).
If everything was accomplished 2,000 years ago, there would be no need for God to send a redeemer to Africa, and it is not useful to engage on argument whether the one spoken of in (Isaiah 19:20) is senior or junior to Jesus. That is irrelevant as long as he was sent is representing the overall boss (Isaiah 19:1) – the rest is not too important to ponder. At times authority is derived from the sender or appointing authority. The second coming is therefore a corporate and not unitary event – it is about the entirety of God’s kingdom. The reason the rider of the white horse in Revelations 19:15 has an unknown name. He but himself knows his name? Who is it that can know even what the angels and the son know not? It is the father (Matthew 24:36). When the father comes, he comes with the Kingdom including the son for they are one. In the same sense spouses are one (Ephesians 5:31). These are not literal statements. Thus apostles usually taught to pray, in the name of the “father, son and holy spirit”.
Questions and comments are welcome and one can always book a Bible study. Physical or virtual.

7. Gospel of God, Australia
Most readers will learn only from this post that Gospel of God is a legally registered entity in Australia. It is the institution hosting the delegation. How and when it came to be is a story for another day. Our immediate membership including the South Sudan and Ethiopia Diaspora is very committed to their call in Australia. Apostles in Australia have worked together to host to the current journey. When the advance party travelled to Australia last year, they also met a team from the Johane Masowe YeChisanu fraternity in the Oceania Region (Australia, New Zealand, ...). 
Last year, when one of the 3 delegates was on a flight, the LORD told him to tell his colleagues that the book (message) that he had been given earlier to deliver would be read by another prophet from Australia. Reason being that if he spoke as a visitor, the message would be understood differently. Such are the ways and means of the living God.
Therefore, there are apostles in Australia who think they went there as immigrants looking for opportunities but to God, there is a reason why they are there. 

8. The Prophecy of Australia
From the instructions given, Australia and India were among the seven countries where there was more evangelical work to be done. That is why even today the Holy Spirit is speaking of pending work in India – which should be done. Guidance on the same will be provided.
As far as Australia is concerned, Baba Johane had asked the country to be visited because for among other reasons it lay on the tropic of Capricorn where he was born. This may not have much meaning to us, but needs to be fulfilled. A comparable example that can be given is the Equator at Nyahururu, Kenya. When he was in Tanzania, he was instructed not to cross the equator. This was followed to the letter. In fact, during the Nyahururu journey he sent apostles to go and read the equator sign on both sides to confirm that it was the correct place and he watched from a reasonable distance.
According to him, the gospel should reach the natives of Australia as well – for it is a gospel of all peoples – every tongue, tribe, people, and nation (Revelation 14:6-7). When the delegates return as usual there will be a briefing on what transpired and the next steps.

She touched the ring and whispered, "Release the painting.”

Thud.

"Damn, it is real interspace storage ring!"

Ragnar whispered, hollow, "Fifty million..."
Alex tilted his head slightly. “You laughed at dreams. Turns out you were laughing at reality."
Ragnar's hands shook. “You said... you said it was fake.”

He glanced at Sofina.
“I never said hers was.”
Belinda's knees buckled. “We sold it for ninety thousand...”

Marlena turned to her, puzzled. “And who are you?”

“Sofina,” Belinda said, her tone sharp and accusing. "Why are you being so selfish? Are you really willing to destroy our class friendship over money? You should give the painting-and the ring-to the class.”

Belinda nodded, relaxed and confident. “Sure. Send me your résumé. I'll mention it to my dad. If any of you want to work with Eden Group, my father can make it easy."
“Thank you, Belinda!" others said quickly.

Sofina stopped her.

She paused, then looked straight at Belinda. "As for the painting, I bought it legally at this auction," Sofina said calmly. “But I'm willing to sell it back to you. Ninety thousand. What do you think?"
A ten-million-dollar painting. For ninety thousand.
Belinda-and everyone else in the room-instantly believed it was the greatest bargain they would ever see.
“Deal,” Belinda said without a second of hesitation. “Sell it to me. Now.” 

Chapter 510

"Transfer the money first," Sofina said, calm but firm.
She wanted the cash back-the money she had used to buy the ring-so at least she wouldn't take a financial hit on top of everything else.
“Fine,” Belinda sneered. "It's only ninety thousand. Do you really think I wouldn't pay such pocket change?"
"No money, no item," Sofina replied flatly, tightening her grip on the ancient painting.
Belinda sent the transfer through her bracelet without hesitation and snatched the painting the moment it cleared.
A wide smile spread across her face. In her mind, the profit was already counted-millions of dollars sitting right in her hands.
"Now,” Belinda said, lifting her chin, her eyes sharp and demanding, “about the ring. Hand it back to me. Right now."

Her voice hardened. “You'll be facing them. Believe me-I will win that ring."
Sofian shook his head, exhausted. He didn't even bother to respond.

Belinda scoffed, pure contempt on her face. 
“What the hell do you know?" she snapped. “If I joined Eden Group, who would run the company we set up to connect with Eden Group's purchasing department? Me staying outside, my father staying inside-that's the perfect setup. That's how real money is made.”
“I... I still don't get it," one of the classmates admitted.
Belinda smirked, clearly savoring the moment. "I own a company that supplies materials to Eden Group. Through my father, I secure the contracts. The materials come from other suppliers, but they pass through my company's name before reaching Eden Group. I just add a few percent to the price-no work, no risk. Every cent of that profit flows straight to me."
“Damn,” someone blurted out. “You must be making a fortune."
Belinda snorted. “It's nothing worth mentioning. Maybe a few million a month."
Then she turned her gaze toward Alex, her smile turning fake and sharp.
"Alex," she said sweetly, her voice coated in sugar and threat, “give me the ring back."
“Give it back?" Alex replied without hesitation, his voice cold and razor-sharp. “How could you even think it was yours in the first place? Don't you feel any shame? It belongs to Sofina-and it always will.”
“Where did you get that ring?" Belinda demanded. “Did you steal it?"
All eyes turned toward Alex, curiosity and suspicion flashing across their faces.
“You don't need to know,” Alex said evenly. “You can report it to the police if you want. See if you find anything illegal."
His gaze was steady, unbothered. “All you'll get is public embarrassment."
Belinda sneered. "So confident now, huh?” Her lips curled. “I heard you work as a gardener at Eden Group. Is that right?”
“You don't need to know,” Alex replied calmly.
Without waiting for his answer, Belinda tapped her bracelet and made a call.
When the connection went through, she switched it to loudspeaker-making sure everyone in the room could hear every word.
“Dad,” Belinda said sharply into her bracelet, her voice dripping with outrage, “there's a lowly gardener from Eden Group. He and his wife cheated us out of a reunion auction item and refuse to give it back. He basically stole what belongs to me. Can you have him fired from Eden Group?"
“How dare he steal from you?" her father's voice thundered through the bracelet. “What's his name?"
“Alexander Saint-Claire,” Belinda sneered.
“Then tell him this,” her father said coldly. “He's fired. And he is never to set foot in Eden Group again.”
“Thank you, Dad,” Belinda said sweetly. “And I'll need to borrow a few lawyers to reclaim the item, same as always.”
“Of course,” her father replied without hesitation. “Use them however you like."
Alex shook his head slowly. Another parasite, openly abusing Eden Group's power for personal gain-without shame, without fear.
“Well, loser,” Belinda laughed loudly, eyes sharp with cruelty. 
“You're unemployed now," she mocked. “What are you going to do from today onward? Don't tell me you plan to live off Sofina, doing housework like a parasite, huh?”
Laughter burst around the table.
Alex only shrugged, his expression calm, almost lazy.
“Well,” he said evenly, “thanks for freeing me from a boring job. Now all I get to do is laundry, cooking, driving my wife to work and picking her up, giving her massages every day-and loving her."
A faint smile crossed his lips. “Honestly? That's a great job. It'll make me happy. I'm going to enjoy it. You're doing me a huge favor.”
Belinda nearly lost control. How dare this shameless bastard sound so proud? So casual? So unapologetic? She swallowed her fury, teeth grinding, and spat out, “Alex, I never knew you were such a happy leech!”
"So?” Alex replied calmly, a faint smile tugging at his lips. “I didn't steal. I didn' t rob anyone. I contribute by doing housework. Make my wife happy. Why shouldn't I be happy? Remember, happy wife is happy life.”
The laughter died instantly.
The room fell into stunned silence.
They had never seen someone so brazen. So openly shameless. And what made it worse-what twisted the knife-was that they were jealous.
Sofina Scheinwald was stunning.
Elegant. Untouchable.
A woman many of them could only dream of. To live off someone like her was a fantasy they could never reach.
And she was an official partner of Eden Group-listed by major magazines as one of the most powerful women in Winchester.
The jealousy burned. Thick. Bitter. Suffocating.
Ragnar stepped forward, glaring at Alex.
“Hey, loser. Don't you have any pride at all?" 
Alex laughed openly. “I'm proud of it. What's wrong with being a live-in husband if it means being with a woman like Sofina Scheinwald?"
His eyes were sharp, mocking. “That's a win in my book. As far as I remember, you're the one stuck with a woman carrying five different STDs-and she's nowhere near as beautiful as Sofina."
He tilted his head slightly. “You're the real loser here."
Ragnar nearly choked, his face flushing as if he'd been punched in the throat.
“Ragnar,” Belinda cut in coldly. “There's no point wasting words on a stupid loser. It's a waste of time. Let's continue the auction.”
She turned away at once and clapped her hands, snapping back into control. One by one, she opened the gifts and began the auction, her voice ringing clearly through the room.
“Thank you, Felix, for your six-hundred-dollar bid!”
“Thank you, Helena, for the useless wall clock. Honestly, who even uses these anymore?"
“Thank you, Ola Rivers, for the so-called beautiful but completely unknown vase!”
“And thank you, Karl, for your gift-worth a grand total of two hundred dollars!" She scoffed.
“Why did you even bother showing up?"
She rolled her eyes and muttered, “Damn, most of you are assholes."
Then Belinda paused. Her gaze landed on one final item.
“I remember this one," she said slowly. "This was Sofina's gift."
Instantly, every pair of eyes locked onto it. Belinda picked it up and examined it. Inside the box lay a single green stone about the size of a chicken egg.
Nothing fancy.
Nothing dazzling.
"Well?” Belinda sneered. "Who wants to bid on this?”
Her lips curled. “Let's start at one thousand dollars."
"Ten thousand,” Alex said calmly, raising his hand.
The room jolted.
“Twenty thousand,” Renata added immediately.
The classmates stared at the stone again, their minds racing.
Painting. Ring. What if this was another treasure worth millions?
"Thirty thousand," Ragnar barked, lifting his hand.
Belinda bit her lip and jumped in herself. “Forty thousand."
The numbers climbed, slowly but steadily-fifty thousand, sixty, eighty-until they finally hit one hundred thousand dollars.
And then-Alex smirked.
Because only he knew the truth.
That green stone was nothing special at all. 
Just an ordinary rock he had picked up off the street.

📍 Greensboro, North Carolina

Nearly two years after she vanished without a trace, police are still asking for answers in the disappearance of Marissa Kay Carmichael, a mother of five who was last seen in Greensboro on January 14, 2024 after making a distressed 911 call. 

Police confirm Carmichael, who was 24 at the time, was captured on surveillance footage around 3:46 a.m. at an Exxon gas station on East Market Street after calling 911 and telling dispatchers she had been left stranded without her phone. In the call, she said a man told her to go inside the station to pick up things, then drove off, leaving her with no way home.  ￼

Officers who arrived shortly after the call found no sign of her at the station itself, and she has not been seen in public since. Police say there is footage of her getting into a vehicle that left the scene, and detectives have since identified and interviewed the driver of that vehicle, who is currently considered a witness. Investigators haven’t released that video publicly.  ￼

Greensboro police stress the case is still an active missing-person investigation, and they are “absolutely” concerned for her welfare as the years have passed, especially given how out of character it is for her to disappear without contacting her family.  ￼

Carmichael’s family shared that the night before she vanished she had gone out with friends, including to a lounge and an after-party, and was then dropped off at the gas station alone. Since then, her phone has been off and inactive, and she has not posted on social media which is something her loved ones say is completely unlike her.  ￼

Police have entered Carmichael’s information into national missing-person databases including NCIC and are asking anyone with information — no matter how small — to contact Greensboro/Guilford Crime Stoppers at 336-373-1000.

PUL Calls for Responsible Journalism and Security Collaboration at Third Media–Security Conference in Ganta

(Ganta, Nimba County, January 13, 2026): The Press Union of Liberia (PUL) has underscored the critical need for a strong and responsible partnership between the Liberian media and the nation’s joint security forces. This call to action was issued on Monday, 12 January 2026, at the opening of the third Media–Security Conference, in Ganta, Nimba County, to foster professionalism, integrity, and mutual respect in electoral processes.

In an address at the conference, PUL President Julius Kanubah emphasized the pivotal roles of journalists and law enforcement in safeguarding Liberia’s democracy and promoting social cohesion. “Constructive engagement between the media and security sector is essential,” Kanubah stated. “Together, we can uphold freedom of expression, a free press, and the rule of law, while ensuring that our conduct reflects the highest professional standards.”

Organized under the auspices of the National Elections Commission (NEC) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the Ganta conference involves 47 journalists and law enforcement officers from Grand Cape Mount, Margibi, Bong, Lofa, and Nimba Counties. 

The primary focus of the gathering is to review and update the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that guide collaboration, cooperation, and coordination between the media and security agencies, particularly during electoral processes.

Representing Joint Security, Deputy Commissioner of Police and Head of the West African Police Information System at the Liberia National Police (LNP), Augustine Browne, stressed the importance of unity in advancing peace and stability. ‘It is imperative for the media and security to work in concert to prevent misunderstandings and foster a peaceful environment’, Browne remarked.

UNDP Programme Officer Roosevelt Zayzay also noted the value of the SOP in reducing potential conflicts and misunderstandings between media professionals and security officers throughout the 2023 General and Presidential Elections. ‘A clear framework ensures that all parties understand their roles and responsibilities, minimizing confrontation and building public trust’, Zayzay said.

Executive Director of the NEC, Anthony Sengbe, urged all stakeholders to maintain the highest levels of professionalism. ‘Our collective commitment will ensure that Liberia’s electoral process remains peaceful and free from violence’, Sengbe stated.

Attorney Christopher Fayiah, Deputy Executive Director of the Liberia Peacebuilding Office, highlighted the need to integrate lessons learned and best practices into the revised SOP. ‘Continuous improvement of the framework is vital to address emerging challenges and to strengthen the role of women in peacebuilding initiatives’, Fayiah said.

The Ganta conference builds on two preceding regional media–security conferences held in Zwedru, Grand Gedeh County, and Buchanan, Grand Bassa County, which collectively engaged media and security representatives from several counties across Liberia. The current review process emphasizes roles and responsibilities, dispute-resolution mechanisms, and the enhancement of women’s participation in peace promotion.

Following the conference on Wednesday, 14 January, a comprehensive working session will collate insights from all three regional gatherings. These findings will inform a validation workshop that will lead to the finalization of the revised SOP.

The SOP review and regional consultations are part of the Liberia Electoral Support Project (LESP), managed by UNDP and generously supported by the European Union and the Governments of Sweden and Ireland.

One thing I have always despised about social media is how literally people take it. Someone shares their highlight reel, and suddenly you feel inadequate—as if you’re behind or doing something wrong.

I never want someone to look at my Facebook and think I have it all together. I think I’ve done a decent job of showing that, but I want to say it clearly: I’m just a normal person with normal struggles.

Some people say they wish they had my “dedication” to health and wellness. Let me remind you that I went nearly two years without any real routine. And this wasn’t just about my physical health—this is my career. I was too busy fighting my own demons to commit to something I encouraged others to commit to. I’m honestly relieved that movement and routine are part of my normal again, but don’t think I don’t still have to talk myself into it some days. When I do show up, though? It changes my life for days afterward.

My marriage? I’m married to a beautiful man I’m incredibly grateful for—but we’ve also grown up together. We’re still learning how to argue in a healthy manner. We still forget to put each other first during this phase of parenthood. But we choose each other and work for one another every single day.

Motherhood? That’s something I feel confident in. And still—I miss nightly suppers, I’m not great at prioritizing homework, and my mind is often somewhere else when it should be fully present with my kids. But I’m working on it. And I’m proud of how much healing motherhood has brought me.

The point of all this is simple: I’m just a normal person rooting for myself—and rooting for you, too. I’m at a pivotal age, trying to get the most out of the rest of my life while also mourning what feels too late to grasp. I’m navigating friendships, learning who and what deserves my time. I’m a work in progress, but I’m working—and that’s the whole point.

When you stop wishing you were somewhere else and start showing up fully in your own story, that’s where peace starts to find you.

In an address at the conference, PUL President Julius Kanubah emphasized the pivotal roles of journalists and law enforcement in safeguarding Liberia’s democracy and promoting social cohesion. “Constructive engagement between the media and security sector is essential,” Kanubah stated. “Together, we can uphold freedom of expression, a free press, and the rule of law, while ensuring that our conduct reflects the highest professional standards.”

Organized under the auspices of the National Elections Commission (NEC) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the Ganta conference involves 47 journalists and law enforcement officers from Grand Cape Mount, Margibi, Bong, Lofa, and Nimba Counties. 

The primary focus of the gathering is to review and update the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that guide collaboration, cooperation, and coordination between the media and security agencies, particularly during electoral processes.

Representing Joint Security, Deputy Commissioner of Police and Head of the West African Police Information System at the Liberia National Police (LNP), Augustine Browne, stressed the importance of unity in advancing peace and stability. ‘It is imperative for the media and security to work in concert to prevent misunderstandings and foster a peaceful environment’, Browne remarked.

UNDP Programme Officer Roosevelt Zayzay also noted the value of the SOP in reducing potential conflicts and misunderstandings between media professionals and security officers throughout the 2023 General and Presidential Elections. ‘A clear framework ensures that all parties understand their roles and responsibilities, minimizing confrontation and building public trust’, Zayzay said.

Executive Director of the NEC, Anthony Sengbe, urged all stakeholders to maintain the highest levels of professionalism. ‘Our collective commitment will ensure that Liberia’s electoral process remains peaceful and free from violence’, Sengbe stated.

Attorney Christopher Fayiah, Deputy Executive Director of the Liberia Peacebuilding Office, highlighted the need to integrate lessons learned and best practices into the revised SOP. ‘Continuous improvement of the framework is vital to address emerging challenges and to strengthen the role of women in peacebuilding initiatives’, Fayiah said.

The Ganta conference builds on two preceding regional media–security conferences held in Zwedru, Grand Gedeh County, and Buchanan, Grand Bassa County, which collectively engaged media and security representatives from several counties across Liberia. The current review process emphasizes roles and responsibilities, dispute-resolution mechanisms, and the enhancement of women’s participation in peace promotion.

Following the conference on Wednesday, 14 January, a comprehensive working session will collate insights from all three regional gatherings. These findings will inform a validation workshop that will lead to the finalization of the revised SOP.

The SOP review and regional consultations are part of the Liberia Electoral Support Project (LESP), managed by UNDP and generously supported by the European Union and the Governments of Sweden and Ireland.

OPEN LETTER TO THE PRESIDENT H.E. JOSEPH N.BOAKAI Sr.

January 14, 2026

Your Excellency,
H.E. Joseph Nyumah Boakai, Sr.
President of the Republic of Liberia
Executive Mansion
Monrovia, Liberia

RE: Legal and Policy Grounds for Withholding a Third Ratification of the ArcelorMittal Mineral Development Agreement.

Your Excellency,

On behalf of the Environmental Eyes Consultancy and Advocacy Firm Inc, we respectfully extend our compliments and acknowledge your administration’s public commitment to the rule of law, environmental protection, accountability, and inclusive national development. These principles are firmly grounded in Liberia’s Constitution and policy framework; and it serves as a guide to our respectful appeal to your office.

We write to urge your government not to ratify the ArcelorMittal Mineral Development Agreement (MDA) for a third time, based on clear legal, policy, environmental, and governance considerations.

1. Constitutional Duty to Protect the Environment and Public Interest
Article 7 of the 1986 Constitution of Liberia obligates the State to manage national resources in a manner that advances the general welfare of the Liberian people. Additionally, Article 6 recognizes the Republic’s duty to ensure social justice and sustainable development. Re-ratifying an agreement that has repeatedly raised concerns about environmental harm, weak enforcement, and limited public benefit risks violating these constitutional principles.

2. Inconsistency with the Environmental Protection and Management Law (EPML):

The Environmental Protection and Management Law of Liberia (2002) requires precautionary measures, strict environmental impact assessments, mitigation, and rehabilitation for projects with significant environmental risks. Evidence from prior operations indicates persistent challenges in enforcement, monitoring, and remediation. Ratifying the MDA again without a demonstrably stronger environmental safeguards and penalties contradicts the intent and spirit of the EPML and weakens environmental governance.

3. Conflict with Community Rights under the Land Rights Act (2018):

The Land Rights Act of 2018 recognizes customary land ownership and requires meaningful community participation and consent in land-use decisions. Ongoing disputes over land access, compensation, and resettlement in mining-affected areas suggest that community rights have not been fully respected. A third ratification without resolving these issues risks further undermining legally protected customary land rights and social stability.

4. Weak Alignment with the Minerals and Mining Development Policy:

Liberia’s Minerals and Mining Development Policy emphasizes value addition, local content, environmental sustainability, and equitable benefit-sharing. The existing MDA continues to prioritize raw ore export, with limited downstream processing, technology transfer, or skilled employment for Liberians. Ratifying the agreement again entrenches a model that is inconsistent with national policy objectives for industrialization and economic diversification.

5. Fiscal and Governance Constraints Contrary to Reform Goals:

Stability clauses, tax concessions, and limited renegotiation flexibility within the MDA constrain Liberia’s fiscal sovereignty and policy space. These provisions conflict with ongoing public sector reform efforts and the principles of transparency and accountability promoted under Liberia’s governance and anti-corruption frameworks, including commitments aligned with the Liberia Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (LEITI).

6. Missed Opportunity for Strategic Reform:

Your Excellency, Liberia is at a critical moment to reform its extractive sector. Proceeding with a third ratification of the same agreement signals continuity with a model that has not delivered broad-based development, environmental sustainability, or social justice.

 This moment instead calls for a comprehensive review and renegotiation framework anchored in constitutional mandates, environmental law, land rights protections, and national development policies.

Our Respectful Appeal:

In light of these legal and policy considerations, the Environmental Eyes Consultancy and Advocacy Firm Inc. respectfully calls on your administration to:

1. Withhold the third ratification of the ArcelorMittal MDA in its current form;
2. Commission an independent legal, environmental, and economic review and audit consistent with Liberian law;
3. Ensure inclusive consultations with affected communities, civil society, and technical experts;
4. Pursue mining agreements that fully comply with Liberia’s Constitution, environmental laws, land rights regime, and development policies.

Your Excellency, the decisions taken today will shape Liberia’s environmental integrity, social cohesion, and economic future for generations. We trust in your leadership to uphold the law and safeguard the long-term interests of the Liberian people. The time is not late to recall the submission of the above mention Arcelor Mittal third extension mineral development agreement.

=================
Every week, my neighbor knocked over my trash bins and threw garbage all over my lawn. I tried talking to him. He denied it all. I confronted him again. He just smirked. As a single mom barely holding everything together, I had no time for his nonsense. So I quit talking and started planning. The guy never expected what was coming.

I'm 33 years old, raising two young kids by myself in a house that's breaking down quicker than I can fix it.

Maverick walked out three weeks after our youngest was born. No reason. No child support. No apology.

We live in the house my grandmother left me. The paint is peeling, the driveway is narrow, and the furnace makes a terrible racket every time it starts.

But it's ours. And I'm doing everything I can to hold onto it.

Winter makes everything ten times tougher.

In our town, when snow builds up, people move their trash bins closer to the road so the trucks can get them. That's just how it is.

Except for my neighbor, Beckett.

Beckett is in his early 50s, drives a huge black SUV that's too big for our street, and always looks at you like you're bothering him just by being there. He's lived next door since before I was born, and he's never been friendly.

The trouble began about a month into winter.

One Tuesday morning, I woke up to both my trash bins tipped over and garbage scattered across the entire front lawn. Diapers frozen in the snow. Food containers everywhere. Coffee grounds mixed with slush.

My three-year-old pressed her face against the window and asked, "Mommy, why is our yard so messy?"

I told her it was an accident and spent twenty minutes in the freezing cold gathering trash with numb fingers before getting the kids ready for daycare.

The second time, I was annoyed. The third time, I was furious.

That's when I noticed the tire tracks.

They ran straight across the corner of my lawn, right where the bins had been. Same direction. Same angle. Every time.

And they matched Beckett's SUV tires exactly.

I decided to talk to him like an adult.

One Saturday afternoon, I saw him at his mailbox. The kids were napping, so I had maybe five minutes before one woke up crying.

"Hey, Beckett," I said, keeping my voice calm and friendly. "Can I ask you something?"

He turned, already looking bored. "What?"

"My trash bins keep getting knocked over. There are tire tracks cutting across my lawn. Do you know anything about that?"

He didn't even hesitate.

"Wasn't me. Probably the snow plow."

I stared at him. "The plow doesn't come down our street until after pickup."

He shrugged. "Then I don't know. Maybe your bins are too close to the road."

"They're exactly where they should be."

"Well, I didn't hit them." He turned back toward his house, ending the conversation. "Maybe stop leaving trash everywhere."

I stood there with clenched fists, watching Beckett walk away like he hadn't just lied right to my face.

That's when I realized talking wasn't going to work.

The next week, it happened again.

I was outside scraping ice off my windshield. I heard Beckett's SUV start up, heard him rev it louder than needed, then watched him swing wide on purpose as he pulled out.

He clipped both bins. Garbage exploded across the lawn.

He didn't stop. Didn't slow down. Just drove off like nothing happened.

My five-year-old ran to the window, hands pressed against the glass.
"Mommy! The trash fell again!"

I stood in the cold holding a torn bag with frozen garbage spilling out, and something inside me snapped.

Not loud or dramatic. Just a quiet, angry decision that I was done being nice.
Because being a single mom means you have no time for this kind of thing. You have no energy for people who think they can push you around because you're alone. You can't let stuff like this slide.

I had two kids depending on me. A car that needed new brakes. A job that barely covered bills.

And now a neighbor who thought he could treat me like trash just because he felt like it.

So when the next trash day came, I made one small, quiet change....⬇⬇⬇

My greatest prayer is that every member of my family comes to know the Lord before it’s too late. Nothing matters more.

“Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.” (Acts 16:31, KJV)

Some prayers feel ordinary—help with today’s needs, guidance for a decision, strength to endure. But there is a deeper kind of prayer, the one that rises from love and eternity: “Lord, please save my family.” If that is your greatest prayer, you are not being dramatic. You are seeing what matters most.

In Acts 16, a frightened jailer asks Paul and Silas what he must do to be saved. The answer is simple and weighty: “Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ.” Salvation is not earned by effort or inherited by bloodline. It is received through faith in Jesus—His life, His cross, His resurrection, His living presence. And yet the promise stretches wider than one trembling man: “and thy house.” God’s heart includes households. He cares about the people who share your last name and the people who share your memories.

Still, loving people this much can hurt. You may feel urgency—time is passing, hearts seem closed, conversations get tense. You may carry regret for moments you stayed silent or spoke harshly. In that ache, remember God’s character: He is “not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.” (2 Peter 3:9, KJV) The urgency you feel is real, but it is held inside the patience of God, who pursues hearts with steady mercy.

Here is a freeing truth: you cannot manufacture faith in someone else. Only the Spirit can open eyes and soften a heart. But you are not powerless. God invites you to participate—not as the savior, but as an intercessor, a witness, and a living example of His grace. Lord, give me tears without despair and courage without harshness, today.

Pray with perseverance, not panic. Panic makes us push, argue, and grasp for control. Perseverance returns to God again and again, trusting that He is working even when nothing looks different. Some breakthroughs come suddenly; many come quietly—through a question asked at the right time, a crisis that exposes need, a memory of truth planted long ago.

Love in a way that makes the gospel believable. Love does not replace truth; it prepares the ground for it. Be quick to apologize when you’re wrong. Be consistent when no one is watching. Be patient when you’re misunderstood. These are not techniques—they are the fruit of Jesus in you. Kindness has a way of disarming resistance and making people curious about the God who is changing you.

Speak when the Lord opens a door. You don’t have to force a sermon into every family gathering. But you can gently name what Jesus means to you: “I prayed about that,” “The Lord helped me,” “I’m learning to trust God here.” Ask questions. Listen well. Let your tone match your message—truth carried in humility.

And entrust the outcome to God. Your family members are not beyond His reach. He loves them more than you do. He knows how to arrange moments, relationships, and circumstances that draw a person toward Him. Keep asking boldly, but rest in this: God is not indifferent, and He is not late.

If nothing matters more, then keep bringing their names to the Lord. Keep loving them with steady grace. Keep watching for small openings. And keep trusting that Jesus saves—not only individuals, but whole stories, whole families, whole generations—by grace alone.

Reflection
• Who am I most burdened for right now? Pray for them by name with compassion rather than anxiety.
• Is there any relationship I need to mend, so my witness is not hindered by unresolved hurt?
• What is one simple sentence I can say this week that naturally points to Jesus?

Lord, You see my family and You know every hidden fear, wound, and question. Reveal Jesus to them—clearly and personally. Give them a hunger for truth and the courage to respond. Open doors for conversations I could never plan. Make me gentle, wise, and patient; help me to love well and speak well. Heal what is broken between us. I trust Your timing, but I will not stop asking: save my family, Lord, and draw them into Your joy. Amen.

Most of us think of trauma as something that only affects our emotions or mental health. 

But did you know that trauma can also mess with your immune system and cause long-lasting inflammation in your body?

The vagus nerve is one of the most important nerves in your body.
Its biggest jobs is to help you relax and recover after stress. 

It also helps control inflammation, which is your body’s way of responding to injury, infection, or irritation.

But when the vagus nerve isn’t working well, like after trauma or long-term stress, it can stop doing its job. 

That means inflammation gets out of control and can lead to chronic health problems.

Over time, this kind of inflammation can lead to autoimmune diseases, where the immune system accidentally attacks healthy parts of your body.

Acetylcholine is a chemical made by the vagus nerve – its your body’s natural anti-inflammatory.

But if the vagus nerve isn’t sending enough acetylcholine, because it’s been weakened by trauma, stress, or illness, your immune system doesn’t get the message to stop.

The connection between trauma, inflammation, and autoimmune illness is real and it's something science is finally beginning to understand. 

If you’ve been dealing with strange symptoms that no one can explain, or if you’ve been diagnosed with an autoimmune disease, it’s worth looking into your nervous system health, especially the vagus nerve.

Freetown, January 13, 2026 — Sierra Leone has formalised a new security partnership with the Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition (IMCTC) following the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding aimed at reinforcing the country’s counter-terrorism framework and boosting regional security collaboration.

The agreement was signed on Tuesday during a high-level ceremony at the Freetown International Conference Centre at Bintumani, coinciding with the official launch of the IMCTC Strategic Initiative in Sierra Leone.

The move is expected to enhance national preparedness against emerging security risks, particularly those linked to instability in the Sahel region.

Under the MOU, the IMCTC will provide specialised training for personnel of Sierra Leone’s defence and security forces. Trained officers will, in turn, engage religious leaders—including Imams and Pastors—to promote counter-extremism awareness and help prevent the spread of radical ideologies. The partnership also includes support for strengthening anti-money laundering systems to curb terrorist financing.

The MOU was signed by the Chief of Defence Staff of the Republic of Sierra Leone Armed Forces, Lieutenant General Amara Idara Bangura, and the IMCTC Secretary-General, Major General Mohammed bin Saeed Al-Moghedi.

I was talking to my mother, and my aunty has been unwell for the last few years. She recently visited my mother’s home and stayed there for a while. She doesn’t have children, and she is the second wife of our chacha, so she is super attached to him — but there’s no one to look after her the way children do. Before she became unwell, her nieces and nephews used to visit regularly, but now they don’t. When she visited my mother’s home and my sister was there, they looked after her, and she felt really good. Sometimes a simple change of environment works like medicine — even staying somewhere else for a few days makes a huge difference.

So I was telling my mother: no matter what happens, in the end it’s your own children who look after you, not nieces and nephews. We always feel naturally drawn back to the place where our parents live — that emotional connection is very real.

I don’t know why women in my generation stopped having children. Just like I have only one child, my sisters also have one each. It wasn’t exactly our choice — life circumstances pushed us there. The men we married weren’t earning well, were dependent on us, had health issues, financial issues, and on top of that, some were busy with “extra” adventures outside the marriage. When a woman sees a man being irresponsible, of course she becomes scared of having more children — we don’t want to depend on someone who is actually depending on us!

We need to understand that children are a woman’s true asset. As women have children, they feel stronger, and even men can become stronger and more stable through their wives and children — at least, ideally! 

In reality, many men just drift through life, while women actually reach the age where they become dependent on daughters, daughters-in-law, and grandchildren. So having more children really does benefit a woman in her old age.

And if someone is thinking, “I’ll just live in this country and go to a nursing home and get good service” — no, it’s not the same. No one can look after you the way your own children can. I’ve seen this with my own eyes.

So my friendly advice: stop obsessing over men — I made that mistake and I fully regret it. Have children, build your own little team. If a man behaves well, wonderful. If not, show him the way out, go to family court, arrange joint custody, and carry on with your life. Keep your children close and under your positive influence. And as for men who forget their responsibilities, society should at least give them strong reminders by punishing them so they can start behaving again by Monday!

I’m excited to share this event because it directly supports something very important to me—the Hopkins County Community Clinic, a free clinic run by my Trover medical school classmates and me under the supervision of Dr. Crump.

Every week, students from our clinic go into the community to provide free cardiovascular risk screenings, including blood pressure, finger-stick glucose, and cholesterol checks. We meet people where they are—at places like the Salvation Army, Breaking Bread, the YMCA, St. Vincent de Paul, health fairs, and community events—to help identify undiagnosed conditions and reduce barriers to care.

For individuals without reliable access to healthcare or insurance, we help connect them with primary care, take them on as free-clinic patients, help obtain and manage medications, provide lifestyle and smoking-cessation resources, and even arrange same-day telehealth visits with our supervising physician when urgent issues are discovered. Our goal is simple: catch disease early, improve quality of life, and make sure no one falls through the cracks.

💙 This color run is how we fund all of this.💙 
Race registrations and donations allow us to continue offering these free services and provide hands-on learning opportunities for future physicians who are learning to care for real patients in our community.

The Coconut Creek Police Department has identified a woman known only as “Jane Doe” for the past 45 years.

On September 28, 1981, officers responded to the 6700 block of Lyons Road to investigate after a woman was found dead in a canal. A subsequent autopsy revealed she had died of gunshot wounds to the head. At the time, she had no identification on her, so the victim was labeled “Jane Doe.”

Last November, the Broward County Medical Examiner’s Office found the victim’s original fingerprint card in its archives. The fingerprints were run through the National Crime Information Center database and there was a hit. The fingerprints matched Barbara Overby, age 24, of Fort Lauderdale.

A detective found Overby’s family in North Carolina. They had not seen or heard from her in more than 45 years. The family recalled rumors of her residing in Florida but could never be completely sure. The family sent two pictures they had of her that are included in this post.

One of our detectives is hoping this might generate new leads in this murder investigation. Anyone who can help can call 954-973-6700.

The investigation is ongoing.

As we edge closer to the 2027 General Election, Kenya’s presidential contest is quietly but clearly taking shape. Barring political earthquakes, three names dominate the national conversation:

William Ruto.
Kalonzo Musyoka.
Fred Matiang’i.

Three men. Three different motivations. Three very different political burdens.

And therein lies the real story.

𝐑𝐮𝐭𝐨 𝐈𝐬 𝐃𝐞𝐟𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐏𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫

President William Samoei Ruto  enters 2027 as an incumbent. That alone is both an advantage and a heavy burden. Every promise made, every policy implemented, every hardship faced by Kenyans will sit squarely on his shoulders.

Incumbency is not just about power, it’s about accountability.
Ruto will not be campaigning on hope; he will be defending a record.

𝐊𝐚𝐥𝐨𝐧𝐳𝐨 𝐅𝐞𝐞𝐥𝐬 “𝐈𝐭’𝐬 𝐇𝐢𝐬 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞”

Kalonzo Musyoka  has waited patiently in Kenyan politics for decades. He has been loyal, strategic, and consistent. For him, 2027 feels like a turn-taking moment, a belief that endurance alone should finally be rewarded.

But elections are not retirement benefits.
They are referendums on vision, energy, and relevance today.

𝐌𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐚𝐧𝐠’𝐢 𝐇𝐚𝐬 𝐍𝐨𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐨 𝐋𝐨𝐬𝐞 𝐀𝐧𝐝 𝐄𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐨 𝐖𝐢𝐧

This is where the race changes completely.

Dr. Fred Matiang’i is not running to protect power.
He is not running out of entitlement.
He is not running to settle scores or revenge anyone.

𝐇𝐞 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐝 𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐛𝐲 𝐊𝐞𝐧𝐲𝐚𝐧𝐬.

That distinction matters.

Matiang’i enters the race with no political baggage, no office to defend, no historical promises haunting him. He carries something far more powerful: a reputation for work, discipline, and delivery.

Vikings wata ƙungiya ce ta mutane da suka rayu a yankin Scandinavia wato ƙasashen Norway Sweden da Denmark a yau.

Sun shahara tsakanin ƙarni na 8 zuwa ƙarni na 11 (kimanin shekara ta 793 zuwa 1066). A wannan lokaci ake kiran zamaninsu da “Viking Age” Kalmar Viking tana nufin mutumin teku mai kai hare hare, domin sun fi shahara da tafiya cikin jiragen ruwa suna kai farmaki, kasuwanci, ko kuma neman sabon wuri da za su zauna.

Vikings sun fito ne daga ƙasashe masu sanyi, duwatsu da ƙanƙara. Rashin wadataccen wurin noma da ƙasa mai kyau ya sa da yawa daga cikinsu suka koma fashin teku, kasuwanci, da binciken sababbin ƙasashe.

Sun kasance jarumai, ƙwararru a iya tuki da kera manyan jiragen ruwa, kuma suna da ƙarfin hali sosai Sannan Vikings ba Kiristoci ba ne. Sun yi imani da alloli da yawa (paganism), daga cikinsu akwai:

Odin sarkin alloli, allahn hikima da yaƙi. Thor allahn tsawa da ƙarfi. Loki allahn yaudara. Frey & Freyja allolin arziki da soyayya

Sun yi imani da Valhalla wato aljannarsu kenan, inda idan jarumai  suka mutu a yaƙi can zasu tafi su rayu tare da Odin.

Ɗaya daga cikin manyan sirrinsu shi ne jiragen ruwa (Longships): suna iya tafiya a teku da manyan koguna, suna sauƙin sauka a bakin ruwa. Wannan ya ba su damar kai hare hare manyan kasashe ba zato ba tsammani.

A shekara ta 793, Vikings sun kai farmaki kan Lindisfarne Monastery a Ingila. Wannan hari ya girgiza Turai, kuma daga nan ne duniya ta fara tsoron Vikings.
Sun kai hare hare a Ingila, Faransa, Spain, Portugal, Italiya, da Gabashin Turai.

Wasu lokuta suna kwashe dukiya, kama bayi, da kone garuruwa. Saboda haka Turawa suna kallon su a matsayin ‘yan ta’adda na teku a zamanin.

Amma ba duk Vikings ne ’yan fashi ba. Da yawa daga cikinsu ’yan kasuwa ne: suna sayar da fata, zinariya, azurfa

Suna sayen kayan yaji, zuma, siliki.. Suna zuwa har Rasha, Baghdad domin kasuwanci, da Byzantine Empire (Istanbul). Wasu Vikings sun yi aiki a matsayin sojojin haya a fadar sarkin Byzantine, ana kiran su Varangian Guard.

A Ingila, Vikings sun kafa yanki mai suna Danelaw, inda dokokinsu ke aiki. Sun zauna, sun yi aure da mutanen Ingila, sun zama mazauna ƙasa.

Shahararrun Sarakunan su sune, Ragnar Lothbrok (ko da yake tarihin sa yana gauraye da almara), da kuma Ivar the Boneless, da Harald Hardrada.

Vikings ne Turawan farko da suka gano: Iceland, Greenland, da Vinland (Arewacin Amurka da Kanada). Leif Erikson ya isa Arewacin Amurka kusan shekara ta 1000, shekaru fiye da 400 kafin Christopher Columbus ya isa, duk da duniya a yau Christopher  Columbus ta sani.

Vikings suna gina gidaje na itace da laka. Mata suna da ’yanci fiye da mata a sauran Turai. Suna da dokoki da taron shari’a da ake kira Thing. Ba su rayu da yaƙi kaɗai ba, suna noma, kiwo da kamun kifi.

Daga ƙarni na 10, Kiristanci ya fara shiga Scandinavia. Sarakuna sun karɓi Kiristanci, hare-haren fashi suka ragu. A shekara ta 1066, bayan mutuwar Harald Hardrada a yaƙin Stamford Bridge a Ingila, ana ɗaukar hakan a matsayin ƙarshen zamanin Vikings.

Har yau Vikings sun bar: harshe (kalmomi a cikin yaren Turanci), al’adu, tsarin gwamnati, da labarai da tatsuniyoyi. A yau ana nuna tarihin su a fina finai kamar Vikings da The Last Kingdom.
